Racism has no place in Europe!

To the President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola, the Directorate-General for Personnel and all members and staff of the European Parliament.

Petition

We call on the European Parliament to reschedule Maboula Soumahoro's conference and to take a firm stand against the racist hatred and threats that led to its postponement.

Why is this important?

Democracy just took a hit. Far-right extremists launched a hate campaign to silence an anti-racism researcher. They succeeded in cancelling her conference at the European Parliament, and in dictating what Europe can - and cannot - discuss. [1] 

This isn’t just a personal attack against researcher Maboula Soumahoro [2]; it’s a calculated effort to silence anyone fighting racism.

These extremists are sending a chilling message: hatred and intimidation can shape Europe’s decisions. If we do nothing, they'll only grow stronger and gain more control over the stories that shape Europe. This is a fight for the soul of Europe.

Researchers, activists and Members of the European Parliament are already mobilising against these attacks and demanding that Soumahoro’s conference be rescheduled. [3] But they need public pressure from people across Europe to make their demands impossible to ignore.

If enough citizens like you act, we can show that Europe is about inclusion, not hate, and force the conference back on the agenda. 

Join the movement to demand that the European Parliament reschedule Soumahoro’s conference. Together, we can ensure that racism has no place in European institutions.

2024-12-trial-environmental-education-pe.description_full:
Europe: let’s teach all children about protecting the planet!

To European governments

Petition

We urge our governments to make environmental education a compulsory subject in schools across Europe!

Why is this important?

Take a trip down memory lane. When you were in school, did you learn about tackling climate change?

Many years may have passed, but schools today are still not giving children the tools they need to respond to the environmental challenges we all face. [1]

In countries like Germany, France, Poland or Spain, environmental education is often optional, fragmented across different subjects, and inconsistent. [2] But there’s hope: Italy has made climate change a compulsory subject in its curriculum. [3] 

Now, we must ensure this policy creates lasting change in Italian schools—and inspires other European governments, like yours, to take bold action.

Environmental education can empower young generations to understand the climate emergency and push to transform the system that’s destroying our planet. 

Our leaders have taken first, timid steps in the right direction, but without realising citizens are watching they won’t deliver on their promises of quality education.

Let’s push our representatives to ensure that all students are equipped to protect our planet.

2024-12-trial-russia-shadow-fleet-petiti.title: EU, stop buying Russian oil and funding the war
2024-12-trial-russia-shadow-fleet-petiti.description_full:
EU, stop buying Russian oil and funding the war

To the European Commission, Governments of Member states of the European Union

Petition

We are calling on the EU and Member states to urgently adopt measures to curb Russia's shadow fleet. We’re urging to:

  • Address the massive environmental risk posed by old shadow fleet tankers operating in EU waters.
  • Close loopholes and step up the enforcement of sanctions on Russian fossil fuels.

Why is this important?

The EU must act now to stop funding Russia's war on Ukraine. This means closing loopholes and stepping up the enforcement of sanctions on Russian fossil fuels. It's time to get serious and cut off the cash to the Kremlin! 

Russia’s “shadow fleet” of ageing, risky oil tankers is funding its brutal war on Ukraine. These ships dodge sanctions, evade safety standards, and threaten catastrophic oil spills in European waters. [1]

Every day, this illegal fleet moves Russian oil, generating money to fund the missiles, tanks, and bullets that kill people. 

The billions Russia has invested into the shadow fleet to evade sanctions shows just how critical it is for them to be able to continue to sell oil. 

But the European Union has the power to dismantle Russia’s shadow fleet. Stronger sanctions on ships and their backers, along with tougher environmental and safety rules, can cut off Putin's war funds and safeguard coastal communities. Let's make it happen!

If thousands of us speak up we can make a difference. A wave of people power could expose and dismantle this dangerous fleet. Europe can’t continue to be outsmarted by Putin - we must stop this trade and cut off the funding it provides for Russia’s war.

References:

[1] https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/14/russias-shadow-fleet-oil-tankers-grows-western-sanctions

2024-12-trial-stop-deforestation-for-ele.title: EU, impede deforestation linked to hydropower production, now
2024-12-trial-stop-deforestation-for-ele.description_full:
EU, impede deforestation linked to hydropower production, now Please accept marketing cookies to watch this video

To The European Commission and its President Ursula von der Leyen and to the Romanian President Calin Georgescu

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The European Commission should add electrical energy to the list of products banned on the Union market and for export if associated with deforestation.

Why is this important?

Further increase in deforestation is completely intolerable, no matter which kind of business constitutes the pretext. For instance, deforestation to make room for hydropower reservoirs.

This practice does not only exterminate the native biodiversity, destroying the ecosystems which used to store carbon but also leads to large emissions and substantial loss of water by evaporation: It is estimated that the evaporative water loss in hydropower reservoirs is equivalent to 20% of the global annual consumption of water use. [1] Knowing the current trend of increasing intensity and duration of droughts in Europe, can we really afford to lose our forests and therefore our water? 

With this petition, we call for the inclusion of deforestation for energy production in the EU’s list of prohibited activities under the regulation on commodities and products associated with deforestation. [2] This regulation, primarily intended to target deforestation outside the EU, is incomplete and ineffective if EU governments are allowed to promote illegal deforestation.

A glaring example is the Răstolița dam project in Romania, which threatens to destroy a protected area within Călimani National Park for minimal energy production. This deforestation risks the extinction of Romania’s only viable huchen population, a unique and endangered freshwater species. [3] The European Commission, contradicting its own prior guidance document, closed the complaint no. CPLT(2023)01366, complaint including the Răstolița case. [4]

Encouraged by the complicity of the European Commission, Hidroelectrica Company resumed this summer the illegal works at the dam project during the environmental impact assessment, without waiting for the environmental permit to be issued - which is completely illegal, and none of the abusive ministers in charge moved a single finger against it.

But now the European Commission has the chance to make up for past mistakes.

According to their own legislation, the European Commission is required to review the Regulation on Deforestation by June 2025 and assess the need to extend its scope to additional commodities and products. We urge the Commission to include the production of electrical energy in this review.

Energy can be produced sustainably and profitably without resorting to new deforestation. Expanding the regulation’s scope is crucial to ensuring that deforestation for energy production is addressed and prevented.

Will you help us save not only this forest from destruction but all the rest as well?

Sign the petition, join the fight!

2024-2-clothes-restoration-EN.title: Clothes restoration
2024-2-clothes-restoration-EN.description_full:
Clothes restoration

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

In a world inundated with fast fashion and disposable trends, a quiet revolution is taking place - one stitch at a time. An initiative dedicated to the restoration and redesign of old garments is gaining momentum, breathing new life into forgotten fabrics and preserving the stories woven within them.

At its heart lies the art of repair, a skill once passed down through generations but now experiencing a renaissance. Rather than discarding torn or stained clothing, individuals are embracing the challenge of restoration. From delicately mending seams to skillfully patching holes, each repair is a testament to sustainability and resourcefulness.

But this movement is not merely about function; it's about elevating garments to works of art. Enter embroidery, the magical fusion of needle and thread. Where there once was a flaw, now blooms a garden of intricate patterns and vibrant colors. The addition of embroidery not only conceals imperfections but transforms them into unique embellishments, turning a garment's history into a thing of beauty.

Beyond the aesthetic appeal, there's a deeper significance to this practice. It's a rejection of the throwaway culture that dominates the fashion industry, a statement against mass production and uniformity. Each embroidered stitch is a declaration of individuality, a celebration of craftsmanship over consumerism.

Moreover, this initiative fosters a sense of community, uniting individuals with a shared passion for sustainability and creativity. Workshops and online forums abound with tips and techniques, offering support and inspiration to novices and experts alike. What begins as a simple repair can spark a lifelong journey of self-expression and skill development.

In a world where trends come and go with alarming speed, the movement to revive and reimagine old garments stands as a beacon of hope. It reminds us that fashion doesn't have to be fleeting, that true style transcends seasons and trends. So let us pick up our needles and threads, and join in the timeless art of clothing repair and embroidery. Together, we can stitch a more sustainable and beautiful world, one garment at a time.

Free Doctor Ahmed Muhanna and the AWDA medical staff!

To the Belgian government, in particular the foreign minister Hadja Lahbib; Development Cooperation Minister Caroline Gennez and Prime Minister Alexander de Croo

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Viva Salud demands the immediate release of Dr Ahmed Muhanna and the seven other hostages from the Al Awda hospital. We call on the Belgian government to take concrete steps to immediately release all those held captive, particularly the carers, who should never be targeted. We also call on the Belgian government to take effective sanctions against Israel, to put in place concrete measures to actively support the ICJ investigation, to ensure that the Court's decisions are implemented, and to do everything possible to achieve an immediate and permanent ceasefire.

Why is this important?

We’ve all seen the images from the war in Gaza; wounded patients being treated on hallway floors, bleeding children in tears, and so much heartache. With these conditions, functioning hospitals and doctors are the only chance to treat the wounded and save lives.

When bombing intensified over Northern Gaza, people fled to the South. But, Doctor Muhanna and his team stayed behind to keep the last hospital running and continue to treat people who had nowhere to go. [1]

While these brave doctors and nurses were caring for their patients, they were abducted by Israeli forces. Even wars have limits: health-care workers can’t be targeted and must be protected. [2] 

Doctor Muhanna’s health team was not working in isolation. For years they’ve been financially supported by the Belgian government. [3] Together, let’s remind Belgium that they cannot abandon health care workers in Gaza when they most need our help. People’s lives, especially children’s, depend on it. 

The Belgian government has already spoken out for peace and humanitarian aid in Palestine. [4] And our partners believe they can negotiate Doctor Muhanna’s release. We need them to demand his release. 

Together, let’s make sure the Belgium government knows that thousands of people across Europe want to free Doctor Muhanna and his team. If enough Europeans raise our voices, we could make sure that he is able to return to his important job of caring for the people of Gaza.

English

Justice on Trial: Will YOU Politicians Stand with Us?

Coalition members of the National Council of the Slovak Republic

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Fellow citizens, the very foundations of our society are at stake. We, the people of Slovakia, stand before you deeply troubled by the proposed changes to our penal code. These changes, if enacted, will severely undermine the safety and security of all Slovaks. They threaten to usher in an era where the safety of our children, families, and communities is jeopardized.

We urge you, the members of the Coalition, to stand with us. You hold the power to ensure our collective security. We entrusted you with the responsibility to make decisions that benefit the entire nation.

Reject these harmful amendments. Uphold the principles of justice and equality for all. Join us in building a stronger, fairer Slovakia, where the law protects the innocent and punishes the guilty.

Together, our voices can make a difference. Let us stand united for justice, for Slovakia!

Sincerely,

Your Concerned Neighbours, Friends, and Fellow Citizens

P.S. Your name will be forever associated with this decision. Choose wisely.

Why is this important?

Imagine...

  • A child walking home from school, feeling safe and secure.
  • A family enjoying a peaceful evening, free from fear.
  • Communities united, knowing justice will prevail.

This future is at stake. Proposed changes to the penal code threaten to weaken the very fabric of our society, putting everyone's safety and security at risk.

It's not just about statistics:

  • Stronger laws mean fewer crimes, creating a safer environment for all.
  • Justice served brings closure to victims and deters future crimes.
  • Equal protection under the law ensures everyone feels secure and valued.

But...

  • These changes could embolden criminals, making communities more vulnerable.
  • Justice may become elusive, leaving victims unheard and the public fearful.
  • Divisions might deepen, eroding trust and the sense of shared security.

We can choose a different path.

By joining our voices, we can tell our leaders:

  • Stand with us, protect our future.
  • Reject harmful changes, uphold justice for all.
  • Together, we can build a stronger, safer Slovakia.

This is not just about a law, it's about our children, our families, our communities, and our future.

Let's act now, together.

Remember, every voice counts. Add yours today.

2024-5-ask-the-un-fao-to-exclude-carnivo.title: Protect Our Oceans from Unsustainable Fish Farms
2024-5-ask-the-un-fao-to-exclude-carnivo.description_full:
Protect Our Oceans from Unsustainable Fish Farms Please accept marketing cookies to watch this video

To the United Nations Food & Agriculture Organization (FAO) - Aquaculture Division

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Ask the UN FAO to EXCLUDE Carnivorous Fish Farming from Sustainable Aquaculture Policy

Why is this important?

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is an agency of the United Nations whose goal is achieving food security for all. For some time, the FAO has been calling for an aggressive increase in farmed fish (“aquaculture”) and promoting a so called “blue agenda.” Its goal is to increase what it calls “sustainable aquaculture” by 75% by 2040. However, “sustainable aquaculture” is an ambiguous term, and the FAO’s own research acknowledges that the production of aquatic foods is not without serious problems, including overfishing, habitat degradation and unequal access to resources and markets.

Some aquaculture can be sustainable, such as the farming of kelp and other aquatic plants, as well as the cultivation of a wide range of bivalve creatures like mussels, clams and oysters in small-scale operations. However, it is not the case of farming  carnivorous  fish like  salmon, sea bass, and sea bream. These species require being fed fish meal and oil from massive quantities of wild fish (more than the farms produce!) and are the most commonly farmed fish in the EU. 

In 2021, Argentina became the first country to ban intensive salmon farming in its waters. The practice is also banned on the West Coast of the US and in British Columbia, Canada as of 2029. Knowing that these countries, renowned for their fishing worldwide, have banned such a practice, it is inevitable to think that the rest of us should - and could - be following their example.

On the occasion of World Oceans Day in June 2024, we collected more than 160 organizations from around the world asking the FAO and world leaders to heed the evidence and EXCLUDE carnivorous fish farming from their definition of what constitutes sustainable aquaculture. Unfortunately, after a week of debates at the July meeting of FAO’s Committee on Fisheries, that body adopted Guidelines for Sustainable Aquaculture that still include carnivorous fish.

And so we are continuing our letter-signing campaign and asking for your support in signing on.

Why? What’s the Deal with Carnivorous Fish Farming?

There is more and more evidence coming to light on the unsustainability and environmentally damaging aspects of open net pen carnivorous fish farming and studies have linked it to the following problems:

  • Despite FAO’s mantra that aquaculture is “feeding the world,” in fact high volumes of wild-caught fish are extracted from food-insecure countries to feed farmed fish. It takes between 1.2 to 6 kgs of forage fish, edible for human consumption, to produce 1 kg of farmed fish destined for wealthy consumer markets. 
  • Increases in harmful algal blooms and negative impact on critical Posidonia meadows, one of the planet’s largest carbon sinks
  • Mass fish die-offs
  • Uncontrolled use of the carcinogen formaldehyde
  • Large amounts of microplastics and debris left behind in the waters under fish farms
  • Prophylactic and overuse of antibiotics

The negative impacts from industrial carnivorous fish farming will only increase as ocean temperatures continue to rise. We need concrete, enforceable international standards for the remediation of damaged environments and the expansion of genuinely sustainable aquaculture options.

We ask that the FAO stop supporting and promoting marine based open net carnivorous fish and that it revises its guidelines on sustainable aquaculture to EXCLUDE carnivorous fish farming.

Learn more at fishfarmsout.org

2024-6-because-our-planet-is-blue-EN.title: Because Our Planet Is Blue
2024-6-because-our-planet-is-blue-EN.description_full:
English

  • Français
  • Deutsch
  • Español
  • Italiano
  • Nederlands
  • Polski

Because Our Planet Is Blue

  • To António Guterres, Secretary General of the United Nations
  • To Emmanuel Macron, President of the French Republic, Co-Host of the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025
  • To Rodrigo Chaves Robles, President of the Republic of Costa Rica, Co-Host of the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025
  • To all Heads of States and Governments represented at the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The Ocean is increasingly being threatened, degraded or destroyed by human activities. 

To turn the tide, we ask the world’s governments to adopt, at the UN Ocean Conference 2025, six steps – as specified in the OceanCare declaration “Because Our Planet Is Blue” – to be implemented immediately at global, regional and national levels:

1. Ban offshore oil and gas exploration and phase out existing fossil fuel extraction;
2. Implement mandatory measures to reduce vessel speed;
3. Ban destructive fisheries such as bottom trawling;
4. Adopt global rules to end plastic pollution, addressing the full life cycle of plastic;
5. Agree on a global moratorium on deep-sea mining;
6. Ensure effective protection of marine habitats and enforce marine conservation measures to restore ecosystems damaged by human activities.

Why is this important?

Our leaders have committed to tackling the climate crisis and protecting biodiversity by 2030. The UN Ocean Conference 2025 is our chance to make this happen. [1] Citizens across the world are calling for urgent action, including mandatory speed limits for ships.

Ship strikes are killing whales at an alarming rate. In the Mediterranean alone, collisions are the main source of human-caused death for endangered fin whales and sperm whales. Current shipping speeds significantly increase the risk of collisions, resulting almost always in lethal strikes. [2]

Beyond collisions, shipping has broader impacts. In some areas, ship noise has doubled every decade for 60 years, creating an underwater acoustic fog that prevents whales from communicating, finding food, and navigating. [3]

Even marine protected areas offer little safety. Current voluntary speed recommendations are widely ignored. In the Northwestern Mediterranean, the home of fin whales and sperm whales, 80% of merchant vessels continue to travel at dangerous speeds above 10 knots. [4] Without mandatory limits, these "protected" areas remain death traps for endangered whales.

Reducing ship speeds by just 10–20% could cut deadly collisions by up to 78% and underwater noise by up to 67%, offering benefits for both marine life and climate goals. [5]

We have the solutions to truly protect the Ocean. Now we need our leaders to turn them into action.

https://archive.iwc.int/pages/view.php?ref=17562&k=c9f67e8c17

[5] Leaper R (2019) The Role of Slower Vessel Speeds in Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Underwater Noise and Collision Risk to Whales. Front. Mar. Sci. 6:505. doi: 10.3389/fmars.2019.00505

President of the Italian Republic, Sergio Mattarella Prime Minister of Italy, Giorgia Meloni Minister of Interior, Matteo Piantedosi Minister of Justice, Carlo Nordio Governor of Calabria, Roberto Occhiuto Court of Crotone Prosecutor's Office of Crotone Members of the European Parliament European Commissioner for Home Affairs, Ylva Johansson European Commissioner for Justice, Didier Reynders

Petition

We want the Italian and European authorities to immediately release Maysoon Majidi, drop all charges against her, provide her with necessary medical and psychological support, grant her refugee status, and ensure fair treatment for all refugees and asylum seekers in the future.

Why is this important?

Our colleague, Maysoon Majidi, fled the fascist Islamist regime in Iran to the Kurdish Autonomous Region, fearing for her life. Unfortunately, she was not spared there either, facing continued persecution and threats. Desperate for safety, she decided to seek refuge in Europe, hoping to find asylum in a democratic country.

Her journey led her to Istanbul, where she had to stay illegally for several months before finding a smuggler who could take her and other refugees to Italy. Upon arrival in Crotone, Italy, she was arrested by the police along with other refugees. While everyone else was released, Maysoon remains unjustly imprisoned. For six long months, Maysoon has been locked up, innocent and desperate.

Maysoon has sought refuge to escape the Iranian Islamist regime, only to be arrested in Europe. She is accused of being involved in human trafficking, a charge based on the dubious statements of two witnesses who were on the boat with her. These two witnesses have denied these accusations, affirming that Maysoon is herself a refugee, not a trafficker. Her situation is dire – in protest against her wrongful imprisonment, she has gone on a hunger strike. She now weighs only 38 kg (84 lbs) at a height of 165 cm (5'5"). Her physical and mental health are deteriorating rapidly.

We urgently call for the immediate release of Maysoon Majidi and urge the Italian authorities, including:

  • President of the Italian Republic, Sergio Mattarella
  • Prime Minister of Italy, Giorgia Meloni
  • Minister of Interior, Matteo Piantedosi
  • Minister of Justice, Carlo Nordio
  • Governor of Calabria, Roberto Occhiuto

and the European authorities, including:

  • Members of the European Parliament
  • European Commissioner for Home Affairs, Ylva Johansson
  • European Commissioner for Justice, Didier Reynders

to end this grave injustice. Maysoon deserves freedom and protection, not imprisonment and despair.

2024-6-stop-deforestation-for-electricit.title: EU, impede deforestation linked to hydropower production, now
2024-6-stop-deforestation-for-electricit.description_full:
English

  • Română

EU, impede deforestation linked to hydropower production, now Please accept marketing cookies to watch this video

European Commission, president Ursula von der Leyen

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The European Commission should add electrical energy to the list of products which are forbidden on the Union market and the export if are associated with deforestation.

Why is this important?

Further increase in deforestation is completely intolerable, no matter which kind of business constitutes the pretext. For instance, deforestation to make room for hydropower reservoirs.

This practice does not only exterminate the native biodiversity, destroying the ecosystems which used to store carbon but also leads to large emissions and substantial loss of water by evaporation: It is estimated that the evaporative water loss in hydropower reservoirs is equivalent to 20% of the global annual consumption of water use. [1] Knowing the current trend of increasing intensity and duration of droughts in Europe, can we really afford to lose our forests and therefore our water? 

With this petition, we call for the inclusion of deforestation for energy production in the EU’s list of prohibited activities under the regulation on commodities and products associated with deforestation. [2] This regulation, primarily intended to target deforestation outside the EU, is incomplete and ineffective if EU governments are allowed to promote illegal deforestation.

A glaring example is the Răstolița dam project in Romania, which threatens to destroy a protected area within Călimani National Park for minimal energy production. This deforestation risks the extinction of Romania’s only viable huchen population, a unique and endangered freshwater species. [3] The European Commission, contradicting its own prior guidance document, closed the complaint no. CPLT(2023)01366, complaint including the Răstolița case. [4]

Encouraged by the complicity of the European Commission, Hidroelectrica Company resumed this summer the illegal works at the dam project during the environmental impact assessment, without waiting for the environmental permit to be issued - which is completely illegal, and none of the abusive ministers in charge moved a single finger against it.

But now the European Commission has the chance to make up for past mistakes.

According to their own legislation, the European Commission is required to review the Regulation on Deforestation by June 2025 and assess the need to extend its scope to additional commodities and products. We urge the Commission to include the production of electrical energy in this review.

Energy can be produced sustainably and profitably without resorting to new deforestation. Expanding the regulation’s scope is crucial to ensuring that deforestation for energy production is addressed and prevented.

Will you help us save not only this forest from destruction but all the rest as well?

Sign the petition, join the fight!

2024-6-trial-AWO-lidl-chickens-scandal-p.title: Lidl: Free chickens from torture!
2024-6-trial-AWO-lidl-chickens-scandal-p.description_full:
Lidl: Free chickens from torture!

Joel Rampoldt, Lidl CEO

Petition

We call on Lidl to eliminate unnecessary suffering of broiler chickens in its supply chain by signing and committing to the standards of the European Chicken Commitment. [1]

Why is this important?

We call on Lidl to eliminate unnecessary suffering of broiler chickens in its supply chain by signing and committing to the standards of the European Chicken Commitment [1]. 

Animal welfare is integral to the sustainability of the food system. The cruel and unsustainable conditions in which we find animals such as broiler chickens [2] reflect the disinterest that supermarkets such as Lidl have shown for years in adapting to minimum animal welfare requirements.

The biggest European grocer [3], the brand that could change the paradigm for animals, has decided to perpetuate animal suffering. Lidl could make a difference, but it prefers to continue turning over millions of euros stained with pain and anguish, not only going against all ethics but also endangering its consumers. 

What do we mean by that? 

High density of broiler chicken:

Science states that disproportionate density leads to an increased risk of virulent outbreaks with the potential for human contagion.

Breeding of fast-growing breeds:

Rapid growth leads to so-called ‘production’ diseases, such as ascites, sudden death syndrome or contact dermatitis.

Failure to meet minimum environmental enrichment standards:

Lack of environmental stimuli prevents the development of their natural behaviours, such as walking, running or burrowing.

Stunning by electrical bathing:

Birds are immersed in electrified water as a method of stunning prior to slaughter. The European Commission points out that a ban on this process is necessary due to the animal suffering involved.

The European Chicken Commitment is more than a list of minimum requirements for chicken welfare. It is the opportunity for the poultry farming sector to get their act together and step up to the demands of a constantly evolving market that is increasingly aware of the cruel conditions broiler chickens are subjected to.

Call on Lidl to eliminate unnecessary animal suffering in its supply chain.

Sign and share the petition today!

References:

[1] European Chicken Commitment - https://welfarecommitments.com/letters/europe/

[2] Lidl’s chicken scandal: a glimpse of the state of animal welfare in the EU - https://www.eurogroupforanimals.org/news/lidls-chicken-scandal-glimpse-state-animal-welfare-eu

[3] Lidl and Schwarz Group continuing as the biggest European grocer - https://adainsights.com/blog/lidl-and-schwarz-group-continuing-as-the-biggest-european-grocer#:~:text=The%20parent%20company%20of%20Lidl,revenues%20topping%20154%20billion%20euros

2024-6-we-demand-the-right-to-defence-in.title: We demand the right to defence in the co-financing of non-governmental culture.
2024-6-we-demand-the-right-to-defence-in.description_full:
English

  • Slovenščina

We demand the right to defence in the co-financing of non-governmental culture.

To the President of the Republic of Slovenia, Nataša Pirc Musar, to the President of the National Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia, Urška Klakočar Zupančič, to the President of the Committee for Culture of the National Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia, Sara Žibrat, to the Minister of Culture of the Republic of Slovenia, Asta Vrečko, to the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, to the President of the European Council, Charles Michel, to the Chair of the Committee on Culture and Education of the European Parliament, Sabine Verheyen

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We demand that the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Slovenia re-introduce the applicant's right to defence and the possibility of mediation when evaluating tenders in the field of co-financing of cultural projects before issuing a final decision.

Why is this important?

In 2016, the Ministry of Culture abolished this right unilaterally and without any public discussion.

Co-financing of non-governmental organizations in the field of culture takes place through tenders issued by the Ministry of Culture. Applications are evaluated by an expert committee. Although it is defined as an advisory body to the minister, it is the main decision-maker in co-financing (Articles 20 and 113 ZUJIK / Act on Culture), which is excluded. The evaluations of the expert commission we consider too often be non-objective, biased, or misleading. The applicant can only appeal to the Administrative Court, which deals with the case only on the procedural side, but not on the content, and returns the case for a new decision, where it is evaluated by the same expert commission.

The current method of decision-making grants unlimited power to the expert committee selected in the tender without apparent recourse or accountability.  It is public funds that are being awarded, not private. Apart from the Administrative Court, which only checks the procedural side, no one supervises its work. Expert commissions can make intentional or unintentional mistakes in their work and thus exclude from co-financing applicants who are entitled to co-financing, but who cannot defend themselves. Due to the commission's decisions, some prominent applicants had to stop the implementation of their projects or were severely limited in doing so and implemented them only with extraordinary effort and perseverance.

The right to defence with the possibility of mediation is the only instrument that permanently enables correct assessment of expert commissions and prevents their arbitrariness and arbitrariness. It enables top NGO projects to continue and exist regardless of the current political climate or other partisan interests. That is why it should also be in the interest of the Ministry of Culture.

By withdrawing the right to defence, we consider Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights is also violated.

The right to defence with the possibility of mediation and an urgent dialogue between the applicant and the expert commission are also included in the pre-election promises of the minister's Left party from 2022: "Repairing the damage of the last two years, especially due to the disregard of expert opinions, the need for radical changes, building new foundations for a comprehensive and coherent the development of all sectors in culture and the establishment of dialogue and regulation of the non-governmental sector". The right to defence with the possibility of mediation is a basic building block of dialogue.

Therefore, we demand that the Ministry of Culture immediately establish the right to defence with the possibility of mediation. We also request an audit of all applications from 2016 to the present, which were dismissed without the right to a defence.

2024-8-deneguemos-la-reapertura-de-la-mi.title: Don't contaminate our Camino!
2024-8-deneguemos-la-reapertura-de-la-mi.description_full:
English

  • Français
  • Deutsch
  • Español
  • Español (Galego)

Don't contaminate our Camino!

President of the Government of Galicia, Cabinet of the Government of Galicia, Spanish Government, Presidency of the European Parliament, UNESCO.

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We ask you to support this campaign against the reopening of the Touro mine. This is a project of Cobre San Rafael, a subsidiary of Atalaya Mining and Explotaciones Gallegas, that has recently been designated as Strategic Industrial Project and is located in the municipalities of Touro and O Pino (A Coruña- Galicia-Spain), very close to the French Way of the Camino de Santiago.

Why is this important?

The reopening of the mine represents a very serious impact and risk on the French Way of the Camino de Santiago and other cultural heritage elements, both tangible and intangible, in the affected municipalities, as stated in a report by ICOMOS - SPANISH NATIONAL COMMITTEE INTERNATIONAL COUNCIL ON MONUMENTS AND SITES - [1] causing significant concern, rejection and social alarm.

This mine would be just a few metres from the protected area of the French Way as it passes through Pedrouzo, which would result in the loss of the tangible and intangible values that make this last stage, before entering Santiago de Compostela, a unique stretch.

Heavy traffic generated by trucks, the continuous movement in the vicinity of or along the Camino, light pollution and the presence of dust and other volatile components in the air are among many other issues which can also seriously affect the environmental qualities of a cultural space which is Galicia’s main calling card for travellers from all over the world.

All this goes against the preservation of the authenticity and physical integrity of this World Heritage site that encompasses a broad cultural, environmental and landscape context. The exceptional universal values that motivated its listing by UNESCO in its World Heritage List must be protected.

Between 1974 and 1986 this same area experienced what it’s like having a mine. In barely twelve years half a dozen rivers became permanently polluted by acid mine drainage, as much agricultural land became totally devastated and transformed into large minepits lacking any type of environmental restoration. Agricultural activities could never be resumed on these lands and numerous springs, wells and water sources were destroyed, rendered unusable or polluted in perpetuity.

In addition to all of the above, this project could cause serious damage to the watershed of the Ulla river and its estuary in the Ría de Arousa by pollution with heavy metals. These are strong reasons to stop this project from going forward.

If you also want to preserve the genuine beauty of these lands, sign today and help us stop this atrocity!

Foto: Manuel G. Vicente

2024-8-trial-stop-deforestation-for-elec.title: EU, impede deforestation linked to hydropower production, now
2024-8-trial-stop-deforestation-for-elec.description_full:
EU, impede deforestation linked to hydropower production, now Please accept marketing cookies to watch this video

To The European Commission and its President Ursula von der Leyen

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The European Commission should add electrical energy to the list of products banned on the Union market and for export if associated with deforestation.

Why is this important?

Further increase in deforestation is completely intolerable, no matter which kind of business constitutes the pretext. For instance, deforestation to make room for hydropower reservoirs.

This practice does not only exterminate the native biodiversity, destroying the ecosystems which used to store carbon but also leads to large emissions and substantial loss of water by evaporation: It is estimated that the evaporative water loss in hydropower reservoirs is equivalent to 20% of the global annual consumption of water use. [1] Knowing the current trend of increasing intensity and duration of droughts in Europe, can we really afford to lose our forests and therefore our water? 

With this petition, we call for the inclusion of deforestation for energy production in the EU’s list of prohibited activities under the regulation on commodities and products associated with deforestation. [2] This regulation, primarily intended to target deforestation outside the EU, is incomplete and ineffective if EU governments are allowed to promote illegal deforestation.

A glaring example is the Răstolița dam project in Romania, which threatens to destroy a protected area within Călimani National Park for minimal energy production. This deforestation risks the extinction of Romania’s only viable huchen population, a unique and endangered freshwater species. [3] The European Commission, contradicting its own prior guidance document, closed the complaint no. CPLT(2023)01366, complaint including the Răstolița case. [4]

Encouraged by the complicity of the European Commission, Hidroelectrica Company resumed this summer the illegal works at the dam project during the environmental impact assessment, without waiting for the environmental permit to be issued - which is completely illegal, and none of the abusive ministers in charge moved a single finger against it.

But now the European Commission has the chance to make up for past mistakes.

According to their own legislation, the European Commission is required to review the Regulation on Deforestation by June 2025 and assess the need to extend its scope to additional commodities and products. We urge the Commission to include the production of electrical energy in this review.

Energy can be produced sustainably and profitably without resorting to new deforestation. Expanding the regulation’s scope is crucial to ensuring that deforestation for energy production is addressed and prevented.

Will you help us save not only this forest from destruction but all the rest as well?

Sign the petition, join the fight!

References:

  1. https://www.waterworld.com/water-utility-management/asset-management/press-release/14279180/study-finds-evaporative-water-loss-increasing-for-lakes-reservoirs
  2. https://novapublishers.com/shop/water-resources-management-methods-applications-and-challenges/
  3. https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/872361468253275900/pdf/Loan-1242-Romania-Riul-Mare-Retezat-Hydropower-Project-Loan-Agreement.pdf
  4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:52019XC1114(02)

2024-9-reclaim-social-media-from-the-adv.title: Reclaim social media from the advertising industry!
2024-9-reclaim-social-media-from-the-adv.description_full:
Reclaim social media from the advertising industry!

Wemove and other progressive campaign platforms

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

This petition calls on Wemove and similar progressive organizations to lead the way by adding share buttons for all petitions for Bluesky, Mastodon, and any other platforms which emerge which are not based on advertising and black box algorithms.

Why is this important?

The internet initially brought hope of connecting people and sharing information. Social media and algorithms initially brought the ability to have content customized to your interests and connections, and discover new content and connections which interest you. This has been completely hijacked by the advertising industry.... The most commonly used social media platforms such as X/Facebook/Instagram/YouTube/Tiktok generate profit through the advertising industry and structure their algorithms around it. They lock users into their platforms because if you leave, you lose all your connections and "like"/"follow" settings.  The algorithms are black boxes which target ads at you to maximize profit of the platform. The organizations with the most ability to buy ads are corporations who want you to consume more and more (often in a way which destroys our planet), and industry special interests who fund political and policy campaigns in their own for-profit interests. People like Elon Musk can control world conversation by buying Twitter/X. There are alternative platforms such as Bluesky and Mastodon which are not modelled on the advertising industry and which support open algorithms and moderation rules, and which are not based on a lock-in model. However very few people are switching because they have already been locked-in to the advertising based lock-in platforms. Even progressive organizations like WeMove are supporting this model by putting "share" buttons only of these advertising social media platforms (X/Facebook) and not putting share buttons for Bluesky and Mastodon. This petition calls on Avaaz and similar organizations to lead the way by adding share buttons for all petitions for Bluesky, Mastodon, and any other platforms which emerge which are not based on advertising and black box algorithms.

EU, stop buying Russian oil and funding the war

Kaja Kallas, High Representative of Europe for Foreign Affairs and Security; The European Commission; Polish Presidency of the Council of the European Union; The EU Member States

Petition

We are calling on the EU and Member states to:

  • Urgently adopt measures to curb Russia's shadow fleet and sanction every single ship in this fleet.               
  • Address the massive environmental risk posed by old shadow fleet tankers operating in EU waters.
  • Close loopholes and step up the enforcement of sanctions on Russian fossil fuels.

Why is this important?

Russia’s shadow fleet is smuggling oil to fund Putin’s war on Ukraine and risks causing  catastrophic oil spills in European waters. One of these aging, unsafe secret ships is even suspected of cutting a vital power cable in the Baltic Sea. [1] 

This secret fleet is critical for Russia’s war machine. Yet, only one-third of these ships face sanctions. [2] To stop Putin’s aggression, the EU must act now and sanction every single ship.

Poland is now leading the EU Presidency. The country has pledged to counter Russian influence and eliminate dependence on Russian energy — so we have a unique opportunity to push for stronger sanctions. It’s time for the EU to step up, dismantle this shadow fleet to cut war funding and protect our coasts from ecological disasters. 

Right now, the EU is preparing its 17th sanctions package. Let’s make sure this package sanctions every single one of Russia’s shadow fleet.

Add your voice and demand Europe stop Russia from smuggling oil to fund Putin’s war on Ukraine!

References:

[1] https://www.politico.eu/article/finland-probes-russian-shadow-fleet-baltic-break-political-involvement/

Protect our democracy against Elon Musk’s X

To the European Commission, to Henna Virkkunen, the Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy.

Petition

We urge you to:

  • Enforce the Digital Services Act (DSA) to protect our democracies by ensuring social media platforms uphold their responsibilities in combating disinformation and safeguarding fair democratic discourse.
  • Launch an investigation into X’s violations of the DSA and other European rules and impose sanctions to prevent the spread of extremist disinformation that endangers the integrity of European elections and democratic norms.

Why is this important?

He helped Trump come to power again. Now the billionaire Elon Musk wants more “Trumps” in Europe.

Elon Musk hosting a live stream on X with Alice Weidel, the head of Germany’s far-right AfD party—a group infamous for its divisive and extremist rhetoric—is not just a conversation. [1] It’s a calculated move to amplify anti-EU propaganda, disrupt democratic norms, and undermine the fairness of the upcoming elections in the EU.

This move violates the very principles of the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) which holds social media platforms accountable for combating disinformation and protecting fair democratic debate. By amplifying extremist voices, X (formerly known as Twitter) is flouting these rules in plain sight. We must demand that the EU Commission enforces the DSA and imposes sanctions on X for endangering our democratic values.

Momentum is building. Leaders across Europe, including French President Emmanuel Macron, have voiced strong opposition to Musk’s actions. [2] Strengthen the call of these leaders and make sure the EU knows its citizens don't want our elections to be determined by social media billionaires.

Will you add your voice to save our democracy?

Protect Greenland from Trump’s grip!

To President Ursula von der Leyen, High Representative for Foreign Affairs Kaja Kallas, and all Members of the European Commission and European Parliament.

Petition

We urge you to take a firm stance in defending Greenland’s sovereignty and its people’s right to shape their own future.

The EU must support Greenland and its citizens in resisting any attempts at annexation or coercion by:

  • Strengthening fair partnerships with the EU,
  • Promoting sustainable development,
  • Recognizing and respecting Greenland as a key partner in the Arctic region.

Why is this important?

Update from 15 January 2026 

Trump is charging ahead with his plan to buy Greenland - and threatening military action if their leaders refuse. [1]

Greenlanders have made one thing clear: their democracy is not for sale. [2] Yet White House staff are telling media outlets they’re “discussing an offer”. They’ve even hinted that refusing their deal could mean they take military action - just like they have in Venezuela and Iran. [3]

This is not just an insult to Europe’s democracy; it’s a direct threat to Greenland’s people. Local communities risk losing their voice and control over their future, alongside their lands, full of rare minerals and vital for the green transition. Under Trump’s agenda, the Arctic ecosystem faces destruction. [4]

After the latest developments, our decision-makers are no longer ignoring Trump’s plan. Eight European leaders signed a statement in solidarity with Greenlanders. [5] But words alone won’t protect Greenland. 

Now is the time for bold, decisive action to defend Greenland’s sovereignty and the Arctic’s future.

We demand the EU stand firm: defend Greenland’s sovereignty, protect the Arctic’s fragile environment, and safeguard democracy across Europe.

2025-01-trial-Cecilia-Sala-EN-trial-EN.title: Free Cecilia Sala
2025-01-trial-Cecilia-Sala-EN-trial-EN.description_full:
Free Cecilia Sala

To the European Commission, the President von der Leyen and all European leaders. 

Petition

We urge the European Commission, under the leadership of Ursula von der Leyen, to go beyond monitoring the situation and actively work towards the release of journalist Cecilia Sala.

Why is this important?

In a desolate cell of only a few square metres, with no windows and a light that never turns off, Cecilia Sala experienced a nightmarish New Year's Eve. The 29-year-old Italian journalist has been locked in isolation in Evin prison in Iran for almost two weeks. [1]

No possibility of communicating with the outside world, no certainty about her own fate, detained without a trial: Cecilia is being punished for doing her job - telling the truth.

She was in Iran collecting chronicles for her Stories podcast about courageous characters challenging the system. Now, she has become one of them. [2]

American sources suggest Cecilia may be a pawn in a dangerous diplomatic game. [3]

Just days before, an Iranian citizen was arrested in Milan at the request of the United States. 

That’s why we must stand up to support her.

The second term of the European Commission led by Ursula von der Leyen has only just begun, but its credibility is already being tested. So far, the Commission has only been “monitoring the situation”. [4] But monitoring is not enough. 

With enough voices, we can force her to act. We can show that European citizens will not tolerate journalists being treated as bargaining chips. 

Freedom of the press is not negotiable - it must be a cornerstone of democracy, not a tool in political games.

References:

[1] https://www.nytimes.com/2024/12/27/world/middleeast/cecilia-sala-italian-journalist-arrested-iran.html 
[2] https://choramedia.com/podcast/stories/
[3] https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce3278qyql1o

EU: Don’t Silence the Voices Fighting for Our Environment

To the European Commission and Parliament

Petition

We call on the European Commission and Parliament to:

  1. Stop any plans to cut EU LIFE funding for environmental non-governmental organisations that amplify citizens’ voices in policymaking.
  2. Recognise the key role of environmental NGOs in protecting democracy, ensuring balanced representation, and addressing climate change and ecosystem collapse.
  3. Strengthen the EU LIFE programme, which provides vital support for addressing Europe’s environmental and climate challenges while involving citizens in decisions.

Why is this important?

1.3 BILLION euros. That’s how much big businesses spend on lobbying in Brussels every year. [1] Before people like you even hear about new policies, corporate lobbyists are already shaping EU decisions to protect their profits.

Thankfully, there are groups that fight back and give citizens a voice in EU policymaking. These non-governmental organisations operate on tiny budgets compared to big business lobbies [2] —and now, many of them risk losing vital EU funds.

The European Commission wants to stop environmental organisations from using EU funding for advocacy. [3] This would ban them from sending letters, organising meetings, or providing materials to influence EU institutions - leaving corporate lobbyists unchecked. 

If this funding is cut, it would silence those who put people and the planet first, undermining Europe’s ability to tackle urgent environmental challenges.

This isn’t the first time the EU has tried to defund organisations that represent citizens. In 2021, the Commission wanted to slash funding for health NGOs, but strong resistance from the affected groups, supported by MEPs, forced them to back down. [4]

Vocal opposition worked in 2021, and together we can do it again to protect groups standing up for nature. Environmental organisations are already pushing back, but EU leaders will be more likely to listen if thousands of Europeans speak up. [5] Tell your representatives: we won’t let them silence the voices fighting for our planet!

We are calling on the EU and Member states to:

  • Urgently adopt measures to curb Russia's shadow fleet and sanction every single ship in this fleet.               
  • Address the massive environmental risk posed by old shadow fleet tankers operating in EU waters.

Together, we can create a groundswell of public pressure to expose and dismantle Russia’s shadow fleet. If we speak up, we can convince EU leaders to prioritize this in their next sanctions package marking the third anniversary of Russia’s full-scale invasion.

Add your voice and push Europe to stop this illegal trade and halt the war funding it provides!

2025-01-trial-SoMe-Age-Limit-petition-EN.title: Protect our kids’ digital future!
2025-01-trial-SoMe-Age-Limit-petition-EN.description_full:
Protect our kids’ digital future!

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on the European Union to:

  • Introduce enforceable and harmonized age limits for social media access, ensuring uniform regulations across all member countries.
  • Hold digital platforms accountable for creating safe online spaces for minors, protecting them from toxic content and abuse.

Why is this important?

Depression. Loneliness. Anxiety.
This is the daily reality for countless children across Europe. [1]

Instead of building real connections, they’re glued to screens, chasing Likes, Followers, and Views - measures of worth dictated by algorithms. Bombarded with toxic content, online bullying, and impossible beauty standards, their mental health is suffering.

This isn’t accidental. Big Tech has deliberately crafted an unregulated digital world that exploits minors to maximise profits. Every click and interaction generates data - data that fuels their profits, even as it puts our children at risk. 

Now, things could get even worse.

Meta has decided to eliminate fact-checking in the United States, opening the floodgates to misinformation and harmful content. [2]  How long before this dangerous trend reaches Europe?  Meanwhile, the absence of a common EU age limit for social media leaves children unprotected, as platforms take advantage of different rules across countries.[3]

But we can change this.

Governments, schools, and civil society are demanding change. [4] Now, it’s time for the European Union to act too. We’re urging the EU to introduce enforceable age limits for social media access and hold platforms accountable for creating safe online spaces for children. 

Our children’s future should not be dictated by algorithms or Big Tech’s greed. Together, we can ensure a safer and healthier digital world for them. 

References:

[1] "At the start of the 2010s, rates of teenage mental illness took a sharp upward turn, and they have been rising ever since. [....] in the decade to 2020 the number of emergency room visits for self-harm rose by 188% among teenage girls in the US and 48% among boys. The suicide rate for younger adolescents also increased, by 167% among girls and 91% among boys. A similar trend has been observed in the UK and many other western countries." https://www.theguardian.com/books/2024/mar/21/the-anxious-generation-by-jonathan-haidt-a-pocket-full-of-poison

[2] https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/1/10/meta-facebook-to-drop-fact-checkers-what-does-this-mean-for-social-media 

[3] Currently, parental consent is required in the EU for the processing of personal data of children under the age of 16. However, the 27 EU member states have the option to lower this threshold to 13. Some countries are beginning to do so: France has lowered the age to 15, although, last April, a group of experts commissioned by President Emmanuel Macron proposed stricter rules, including a ban on cell phones for children under 11 and on phones with Internet access for those under 13. https://www.reuters.com/technology/what-countries-do-regulate-childrens-social-media-access-2024-11-28/ 

[4] https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/france-must-curb-child-teen-use-smartphones-social-media-says-panel-2024-04-30/

2025-02-because-our-planet-is-blue-3-tri.title: Because Our Planet Is Blue
2025-02-because-our-planet-is-blue-3-tri.description_full:
Because Our Planet Is Blue

    To António Guterres, Secretary General of the United Nations
    To Emmanuel Macron, President of the French Republic, Co-Host of the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025
    To Rodrigo Chaves Robles, President of the Republic of Costa Rica, Co-Host of the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025
    To all Heads of States and Governments represented at the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The Ocean is increasingly being threatened, degraded or destroyed by human activities. 

To turn the tide, we ask the world’s governments to adopt, at the UN Ocean Conference 2025, six steps – as specified in the OceanCare declaration “Because Our Planet Is Blue” – to be implemented immediately at global, regional and national levels:

1. Ban offshore oil and gas exploration and phase out existing fossil fuel extraction;
2. Implement mandatory measures to reduce vessel speed;
3. Ban destructive fisheries such as bottom trawling;
4. Adopt global rules to end plastic pollution, addressing the full life cycle of plastic;
5. Agree on a global moratorium on deep-sea mining;
6. Ensure effective protection of marine habitats and enforce marine conservation measures to restore ecosystems damaged by human activities.

Why is this important?

Our leaders have committed to tackling the climate crisis and protecting biodiversity by 2030. The UN Ocean Conference 2025 is our chance to make this happen. [1] Citizens across the world are calling for urgent action, including mandatory speed limits for ships.

Ship strikes are killing whales at an alarming rate. In the Mediterranean alone, collisions are the main source of human-caused death for endangered fin whales and sperm whales. Current shipping speeds significantly increase the risk of collisions, resulting almost always in lethal strikes. [2]

Beyond collisions, shipping has broader impacts. In some areas, ship noise has doubled every decade for 60 years, creating an underwater acoustic fog that prevents whales from communicating, finding food, and navigating. [3]

Even marine protected areas offer little safety. Current voluntary speed recommendations are widely ignored. In the Northwestern Mediterranean, the home of fin whales and sperm whales, 80% of merchant vessels continue to travel at dangerous speeds above 10 knots. [4] Without mandatory limits, these "protected" areas remain death traps for endangered whales.

Reducing ship speeds by just 10–20% could cut deadly collisions by up to 78% and underwater noise by up to 67%, offering benefits for both marine life and climate goals. [5]

We have the solutions to truly protect the Ocean. Now we need our leaders to turn them into action.

References:

[1] https://sdgs.un.org/es/conferences/ocean2025

[2] https://iwc.int/management-and-conservation/ship-strikes

https://archive.iwc.int/pages/view.php?ref=17562&k=c9f67e8c17

[3] https://wwfwhales.org/ship-strikes-underwater-noise

[4] https://www.oceancare.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Infographs_Vessel_Traffic_Analyses_2023_NW_Mediterranean_EN_v2.pdf

[5] Leaper R (2019) The Role of Slower Vessel Speeds in Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Underwater Noise and Collision Risk to Whales. Front. Mar. Sci. 6:505. doi: 10.3389/fmars.2019.00505

Keep Banned Pesticides Out of our Food

Ministers and Members of the European Parliament 

Petition

We call on EU Member States and the European Parliament to:

  • Reject the EU-Mercosur trade deal, which would allow food grown with pesticides banned in Europe to flood our markets, endangering public health and the environment.
  • Uphold EU food safety standards by preventing toxic pesticide loopholes that benefit big agribusiness at the expense of farmers, consumers, and biodiversity.
  • Ensure fair trade policies that protect European farmers and promote sustainable agriculture instead of prioritizing corporate profits.

We must not let trade agreements undermine the health and environmental protections that Europeans fought hard to achieve. Stop this toxic trade deal—protect our health, farmers, and planet!

Why is this important?

Toxic pesticides banned in Europe are about to end up on our plates. 

The EU-Mercosur trade deal would allow massive amounts of meat, soy and grains, fruit and vegetables from South America—where pesticides banned in Europe are still widely used—to flood our markets. [1] This isn’t just a trade deal—it’s a backdoor for toxic chemicals to sneak onto our plates.

It’s a gift to Big Agribusiness, but a disaster for our health and Europe’s small, local farmers. While they are forced to follow strict environmental and health standards, corporate giants would be free to import cheap food containing banned pesticides. It’s unfair, unsafe, and completely unacceptable.[2]

But here’s the good news: we have the power to stop this. France, Poland, Austria, and Italy already oppose this deal. And if they hold the line, the whole toxic agreement collapses. [3] 

Big Agribusiness is fighting hard to change their stance, and this is where we come in. If we make enough noise, we can show these governments that people across Europe stand with them—and convince even more countries to reject the deal.

Defend the Green Deal from the polluters' lobby!

To the European Commission and national EU governments

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We demand:

  • Strengthen the Green Deal! No rollback of environmental and climate policies. Instead of undermining the Green Deal, we want to develop it further to systematically orient Europe towards climate neutrality, nature-friendly agriculture, a circular economy, and zero pollution as quickly as possible.
  • Socially just environmental and climate policy. Shape the implementation of the Green Deal in such a way that it equally pursues social justice and economic strength. This will bring secure jobs, good wages and a sustainable economy!
  • Simplification instead of trickery! Reducing unnecessary bureaucracy must not be misused to undermine the goals for nature conservation, climate protection and the circular economy!

Why is this important?

The European Green Deal is the most significant environmental and climate protection programme the European Union has ever launched. It is a real milestone for nature conservation, climate protection and the circular economy. In the last five years, 38 EU laws have been adopted to make Europe more climate-friendly and economically sustainable. Their implementation will take Europe a considerable step forward in climate protection and transitioning to a sustainable economy.

However, the ambitious roadmap to make Europe the first climate-neutral continent by 2050 is under threat from the Europe-wide shift to the right.

An alliance of right-wingers and conservatives in the EU Parliament and EU member states is putting pressure on Ursula von der Leyen. Now, the Commission President has presented first proposals that will significantly undermine the Green Deal. And this is just the beginning. More is to follow! The so-called ‘omnibus’ proposals are a veritable festival for the polluters’ lobby. Under the guise of reducing bureaucracy, the EU Commission wants to gut the Green Deal systematically. The end of new climate-damaging combustion engine cars is just as much at risk as protecting fundamental human rights through the European Supply Chain Act. The EU Commission does not even want to enforce existing legislation for the expansion of renewable energies.

This attack on the Green Deal not only jeopardises the basis of our survival but also the future of a prosperous European economy.

  • Reject the EU-Mercosur trade deal, which would flood Europe with cheap, industrially-produced food imports, undercutting small farmers and rural livelihoods.
  • Defend Europe’s small and sustainable farmers by ensuring fair competition and preventing unfair advantages for agribusiness giants that exploit weaker environmental and labor standards.
  • Support food sovereignty and rural communities by prioritizing local, high-quality, and sustainable food production over mass imports that fuel deforestation and industrial farming.

The EU-Mercosur deal is a bad deal for farmers, consumers, and the planet—it’s time for European leaders to put people before corporate profits!

Stop this unfair trade deal—protect our farmers and our food!

Why is this important?

Europe’s small farmers are struggling to survive. Now, a dangerous trade deal between the EU and South America could be the final nail in their coffin. [1]

The EU-Mercosur deal would flood our markets with cheap, industrially-produced meat, grains, and other products—pushing small farmers out of business. How can a local dairy farm or an organic wheat grower compete with giant agribusiness, who destroy forests and use harmful pesticides banned in Europe. [2]

It’s a disaster for farmers, for rural communities, and for our planet. But there’s still time to stop it. European leaders are about to make their final decision—if we act now, we can force them to reject this unfair deal.

Small farmers across Europe are already speaking out, and they can’t fight this battle alone. If we  mobilise enough public opposition, we can convince EU leaders to reject this toxic deal and support sustainable farming instead of bowing to corporate greed.

2025-02-trial-mercosur-pesticides-petiti.description_full:
Keep Banned Pesticides Out of our Food

To the European Parliament and Member States

Petition

We call on the European Parliament and EU Member States to:

  • Reject the EU-Mercosur trade deal, which would allow food grown with pesticides banned in Europe to flood our markets, endangering public health and the environment.
  • Uphold EU food safety standards by preventing toxic pesticide loopholes that benefit big agribusiness at the expense of farmers, consumers, and biodiversity.
  • Ensure fair trade policies that protect European farmers and promote sustainable agriculture instead of prioritizing corporate profits.


We must not let trade agreements undermine the health and environmental protections that Europeans fought hard to achieve. Stop this toxic trade deal—protect our health, farmers, and planet!

Why is this important?

Toxic pesticides banned in Europe are about to end up on our plates more than ever before.

The EU-Mercosur trade deal would allow huge amounts of meat, soy and grains, fruit and vegetables from South America—where pesticides banned in Europe are still widely used—to flood our markets. [1]

The deal is a gift to agribusiness, letting them flood Europe with pesticide-soaked food while our farmers must adhere to strict environmental and health standards. It’s unfair, unsafe, and unacceptable. [2] This deal creates a dangerous loophole for toxic chemicals to sneak into our food system.

Big agribusiness and pesticide giants are pushing hard for this deal, but we can fight back. If enough of us speak out, we can pressure our leaders to reject Mercosur and protect our right to safe, healthy food.

2025-02-trial-omnibus-petition-EN.title: Defend the Green Deal from the polluters' lobby!
2025-02-trial-omnibus-petition-EN.description_full:
Defend the Green Deal from the polluters' lobby!

To the European Commission and national EU governments

Petition

We demand:

  • Strengthen the Green Deal! No rollback of environmental and climate policies. Instead of undermining the Green Deal, we want to develop it further to systematically orient Europe towards climate neutrality, nature-friendly agriculture, a circular economy, and zero pollution as quickly as possible.
  • Socially just environmental and climate policy. Shape the implementation of the Green Deal in such a way that it equally pursues social justice and economic strength. This will bring secure jobs, good wages and a sustainable economy!
  • Simplification instead of trickery! Reducing unnecessary bureaucracy must not be misused to undermine the goals for nature conservation, climate protection and the circular economy!

Why is this important?

The European Green Deal is the most significant environmental and climate protection programme the European Union has ever launched. It is a real milestone for nature conservation, climate protection and the circular economy. In the last five years, 38 EU laws have been adopted to make Europe more climate-friendly and economically sustainable. Their implementation will take Europe a considerable step forward in climate protection and transitioning to a sustainable economy.

However, the ambitious roadmap to make Europe the first climate-neutral continent by 2050 is under threat from the Europe-wide shift to the right.

An alliance of right-wingers and conservatives in the EU Parliament and EU member states is putting pressure on Ursula von der Leyen. The Commission President intends to present proposals that will significantly undermine the Green Deal in the coming weeks. And this is just the beginning. More is to follow! The so-called ‘omnibus’ proposals are a veritable festival for the polluters’ lobby. Under the guise of reducing bureaucracy, the EU Commission wants to gut the Green Deal systematically. The end of new climate-damaging combustion engine cars is just as much at risk as protecting fundamental human rights through the European Supply Chain Act. The EU Commission does not even want to enforce existing legislation for the expansion of renewable energies.

This attack on the Green Deal not only jeopardises the basis of our survival but also the future of a prosperous European economy.

2025-02-trial-youmove-natural-time-petit.title: Are you sick and tired of changing the clock twice a year?
2025-02-trial-youmove-natural-time-petit.description_full:
Are you sick and tired of changing the clock twice a year?

To the Council of the European Union and the European Commission

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We urge our ministers to adopt our countries’ geographical time zones (natural standard time) and put an end to the twice-yearly clock changes in the European Union.

Why is this important?

For thousands of years, people lived according to their biological clocks, which are set by the natural day-night cycle. Our bodies are biologically synchronised with the Earth's natural orbit. Therefore, a healthy time system places the sun at its highest point at 12:00 PM. [1]

However, instead of using permanent natural time, the EU still enforces twice-yearly clock changes. [2] This Daylight Saving Time (DST) system disrupts our biological rhythms and has serious health consequences, including sleep loss, decreased attention and alertness, heart problems, and depression. [3]

The twice-yearly clock changes were originally introduced to reduce energy consumption. Yet, while we may save electricity by turning off lights, more energy is consumed for heating and cooling, which costs more and harms the environment. [4]

In 2018, the European Commission ran a public consultation on clock changes. Out of the 4.6 million Europeans who participated, 84% supported ending clock changes. [5] Concerns included negative health impacts, increased road accidents, and minimal energy savings.

Following overwhelming public support, the Commission proposed a law to abolish clock changes between Standard Time and Daylight Saving Time in the EU. In 2019, the European Parliament adopted this proposal. However, national ministers representing EU countries in the Transport, Telecommunications, and Energy Council (TTE) put the law on hold. Since then, there has been no political progress. [6]

For the EU law to take effect, ministers must ratify it and decide which time zone their countries will adopt permanently. Let’s show our leaders that we, Europeans, want our natural time back!

References:

[1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time 

[2] https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/seasonal-time-changes/

[3] https://www.health.harvard.edu/staying-healthy/the-dark-side-of-daylight-saving-time

https://theconversation.com/why-daylight-saving-time-is-unhealthy-a-neurologist-explains-175427 

[4] https://www.bbc.com/worklife/article/20181102-whats-the-real-cost-of-changing-the-clocks 

[5] Out of the 4.6 million Europeans who participated in a public consultation, 84% supported ending clock changes. 

https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_18_5302 

[6] For the EU law to take effect, our governments, represented in the Council of the European Union, must agree on their position on the proposal, and then negotiate the final text with the European Parliament. https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/policies/seasonal-time-changes/

They also need to decide which time zone their countries will adopt permanently. An easy solution which does not require a patchwork of time zones exists. More here: https://timeuse.barcelona/what-we-do/permanent-time-zones-eu/

2025-03-trial-coffee-child-labour-petiti.title: Our coffee shouldn’t cost a childhood
2025-03-trial-coffee-child-labour-petiti.description_full:
Our coffee shouldn’t cost a childhood

To the coffee industry: especially Illy, Lavazza, Costa Coffee, Rainforest Alliance

Petition

  • End child labor in your entire supply chain through rigorous monitoring, effective remediation, and strong prevention measures.
  • Guarantee a living income for coffee farmers by ensuring fair and stable prices for coffee.
  • Adopt comprehensive human rights policies that cover your entire supply chain, from farm to cup.
  • Conduct regular, unannounced inspections to enforce ethical labor standards and prevent exploitation.
  • Ensure your coffee is deforestation-free by committing to sustainable sourcing practices that protect forests and biodiversity.

Why is this important?

In Chiapas, Mexico, coffee farmers face an impossible choice: send their children to school or put food on the table. Instead of learning to read, many kids, as young as 5 years old, spend their days picking coffee berries for our morning cup of coffee. [1]

This injustice is happening on coffee farms around the world - including those selling to companies that proudly display “ethical” certifications. [2] These companies refuse to pay farmers a fair wage, trapping entire families in poverty and fueling child labor.

But you have the power to help end this abuse.

These coffee giants thrive on a feel-good image. They spend millions convincing consumers they’re ethical while turning a blind eye to child labor. 

We’ve partnered with activists who know this industry inside out. They know which coffee companies are not used to pressure from people like us. When thousands of us shine a light on their “ethical” coffee scam—they’ll be forced to finally clean up their act.

Our coffee shouldn’t cost a childhood. Will you add your name and demand truly fair coffee?

References:

  1.  https://abcnews.go.com/US/caffeine-jungle-child-labor-struggling-farmers-found-ethically/story?id=91735230 
  2. https://coffeewatch.org/coffee-and-human-rights-abuses/

2025-03-trial-rearm-europe-petition-EN.title: Yes to peace, No to the militarisation of Europe!
2025-03-trial-rearm-europe-petition-EN.description_full:
Yes to peace, No to the militarisation of Europe!

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on EU leaders to:

  • Reject the ReArm Europe plan, which diverts billions of euros into the arms industry instead of investing in healthcare, education, and the green transition.
  • Defend peace and diplomacy, opposing an arms race that threatens global security rather than ensuring it.
  • Block the militarisation of the EU budget, ensuring our tax money is used for the well-being of citizens and the building of a fairer, more sustainable Europe.

Europe must not give in to the logic of war and increased military spending. Security is built through cooperation, not weapons. Say NO to the militarisation of the EU!

Why is this important?

A dangerous new arms race is happening in Europe. Our European leaders plan to pour 800 billion euros of our tax money into military expansion. [1]

That’s 800 billion that should be funding our hospitals, schools, and the fight against the climate crisis. Instead, the arms industry and their lobbyists are cashing in.

Scared about Trump’s announcement to cut military support to Europe, politicians want you to think this is about security, but it’s really about profit. Right now, weapons lobbyists are flooding Brussels, demanding public money for more missiles, tanks, and bombs. [2]

As history shows, more weapons don’t bring peace, they lead to escalation and more conflict. [3] A Europe built on arms and militarization will not be safer, it will be one ruled by fear, conflict and instability.

Across Europe, scientists and peace advocates are speaking out against this reckless plan. [4] Now, we must join them and raise our voices louder than the arms lobby.

Tell European leaders: NO to the militarization of Europe—YES to peace, diplomacy, and investment in our future!

References:

[1] https://www.euractiv.com/section/defence/news/von-der-leyens-rearm-europe-plan-and-the-holes-in-it/

[2] https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-defense-industry-goes-big-on-lobbying-in-brussels/ https://enaat.org/2023/12/07/from-war-lobby-to-war-economy-new-enaat-report/

[3] https://www.britannica.com/event/Cold-War/Toward-a-new-world-order  ; https://www.cfr.org/timeline/us-russia-nuclear-arms-control

[4] https://www.iuscientists.org/against-militarization-scientists-unite-in-opposition-to-eu-rearmament/
