2025-08-trial-2-USAID-contraceptives-pet.description_full:
Don’t burn care: save contraceptives, save lives

To the European Commission and the French and Belgian governments

Petition

We call on the European Commission, along with the French and Belgian governments, to:

  • Launch a joint diplomatic effort to stop the destruction of massive stocks of US-funded contraceptives on EU soil, and to help coordinate their delivery to the intended recipients through humanitarian organisations;
  • Conduct a legal review to assess whether this destruction is allowed under EU law, especially considering the EU’s commitments to sustainability and gender equality;
  • Publicly support humanitarian organisations working to redistribute these contraceptives, in line with the EU’s, France’s and Belgium’s pledges to protect women’s health and rights globally.

Why is this important?

Any day now, nearly $10 million worth of US-funded contraceptives could be burned in Europe – all because Trump blocks aid to organisations that support women’s right to choose. [1]

These essential supplies like IUDs and birth control implants, stored in Belgium and scheduled for destruction in France, could save lives, prevent unwanted pregnancies, and support women's autonomy around the world.

Several global health organisations have offered to collect and distribute them where they’re needed most. But the US has rejected those offers. [2]

This is no longer just a US problem. Because the supplies are in Europe, it’s a European responsibility now. Will our leaders let them burn or act to stop this senseless destruction?

The good news: pressure is working.

French and Belgian officials are in talks with the US. French EU lawmakers are urging the European Commission to intervene. [3] And even the US seems to be backing down – the incineration was due by the end of July, but it hasn’t happened yet. [4]

This isn’t just about contraception. It’s about whether Europe will be complicit in Trump’s war on reproductive rights, or stand up for women’s health and dignity. Add your name now to defend women's rights and global health.

But most people - your neighbours, relatives, friends, you and I - still want climate action. [3] We still want to swim in clean rivers, breathe fresh air, and spend our summers in thriving green spaces that haven’t been ravaged by wildfires or floods. 

Let’s build a thousands strong petition now so that by the time our leaders return from the summer break we’ve made clear that any attempt to roll back action on climate change will be met by fierce opposition.

EU: Stop turning your back on the climate!

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

In the face of worsening wildfires, floods and deadly heatwaves across Europe, the EU has just proposed a budget that weakens climate action instead of strengthening it. This is unacceptable.

We call on the European leaders to:

  • Rewrite the 2025–2034 EU budget proposal to ensure that at least 50% of EU funds go toward fighting climate change, restoring nature, and protecting people from its impacts.
  • Reject any budget proposal that fails to meet this target and prioritises short-term profits over the future of our planet.

Why is this important?

Europe is on fire — again.

Heatwaves in Italy, Portugal, Spain, France, Greece and beyond are claiming lives and livelihoods. Droughts are killing crops. Floods are displacing families. [1] And still, the EU is planning to spend the next decade as if none of this is happening.

The EU just proposed its new long-term budget — a once-in-a-decade decision that will shape how trillions of euros are spent until 2034. [2] But right now, that proposal cuts back dedicated climate and nature funding. [3]

If the budget goes through unchanged, it will lock Europe into 10 more years of climate inaction. Wildfires, floods and food shortages will intensify. The EU’s own goals — and our future — will be out of reach. Even the International Court of Justice now says countries have a legal duty to act for the climate, or they may be responsible for human rights violations. [4]

There’s still time to change course. Right now, the Commission can revise the budget. And both the European Parliament and national governments in the Council can reject it unless it puts people and the planet first.

Let’s make sure EU leaders get a message from thousands of Europeans: fix the EU budget, NOW.

2025-08-trial-noise-pollution-petition-E.description_full:
Europe: End dangerous noise pollution now

To EU institutions and national governments

Petition

We call on the European Union and Member States to urgently tackle the noise pollution crisis and protect public health by:

  • Setting legally binding national noise reduction targets aligned with the EU Zero Pollution Action Plan, aiming to reduce by 30% the number of people chronically disturbed by transport noise by 2030. 
  • Increasing dedicated funding for noise mitigation measures, including investments in quieter transport technologies, improved road surfaces, and the construction of noise barriers to reduce noise at its source.
  • Integrating noise management into urban planning and design, prioritising the creation of quieter, healthier public spaces.
  • Providing cities with updated guidance and tools to effectively measure, map, and manage noise pollution using the latest EU noise calculation methodologies, ensuring comparable data and targeted action.
  • Promoting and scaling proven local solutions to demonstrate best practices across Europe.

Why is this important?

Imagine never getting a good night’s sleep because of constant road traffic or aircraft overhead. This is the daily reality for 1 in 3 Europeans. [1]

This isn’t just annoying. Transport noise harms our health. It’s linked to heart disease, depression [2], and even early death. Children’s learning suffers. Wildlife is disrupted. And our economy bears the cost – nearly €100 billion every year. [3]

The EU has promised to reduce the number of people chronically harmed by transport noise by 30% by 2030. But at the current pace, not only will we miss that target – we’re on track for things to get worse. [4]

The good news? Cities across Europe are already proving change is possible.

In Antwerp, parks have been redesigned with noise barriers and water features to create peaceful urban spaces. Rotterdam has introduced excessive noise alerts to encourage quieter driving habits. [5] Florence is testing quieter road surfaces for electric vehicles. [6]

These are practical, proven steps – what’s missing is political will to scale them up for all cities in Europe.

Our leaders like to present themselves as champions of innovation. Let’s challenge them to prove it – by matching the ambition of these cities and delivering on their EU obligations. 

Your voice will help show there’s strong public support for bold action – and that the time to lead is now.

Let’s tell our leaders: don’t fall behind – lead the way in building a healthier future for us all.

Building on this success, Rotterdam is exploring the possibility of introducing noise flash cameras that could automatically issue fines to those who violate noise regulations, further enhancing enforcement.”

2025-08-trial-underwater-garden-youmove-.title: Immediate cancellation of the Underwater Garden megaproject!
2025-08-trial-underwater-garden-youmove-.description_full:
Immediate cancellation of the Underwater Garden megaproject!

To Marc García-Durán Huet and the Cabildo of Tenerife

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We demand:

  • The immediate withdrawal of Marc García-Durán Huet from the Underwater Garden project.
  • A public commitment from the Cabildo of Tenerife to not support massive tourism infrastructures disguised as sustainability.
  • The prioritisation of real marine conservation measures and the expansion of marine reserves instead of tourism megaprojects.

Why is this important?

Presented as a “regenerative” space with underwater gardens and high-end entertainment activities, Underwater Garden is in fact a speculative megaproject in a protected area that will endanger the ecosystem, restrict free access to the sea, and negatively impact the lifestyle of the local community.

Why we say NO:

  • It is not regenerative: it is a luxury theme park that will bring speculation, overcrowding, and destruction.
  • Severe environmental impact: it will alter marine and coastal ecosystems, increase boat traffic, and affect vulnerable species.
  • It excludes the community: it effectively privatizes a space that has always been freely used by locals.
  • A threat to a unique wave: its infrastructure could change currents and ruin an iconic wave for surfers and biodiversity.
  • Gentrification: it will raise housing prices and displace the local population.
  • Lack of transparency: the promoter hides key information and greenwashes the project.
  • Dangerous precedent: it would open the door to more destructive megaprojects we’ve been fighting for years, like the now-forgotten Fonsalía port.

 

Instead of further destroying the coast and local lifestyle, there are sustainable and respectful alternatives for nature and island culture:

  • Protect the coast and seabed: expand reserves like the Special Conservation Zone (ZEC) Teno-Rasca and effectively protect existing ones.
  • Regenerate degraded coastal areas: restore natural spaces and conserve biodiversity without turning nature into a business.
  • Promote dignified local economies: support the primary sector and the blue economy, creating real jobs for the local population.

 

Tenerife doesn’t need more theme parks and greenwashing projects—it needs to protect its natural wealth.

Sign and join us to stop Underwater Garden! The island belongs to its people, not to multinationals.

Don’t burn care: save contraceptives, save lives

To the European Commission and the French and Belgian governments

Petition

We call on the European Commission, along with the French and Belgian governments, to:

  • Launch a joint diplomatic effort to stop the destruction of massive stocks of US-funded contraceptives on EU soil, and to help coordinate their delivery to the intended recipients through humanitarian organisations;
  • Conduct a legal review to assess whether this destruction is allowed under EU law, especially considering the EU’s commitments to sustainability and gender equality;
  • Publicly support humanitarian organisations working to redistribute these contraceptives, in line with the EU’s, France’s and Belgium’s pledges to protect women’s health and rights globally.

Why is this important?

Any day now, nearly $10 million worth of US-funded contraceptives could be burned in Europe – all because Trump blocks aid to organisations that support women’s right to choose. [1]

These essential supplies like IUDs and birth control implants, stored in Belgium and scheduled for destruction in France, could save lives, prevent unwanted pregnancies, and support women's autonomy around the world.

Several global health organisations have offered to collect and distribute them where they’re needed most. But the US has rejected those offers. [2]

This is no longer just a US problem. Because the supplies are in Europe, it’s a European responsibility now. Will our leaders let them burn or act to stop this senseless destruction?

The good news: pressure is working.

French and Belgian officials are in talks with the US. French EU lawmakers are urging the European Commission to intervene. [3] And even the US seems to be backing down – the incineration was due by the end of July, but it hasn’t happened yet. [4]

This isn’t just about contraception. It’s about whether Europe will be complicit in Trump’s war on reproductive rights, or stand up for women’s health and dignity. Add your name now to defend women's rights and global health.

We call on the European Union and its Member States to:

According to testimonies, Thiago has been subjected to “extreme brutality” by the Israeli military, including being “dragged face-down across the floor and beaten so severely that he passed out twice”. [4] 

Others from the flotilla describe violence, humiliation, denial of care. [5] This is what happens today to people who refuse to look away from Gaza.

Send an email to Ursula von der Leyen and Kaja Kallas now. Demand they use every tool at their disposal to secure the immediate release of the hostages, protect humanitarian missions, and defend Palestinians.

We cannot accept this. Not in our name. Because silence, right now, is a choice.

Break up Big Tech

To the European Commission

Petition

We call on the European Commission to break up Google’s monopoly over digital advertising, and take broader action to dismantle the unchecked power of Big Tech monopolies across Europe’s digital economy. This includes robust enforcement of competition law to force dominant tech companies to sell off parts of their businesses where needed to restore fair competition, protect consumers, and defend our democracy.

Why is this important?

Every time you open a news site, Google gets paid. These days most of us consume our information and news online. But every time you search, Google decides what you see. 

Google’s monopoly over digital advertising has bankrupted independent journalism. By dominating the ad market, it sucks up the money that used to fund independent media, leaving newsrooms struggling or shutting down. [1]

But it’s not just the media that suffers, it’s all of us. When independent journalism dies, so does our right to know the truth. And without the truth, democracy plunges into the dark.

But for the first time in decades, we have a real shot to break the stranglehold. A US judge just confirmed that Google has an illegal advertising monopoly. [2]

At the same time, the European Commission is about to finish its own investigation into Google’s ad tech monopoly any day now. [3]

This is a once-in-a-generation moment to disrupt Big Tech’s power, by breaking up Google and others like Meta and Apple into separate companies. Tell the EU Commission they have a mandate from people across Europe to break up Big Tech monopolies!

2025-09-trial-mercosur-pesticides-kicker.title: Keep Banned Pesticides Out of our Food
2025-09-trial-mercosur-pesticides-kicker.description_full:
Keep Banned Pesticides Out of our Food

Ministers and Members of the European Parliament 

Petition

We call on EU Member States and the European Parliament to:

  • Reject the EU-Mercosur trade deal, which would allow food grown with pesticides banned in Europe to flood our markets, endangering public health and the environment.
  • Uphold EU food safety standards by preventing toxic pesticide loopholes that benefit big agribusiness at the expense of farmers, consumers, and biodiversity.
  • Ensure fair trade policies that protect European farmers and promote sustainable agriculture instead of prioritizing corporate profits.

We must not let trade agreements undermine the health and environmental protections that Europeans fought hard to achieve. Stop this toxic trade deal—protect our health, farmers, and planet!

Why is this important?

Trump’s tariffs on the EU have sparked panic in Brussels. But at the same time as selling out to Trump, they’re rushing to sign off on another dangerous deal – to secure free trade with South America. [1]

If the Mercosur trade deal passes, more toxic pesticides will end up in our food. [2] Europe’s farmers will struggle even more, undercut by cheap imports of beef, soy and other products that don’t have to follow European environmental standards. The EU will also be part of destroying hectares of forests in South America and displacing indigenous communities. [3] 

This week, the European Commission will send the treaty to EU countries and the European Parliament for approval.[4] 

The good news? Major governments like France and Poland oppose the deal, and it can’t pass without a strong majority. 

Politicians are already under pressure after agreeing to Trump’s tariffs. Together let’s expose how the EU is risking our climate and food standards again in another toxic trade deal. More than 90,000 people have already joined. Add your name now to protect our food, our farmers, and our forests.

2025-09-trial-methane-companies-petition.description_full:
Call on European supermarkets: Cut methane, cut meat!

To the Europe’s biggest retailers: Carrefour, Ahold Delhaize, Schwarz (Lidl), ALDI, Migros

Petition

Cut methane from your produce that is driving climate change and report transparently!

  • Commit to a methane reduction target of at least 30% by 2030
  • Set a clear sales target of 60% plant-based and 40% animal-based proteins by 2030. By expanding the range of attractive plant-based products, you can cut emissions and support healthier diets.
  • Disclose your emissions and sales of methane-emitting produce each year, including from meat and dairy.

Why is this important?

A new report has exposed how Europe’s biggest supermarkets are fuelling climate change through the produce they sell. Methane from meat and dairy is among the fastest-acting emissions heating our planet. [1] And yet, supermarkets are failing to act. Most have no targets to cut methane and hide the true cost to the planet of our shopping baskets.

Europe’s biggest supermarkets – like Carrefour, Lidl, ALDI, and Migros – have the power to transform the sustainability of our food systems. With their influence over food supply chains and what ends up on our plates, they are uniquely positioned to tackle methane from meat and dairy. [2]

We’ve already seen it can work. Dutch supermarket chain Albert Heijn has just become the first major supermarket to publicly disclose its methane emissions. [3] Transparency is the first step toward protecting our planet – and communities on the frontline of wildfires, floods and other climate disasters.

Together, let's urge Europe’s biggest supermarkets to cut methane emissions and report with full transparency!

2025-09-trial-oil-gas-Baltic-petition-EN.description_full:
Stop new oil and gas extraction in the Baltic Sea!

To the Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland, the Helsinki Commission (HELCOM), the European Commission, and the Secretariat of the Espoo Convention

Petition

We call on you to undertake urgent actions to:

  • Stop the plans for oil and gas extraction in the Oder Estuary and the Pomeranian Bay, violating climate and environmental regulations and goals;
  • Ban any new oil and gas extraction across the Baltic Sea, preventing deterioration and ensuring protection of Baltic marine ecosystem;
  • Ensure strong cross-border cooperation and communication amongst all involved states, including sharing of environmental impact assessments and timely notifications of planned consultations or other measures.

Why is this important?

Shocking plans just came to light: drilling for oil and gas in the Baltic Sea on the edge of a protected bird sanctuary in Poland. [1] Imagine holiday beaches shadowed by drilling rigs, seas filled with toxic leaks, and porpoises silenced by constant underwater noise. It’s an immediate danger to nature, our climate and the livelihoods of people who depend on tourism and a clean Baltic sea.

Scientists are clear: if we want to slow down global warming, no new oil or gas fields can be developed. [2] Yet the Polish government risks locking us all into decades more of fossil fuel dependence, while breaking EU nature protection rules and climate goals. [3] 

We can force decision-makers in Warsaw and Brussels to stop the drilling plans off the Polish coast and ban all oil and gas extraction in the Baltic Sea. At  a meeting in just two weeks, Baltic governments, EU ministers and policymakers will come together. This is our chance to be heard. [4] If we flood them with signatures and community voices just before that meeting, they’ll be forced to respond.

Every signature is proof that people across Europe refuse to let short-term profits destroy our seas and our future. Add your voice to a growing European movement calling for a rig-free, safe Baltic!

References:

[1] https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7786/artykul/3554241,central-european-petroleum-confirms-major-oil-discovery-off-baltic-coast 

[2] https://www.iea.org/reports/net-zero-by-2050 

[3] Such projects contradict the purpose of EU NATURA 2000 protected areas and would breach several EU and international commitments, including the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, the Birds Directive, the Habitats Directive, the Helsinki Convention and its Baltic Sea Action Plan (BSAP) as well as climate goals. 

[4] https://oceans-and-fisheries.ec.europa.eu/events/our-baltic-ministerial-conference-2025-09-30_enm

2025-09-trial-trump-trade-deal-trial-pet.description_full:
Say no to Trump’s trade deal

To the Members of the European Parliament

Petition

We call on the Members of the European Parliament to reject the EU-US trade deal under the current conditions. A new deal should:

  1. Ensure that the EU stays on track with the climate goals it has committed to and doesn’t agree to fossil gas imports from the US.
  2. Protect EU digital consumer rules and make sure US tech companies don’t misuse their market dominance.

 

If Commission President Ursula von der Leyen isn’t able to negotiate a deal that works for the people and the planet, we ask you to support a no-confidence vote in the European Parliament.

Why is this important?

Many people across Europe may be feeling like you do. A new survey proves what the majority of Europeans think: we don’t want Trump’s trade deal. [1]

And we’re right to resist. Trump’s trade pact would lock Europe into €700 billion worth of fossil gas — tying us to decades of pollution and climate damage. [2] It could also undermine the rules that protect consumers and rein in powerful corporations like Google. [3]

But Europe can do better. We can invest in clean, reliable energy instead of fossil fuels. We can protect people, not corporations. We can show the world that Europe stands for climate action, fairness, and democracy. 

The good news: the deal isn’t a done deal. 

The European Parliament still needs to approve it. Already, one of the biggest groups in Parliament is against it, and pressure is mounting on Commission President von der Leyen to change course. [4]

This is our moment to show Europe’s strength. By raising our voices now, we can push MEPs to reject this deal — and open the door for a Europe that invests in clean, reliable energy, protects people, and stands strong against bullies like Trump.

Tell your representatives today: Vote NO to Trump’s trade deal.

2025-10-07-tax-the-rich-re-activation-tr.title: Tax the Super Rich!
2025-10-07-tax-the-rich-re-activation-tr.description_full:
Tax the Super Rich! Please accept marketing cookies to watch this video

To the European Commission

Petition

We call on the European Commission to establish a European excess wealth tax, based on Article 115 TFEU. This tax will create a common policy approach and coordinated action to maximize the positive impact of excess wealth taxation.

Why is this important?

While thousands of us face the impossible rise in the cost of basic goods or heating our homes this winter, the mega rich keep getting richer. It’s because billionaires don’t pay their fair share of taxes. [1]  

The richest 1% own nearly half of all the wealth, but they barely pay any tax. They exploit tax havens and use loopholes to send as little taxes as possible to our governments - depriving  all of us of vital money to finance our hospitals, teachers, and nurses. [2] 

But now we have an opportunity to stop this injustice. Spain is already experimenting with taxing the wealth of the super rich. [3] This tax has and can generate billions of Euros, and bring the resources to finance the essential services we desperately need.

Together, let’s call for a tax on the rich for a more fair Europe! Demand a European wealth tax for the super rich! 

This wealth tax on the super rich is already a reality in Spain: it’s currently raised over 1.8 billion Euros in 2023. [4] If adopted across Europe, we could inject billions into our healthcare systems, education and public transport. [5] 

And we wouldn’t just have money for our failing public services, but also use it to help those communities most affected by the climate crisis. While the super-rich are most responsible for the climate crisis, it’s young people and the poor who are most affected. [6] They face the worst of droughts, floods, heatwaves and fires. 

We believe we all should pay our fair share in tax and help those in need. Taxing the wealthiest more is what’s right, what’s needed, and will make a huge difference! But politicians won’t take action until they know the public is behind them. Together, let’s demand a wealth tax on the super rich!

2025-10-trial-dpc-ireland-petition-2-EN.description_full:
Don’t let Big Tech lobbyists exploit our data!

To the Irish Government, the Irish Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration, and the European Commission

Petition

We call on Ireland to ensure the independence of their data supervisory body by:

  1. Re-hiring a new Commissioner to the Irish Data Protection Commission with a track-record of protecting citizen rights and fundamental freedoms, and data protection in particular.
  2. Doing an independent review of the process by which the current appointment was made.

We also call on the European Commission to ensure the impartiality and independence of all national Data Protection Authorities.

Why is this important?

Facebook lobbyists deciding how much of your data Big Tech can grab sounds like a nightmare, right?

Well, that’s what’s happening. Ireland just appointed an ex-Facebook lobbyist as its new data chief - the person meant to keep Big Tech in check. [1]

Ireland is home to all the Big Tech companies. They chose it because of low taxes. And because regulators there have looked the other way for years.

Now, the government has dropped all pretense, and put a Facebook insider in charge of policing Big Tech. Policing their former bosses.

What happens in Ireland affects us all. If Europe’s privacy laws don’t apply to Big Tech in Ireland, they don’t protect anyone, anywhere in Europe.

Digital rights groups have raised the alarm, but the government hopes it will disappear. [3]

Enough of us need to speak up and make them appoint someone who actually defends our rights, not corporate profits.

They have their backroom deals. We have people power. Every signature adds to the growing outcry. Together we can force Ireland to reverse course.

Add your name now to demand real data protection in Ireland — and all of Europe.

2025-10-trial-harmit-onboarding-petition.description_full:
Harmit trial onboarding

To the European Commission, the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on the European Union to urgently revise and strengthen its tobacco control legislation in light of the rising use of novel nicotine products, particularly among young people.

Specifically, we urge the EU to update the following directives:

  • The Tobacco Taxation Directive (2011)
  • The Tobacco Products Directive (2014)
  • The Tobacco Advertising Directive (2003)

These revisions should aim to:

  1. Increase excise taxes on all tobacco and nicotine-containing products to effectively discourage consumption.

  2. Broaden the scope of regulation to explicitly include emerging products such as e-cigarettes, heated tobacco products, and nicotine pouches. Clear and comprehensive definitions must be established to close existing regulatory loopholes.

  3. Modernize advertising restrictions by expanding the Tobacco Advertising Directive to cover all media channels—especially online platforms and digital marketing—and include indirect advertising methods, such as corporate social responsibility sponsorships.

By updating these outdated directives, the EU can better protect public health and achieve a tobacco-free generation by 2040, as set out in Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan.

Why is this important?

<NAME>, across Europe, a new generation is getting hooked — not on cigarettes, but on nicotine pouches, vapes, and other addictive products flooding the market. [1]

While teens face serious risks to brain development and lifelong addiction [2], Big Tobacco is pushing hard for EU laws to remain dangerously out of date. [3]

The EU has pledged a tobacco-free generation by 2040. [4] But a minority of tobacco-producing countries are stalling progress.

Since March, the majority of EU states — backed by over 120 organisations — have called on the European Commission to finally update tobacco laws and tax vapes and nicotine pouches across the EU. [5]  A key Commissioner said a new tax proposal could come by summer. [6]

It’s now June. Still no action. That’s why I’m writing to you today, <NAME>. 

Big Tobacco is doing everything it can to keep laws weak and profits high — but no politician wants to be seen as putting the profits of a cancerous industry before the health of our teens.

We need a surge of public pressure to cut through the influence of the toxic tobacco lobby. Add your name now and tell the EU to stand up to Big Tobacco, tax addictive nicotine products, and protect young people across Europe.

Since March, the majority of EU states — backed by over 120 organisations — have called on the European Commission to finally update tobacco laws and tax vapes and nicotine pouches across the EU. [5]  A key Commissioner said a new tax proposal could come by summer. [6]

It’s now June. Still no action. That’s why I’m writing to you today. 

Big Tobacco is doing everything it can to keep laws weak and profits high — but no politician wants to be seen as putting the profits of a cancerous industry before the health of our teens.

We need a surge of public pressure to cut through the influence of the toxic tobacco lobby. Add your name now and tell the EU to stand up to Big Tobacco, tax addictive nicotine products, and protect young people across Europe.

Say NO to Trump’s trade deal

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on you to reject the EU-US trade deal in its current form. A new deal should:

  1. Ensure that the EU stays on track with its climate goals, doesn’t agree to buy fossil fuels from the US, and doesn’t weaken existing EU climate laws like the methane regulation
  2. Protect EU digital consumers and make sure US Big Tech companies don’t abuse their market dominance.

We want you to negotiate a deal that puts people and the planet above corporate profits.

Why is this important?

People across Europe are feeling like you do. A recent survey shows that the majority of Europeans don’t want Trump’s trade deal. [1]

A deal that forces the EU to buy €700 billion of fossil fuels and nuclear energy from the US. This dirty deal would set us back — on fighting climate change and protecting citizens from powerful corporations. [2]

But Europe can do better. We can invest in clean, reliable energy instead of fossil fuels. We can protect people, not fossil fuel companies. We can show the US that Europe stands for climate action, fairness and democracy. 

The good news: this isn’t a done deal. 

The European Parliament and our governments haven’t approved it yet. So the earlier we step in, the more chances we will have to stop it.

Already, pressure is mounting on Commission President von der Leyen to change course. Her job is even on the line! [3] 

This is our moment to show Europe’s strength. By raising our voices now, we can push our leaders to reject this deal — and open the door for a Europe that invests in clean, homegrown energy. And stands strong against bullies like Trump.

Tell European leaders today: Say NO to Trump’s trade deal.

2025-11-04-trial-housing-for-all-petitio.description_full:
Make Homes for People, Not for Profit

To: Dan Jørgensen, European Commissioner for Climate Action and Housing/Urban Policy; the European Commission’s Housing Task Force (DG GROW); and Members of the European Parliament’s Committee on Housing (HOUS)

Petition

Homes are disappearing for ordinary Europeans. Families freeze, students struggle, locals are pushed out.

Housing is a human right — not a profit opportunity.

We call on those in power to act now:

  • Guarantee decent, affordable housing for all.
  • Hold developers and investors accountable for speculation and empty homes.
  • Invest in social and public housing that keeps people in their communities.
  • Renovate homes for people and planet — with fair rules that keep bills low and residents in place
  • Keep rents fair and limit tourist rentals so cities stay homes for people.

Homes are the foundation of our lives and our future.

It’s time to put people before profit — and make housing a right for all.

Why is this important?

Everyone deserves a safe, affordable place to call home.

But across Europe, people are being priced out of their cities. [1] People are forced to move farther and farther away from their jobs, their friends, their roots.

It doesn’t have to be this way. And European lawmakers know it.

Last week, EU leaders discussed housing for the first time in history. [2] 

We are a part of a movement putting affordable housing at the top of the EU agenda. Together, we refuse to accept a system that puts profit before people. [3]  

European lawmakers are now looking at solutions to the housing crisis. [4]

Now is the time to speak up. We can still change the course, if we act now.

Let’s make it impossible for leaders to ignore us: our right to housing is not for sale.

Name storms after climate culprits

To the EUMETNET (the network of 33 European National Meteorological & Hydrological Services)

Petition

The people and corporations most responsible for climate catastrophe need to be held accountable for the devastation their actions cause. We call on the EUMETNET to name storms after individuals and corporations with the highest climate emission contributions.

Why is this important?

The world’s wealthiest 10% have caused two thirds of global warming since 1990. [1] The people most impacted by climate change are the least likely to have caused it. [2]

People in Jamaica are recovering from one of the worst hurricanes on record, and people in China faced a summer of deadly floods. [3] [4] While these and countless other communities try to rebuild from the impact of climate change, the wealthy individuals most responsible for this destruction stay in the shadows. 

It’s time we put these names in the headlines for their real impact - destroying the planet and people's lives. Naming storms after billionaires and corporations will make it impossible for them to hide their complicity from the public. 

_______

Tax the Super Rich! Please accept marketing cookies to watch this video

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on the European Commission to establish a European excess wealth tax, based on Article 115 TFEU. This tax will create a common policy approach and coordinated action to maximize the positive impact of excess wealth taxation.

Why is this important?

While thousands of us face the impossible rise in the cost of basic goods or heating our homes this winter, the mega rich keep getting richer. It’s because billionaires don’t pay their fair share of taxes. [1]  

The richest 1% own nearly half of all the wealth, but they barely pay any tax. They exploit tax havens and use loopholes to send as little taxes as possible to our governments - depriving  all of us of vital money to finance our hospitals, teachers, and nurses. [2] 

But now we have an opportunity to stop this injustice. Spain is already experimenting with taxing the wealth of the super rich. [3] This tax has and can generate billions of Euros, and bring the resources to finance the essential services we desperately need.

Together, let’s call for a tax on the rich for a more fair Europe! Demand a European wealth tax for the super rich! 

This wealth tax on the super rich is already a reality in Spain: it’s currently raised over 1.8 billion Euros in 2023. [4] If adopted across Europe, we could inject billions into our healthcare systems, education and public transport. [5] 

And we wouldn’t just have money for our failing public services, but also use it to help those communities most affected by the climate crisis. While the super-rich are most responsible for the climate crisis, it’s young people and the poor who are most affected. [6] They face the worst of droughts, floods, heatwaves and fires. 

We believe we all should pay our fair share in tax and help those in need. Taxing the wealthiest more is what’s right, what’s needed, and will make a huge difference! But politicians won’t take action until they know the public is behind them. Together, let’s demand a wealth tax on the super rich!

2025-11-ban-shark-meat-2-A-trial-petitio.title: Ban shark meat! Protect our oceans and our health
2025-11-ban-shark-meat-2-A-trial-petitio.description_full:
Ban shark meat! Protect our oceans and our health

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on you to:

  1. Equal health standards for all fish: Align the legal limit for methylmercury in shark and ray meat with that of other predatory fish, reducing it from 1.0 mg/kg to 0.5 mg/kg.
  2. Ban shark meat: Ban the sale of shark and ray products that exceed EU limits for toxic substances.
  3. Ensure transparency and traceability: Make labelling of species, origin, and toxin levels mandatory for all seafood products and increase official controls.
  4. Take responsibility through cooperation: Strengthen collaboration between EU health, environment, and fisheries authorities to reduce global shark and ray trade and support marine protected areas.

Why is this important?

270,000 sharks are killed every day. That’s three every second. [1] And with every single one of them, the fragile balance of the ocean crumbles a little more.

Sharks are the guardians of the seas. For millions of years, they’ve kept marine life in check - helping coral reefs breathe, fish populations recover, and the ocean stay alive. But now, over one in three shark species is threatened with extinction. [2]

And Europe is a big part of the problem.

Our fishing boats are among the world’s largest exporters of shark meat. Our supermarkets, hospitals and schools still sell it [3] - often under hidden names like rock salmon or dog fish. Every fillet on a shelf means another animal pulled from the sea, often brutally killed.

But it doesn’t have to be this way. Austria has already banned all shark products - proving that change is possible and that Europe can choose protection over profit. [4]

By banning all shark products from the EU, we can follow that lead - protecting sharks, the ocean, and the future of life on Earth.

Sign today to protect sharks. Because without sharks, the ocean collapses. And without the ocean, so do we.

Ban shark meat! Protect our oceans and our health

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on you to:

  1. Equal health standards for all fish: Align the legal limit for methylmercury in shark and ray meat with that of other predatory fish, reducing it from 1.0 mg/kg to 0.5 mg/kg.
  2. Ban shark meat: Ban the sale of shark and ray products that exceed EU limits for toxic substances.
  3. Ensure transparency and traceability: Make labelling of species, origin, and toxin levels mandatory for all seafood products and increase official controls.
  4. Take responsibility through cooperation: Strengthen collaboration between EU health, environment, and fisheries authorities to reduce global shark and ray trade and support marine protected areas.

Why is this important?

Memory loss. Tremors. Loss of coordination. Vision and hearing problems. Irreversible brain damage. [1] 

These are some of the symptoms of mercury poisoning. And a new study shows that shark meat sold in Europe contains alarming and illegal levels of it. [2] 

Nearly two-thirds of samples tested in supermarkets and restaurants across Europe had unsafe levels of mercury,  some four times above what’s considered “safe”. This toxin builds up in the body and attacks the nervous system. 

Yet EU law still allows twice as much mercury in shark and ray meat as in other fish - leaving consumers unprotected and unaware. [3] 

Why? Because Europe is one of the biggest shark traders in the world. [4] This double standard keeps contaminated products on our plates - and keeps a dangerous, destructive trade alive.

It doesn’t have to be this way. Austria has already banned all shark products, proving that change is possible. [5]

Sign now to tell the EU that it must act to protect our health - and the ocean we depend on.

Sharks are the guardians of the seas. For millions of years, they’ve kept marine life in check - helping coral reefs breathe, fish populations recover, and the ocean stay alive. But now, more than one in three shark species is threatened with extinction. [2]

And Europe is a big part of the problem.

Spain, Portugal, France and Italy are among the world’s largest exporters of shark meat. Our supermarkets, hospitals and schools still sell it [3] - often under hidden names like rock salmon or dogfish. Every fillet on a shelf means another animal pulled from the sea, often brutally killed.

2025-11-dare-to-solidare-europe-keep-you.description_full:
DARE to SoliDARE - Europe, keep youth and solidarity alive for your future sake!

European Commission (Ursula von der Leyen, President / Glenn Micallef, Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport / Roxana Mînzatu, Vice-President, Commissioner for Social Rights and Skills, Quality Jobs and Preparedness / Dubravka Šuica, Mediterranean Commissioner, DGEAC) Members of the European Parliament (especially committees such as CULT Culture and Education / BUDG Budgets / EMPL Employment and Social Affairs / EUDS European Democracy Shield) European Council (especially Youth Working Party)

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We call on the European Commission, the European Parliament, and the Council of the EU to ensure that youth, solidarity, and volunteering remain at the core of the next Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps (2028–2034).
Specifically, we ask them to:

  • Reinstate a dedicated Youth Chapter with a clear budget (minimum 15% of Erasmus+).
  • Safeguard Solidarity Projects as a separate and accessible action.
  • Guarantee sustainable, multi-annual funding for volunteering organisations.
  • Invest in capacity building for the youth civil sector and support structures.
  • Ensure equal opportunities for young people from Neighbouring Countries.

In short: Keep youth and solidarity alive in Europe’s next Erasmus+ — for the sake of our shared future.
 


__________________________________

Full text - SoliDARE Proclamation

 

Adopted by the 105 participants at the SoliDARE Meeting, October 2025

(organisations active in the European Solidarity Corps in Programme and Partner Countries)

 

Addressed to the European Commission, European Parliament, and Council of the EU

 

We, the participants of the SoliDARE 2025 Meeting, representing 99 organizations from 31 Programme and Partner Countries, united by the values of solidarity, inclusion, and youth empowerment, call on the European institutions to strengthen the future Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes (2028–2034).

Our united voice reaffirms that youth and solidarity must remain at the core of Europe’s future. The interim evaluation has shown this clearly: 71% of ESC participants say they would not have had access to comparable opportunities without the programme, underscoring the unique and irreplaceable role of ESC. 

We welcome the Commission’s intention to place mobility, civic engagement, and volunteering as central pillars of the next generation of programmes – essential both to sustain established frameworks like the European Youth Strategy and to connect with newer priorities such as the Union of Skills and Preparedness. However, we are concerned that youth policy, youth work, and solidarity could lose visibility, resources, and impact unless key safeguards are secured.

 

Our Key Messages

 

1. We NEED A Strong Youth Chapter with a Clear Budget

- Reinstate a dedicated Youth Chapter with its own objectives and visibility.
- Ensure an earmarked budget of minimum 15% of the overall Erasmus+ allocation for youth, to keep in line with the current programmes.

2. Young people NEED Solidarity Projects as a Separate Action

- Safeguard Solidarity Projects as an independent action, distinct from Youth Participation activities.
- Recognise them as the entry point for newcomers, local groups, and grassroots actors.
- Expand the model through micro-granting schemes, making funding accessible and youth friendly.

3. Youth Organizations NEED Sustainable Funding for Volunteering

- Guarantee multi-annual and predictable funding for planning sustainable volunteering activities.
- Ensure that the average annual grant per organisation does not decrease, reversing negative trends observed in the current ESC programme.

4. Youth Sector NEEDs Capacity Building for Youth Civil Sector

- Allocate specific measures and budgets for capacity building and operational support of national and local youth NGOs, managed by National Agencies.
- Reinforce supporting instruments (Training & Cooperation Activities, SALTO Resource Centres, Youthpass, Youth Dialogue) as the fundamental pillars of quality youth work which drive successful outcomes.

5. World NEEDs Equal Treatment for Neighboring Countries

- Address  barriers which can lead to exclusionary outcomes, such as the 25% budget cap on cooperation with Partner Countries. This inclusive vision should also reflect the renewed framework of cooperation under the New Pact for the Mediterranean, reinforcing youth engagement and civic participation across the Southern Neighbourhood within a shared Euro-Mediterranean vision.
- Allow youth in Neighboring Regions to access Solidarity Projects, Youth Participation activities, and mobility on equal terms, strengthening Europe’s partnerships and solidarity beyond borders.

 

Conclusion

The SoliDARE community believes that Youth, Solidarity, and Volunteering MUST remain central in the next Erasmus+ framework. 

Europe’s resilience, inclusiveness, and democratic future depend on empowered young people who can act locally, and connect globally with a specific focus on the Neighboring Regions such as the Southern Neighborhood, Eastern Europe & Caucasus, and South-East Europe.

The future Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps should also align with the EU’s Global Gateway, positioning the youth sector as a central actor in advancing human connectivity, education, and civic cooperation between Europe and its partners. We therefore urge the European institutions to take these demands into account in the ongoing negotiations for Erasmus+ 2028–2034.

SoliDARE Participants, 2025

Why is this important?

Because without youth and solidarity, Europe loses its future.

The European Solidarity Corps has given hundreds of thousands of young people the chance to volunteer, learn, and act for their communities — opportunities they would not otherwise have had. Yet in the design of the next Erasmus+ (2028–2034), youth work, volunteering, and solidarity risk losing visibility, funding, and dedicated space.

This petition calls on European leaders to protect what makes Europe unique: its young people’s capacity to connect, care, and create change.

A strong Youth Chapter, accessible Solidarity Projects, and fair inclusion for all regions are not just policy details — they are minimum requirements for a united, resilient, and democratic Europe.

Let’s make sure solidarity and youth stays at the heart of Europe’s future!

For a welcoming Europe!

To the Members of the European Parliament, the European Commission, and the Council of the European Union

Petition

The European Commission’s new Deportation Regulation would tear families apart, expand detention, and turn migration into a business for private security and surveillance companies.

We call on the EU to choose care, dignity, and humanity - not fear and profit.

We urge you to:

  • Reject the Deportation Regulation in its current form;
  • Stop outsourcing migration control to private corporations and third countries;
  • Invest in protection, inclusion, and safe pathways for people on the move.

Europe must stand for human rights, not human suffering.

Why is this important?

Freddie Mercury is shining again on a giant London billboard with one simple truth: Thank god for immigrants. [1]

It’s a reminder that migration built the Europe we love - our nurses and doctors, our teachers and artists, our neighbours and friends. But right now, in Brussels, politicians are pushing laws that would silence that truth.

As you read this, private security and detention companies are lobbying behind closed doors in Brussels - pushing a plan to send people away instead of protecting them. [2] 

A law that would tear families apart, send people to countries they barely know, and even lock children in detention camps, cut off from schools, lawyers, and care. [3]

This isn’t the Europe we believe in. And it’s not the Europe we want to become.

Across the continent, hundreds of organisations are already raising their voices, and even some governments are questioning this path. [4]

But the most powerful voice is still missing: that of regular people like you and me. Every movement that ever changed Europe started when people like us decided to speak out - and refused to look away. Add your name to say: not in my name!

Don’t let Big Tech lobbyists exploit our data!

To the European Commission, the Irish Government, and the Irish Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration

Petition

We call on the European Commission to ensure 

  • The impartiality and independence of all national Data Protection Authorities.
  • Especially the impartiality and independence of the Data Protection Commission in Ireland, responsible to enforce Europe’s GDPR rules on tech companies operating all over Europe from Ireland. 

We also call on Ireland to ensure the independence of their data supervisory body by

  • Re-hiring a new Commissioner to the Irish Data Protection Commission with a track-record of protecting citizen rights and fundamental freedoms, and data protection in particular.
  • Doing an independent review of the hiring process by which the current appointment was made.

Why is this important?

Ireland has appointed an ex-Facebook lobbyist as its new data chief - the person meant to keep Big Tech in check. [1]

Ireland is home to all the Big Tech companies. They chose it because of low taxes. And because regulators there have looked the other way for years.

Now, the government has dropped all pretense, and put a Facebook insider in charge of policing Big Tech. Policing their former bosses.

What happens in Ireland affects us all. If Europe’s privacy laws don’t apply to Big Tech in Ireland, they don’t protect anyone, anywhere in Europe.

Digital rights groups have raised the alarm, but the government hopes it will disappear. [2]

Enough of us need to speak up and make them appoint someone who actually defends our rights, not corporate profits.

They have their backroom deals. We have people power. Every signature adds to the growing outcry. Together we can force the EU to call on Ireland to reverse course.

Add your name now to demand real data protection in Ireland — and all of Europe.

It’s time to put people before profit and make housing a right for all.

Everyone deserves a safe, affordable place to call home.

But across Europe, people are being priced out of their cities. [1] Forced to move farther and farther away from their jobs, their friends, their roots.

It doesn’t have to be this way. And European lawmakers know it.

EU leaders discussed housing for the first time in history. [2] They are now looking at solutions to the housing crisis. [3]

We are a part of a movement putting affordable housing at the top of the EU agenda. Together, we refuse to accept a system that puts profit before people. [4]  

As our leaders look at solutions, now is the time to speak up. We can still change the course, if we act now. Let’s make it impossible for leaders to ignore us: our right to housing is not for sale.

2025-11-restore-multi-entry-visas-judge-.title: Restore Multi-Entry Visas – Judge by Individual Risk, Not by Passport
2025-11-restore-multi-entry-visas-judge-.description_full:
Restore Multi-Entry Visas – Judge by Individual Risk, Not by Passport

The European Commission, the Council of the European Union, the European Parliament and the governments of Schengen Area states

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Restore a targeted approach: allow multi-entry visas for applicants with a clean travel record and transparent histories, regardless of the place of application; strengthen risk-based screening rather than passport-based exclusions.

Create a fast-track humanitarian and family corridor for journalists, human rights defenders, scholars, students, and close relatives – with clear criteria and timelines.

Introduce a mandatory 12-month review with a published impact assessment balancing security and societal/foreign-policy effects.

Ensure uniform application of the rules by all consulates to avoid arbitrariness and a “visa lottery.”

 

Why is this important?

We are Russians living in Europe who oppose the war.

We ask you to revisit the European Commission’s implementing decision of 6 November 2025, which effectively halts multi-entry visas for most applicants from Russia (with narrow exceptions for close family members and transport workers, and case-by-case consideration for dissidents, independent journalists, and human rights defenders). This policy is misguided and counterproductive.

Why this harms rather than helps

It hits regime opponents the hardest. Students, researchers, cultural professionals, and families who choose Europe are the ones most affected. The Kremlin exploits this as “proof” of Western hostility.

It weakens the EU’s soft power. People-to-people ties change minds better than symbolic restrictions. Cutting these ties reduces the EU’s influence inside Russia.

It brings little security gain. The EU already has tools for precise filtering – biometrics, PNR/API data, interviews, and risk profiling. Blanket limits are costly and blunt.

It hurts EU families and the EU economy. Mixed families, universities, tourism and creative SMEs bear direct costs without clear security benefits.

It politically helps the Kremlin. Passport-based collective treatment strengthens the “besieged fortress” narrative.

Petition

We citizens demand the inclusion of our proposals in the revision of Directive 2014/40/EU making it mandatory for tobacco manufacturers

To organize and finance the collection and recycling of cigarette butts throughout the EU

To create recycling chains to support the circular economy: transformation into street furniture, insulation...

To write the following message on tobacco products: "The best cigarette is the one you don't smoke; Otherwise recycle your butt!"

To install cigarette butt collection terminals

Why is this important?

The revision of Directive 2014/40/EU on the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco products and related tobacco products is scheduled for 2026!

800 billion cigarette butts thrown away each year in Europe; it is the most polluting waste in the world

Tobacco manufacturers make €50 billion in annual profits but do not finance any recycling.

Cost for taxpayers: 1.5 billion euros for  cleaning. ADEME

1 butt = 500 liters of polluted water + takes between 12 and 15 years to degrade by releasing microplastics and pollutants

75% of Europeans are NON-SMOKERS and pay for the cleaning of a product they do not use!

The European Union has already banned straws and plastic bags; it's the turn of cigarette butts.

In California, an ecotax on cigarettes finances recycling: -40% of butts in 2 years

In France MéGo recycles butts into street furniture

2025-11-trial-deforestation-deregulation.description_full:
Save forests before it’s too late!

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

Scientists are warning we are almost out of time to save the global forests that remain. But there’s one law proposal that could turn this around: the European Union Deforestation Regulation.

Unfortunately, it has come under fierce attacks. Changes proposed by Member States and the European Parliament would open the door to greenwashing and destruction. What’s more, they’d lead to endless legal uncertainty and  a downward spiral of postponements and further weakening of the law.

Delaying and gutting the approval of this new directive comes at a cost. Let it come into force to protect the world’s forests.

Why is this important?

Forests are silent heroes. They tame violent storms, shield your city from floods, and quietly shrink your energy bills - even from far away. But we’re losing them.

There is a law that could hold to account big coffee, rubber, palm oil, and other industries accountable for destroying forests worldwide. This law is now under attack from Europe's leaders who want to put short term profits over forests.

But some European governments are trying to weaken the law. They’re putting short-term profits above forests - and our stable weather and bills. 

We have a chance. The European Commission’s president, von der Leyen, can reject the watered-down deal which sacrifices more forests. She can stand behind her original proposal. 

The Commission’s president cares about her reputation. A big mass of citizens’ support will give her the strength to reclaim control over her own proposal to save the forests - before she makes a move.

The people’s movement for forests has called on our community to urgently join them. Our demand to Ursula von der Leyen is to stand as a brave leader in defense of nature. The more support she gets from the people, the more chances a genuinely strong law will pass.

But some European governments are trying to weaken the law. They’re putting short-term profits above forests - and our stable weather and bills. 

We have a chance. The European Commission’s president, von der Leyen, can reject the watered-down deal which sacrifices more forests. She can stand behind her original proposal. 

The Commission’s president cares about her reputation. A big mass of citizens’ support will give her the strength to reclaim control over her own proposal to save the forests - before she makes a move.

The people’s movement for forests has called on our community to urgently join them. Our demand to Ursula von der Leyen is to stand as a brave leader in defense of nature. The more support she gets from the people, the more chances a genuinely strong law will pass.

To Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, Olivér Várhelyi, European Commissioner for Health and Animal Welfare, Ilze Juhansone, Secretary-General of the European Commission, Sandra Gallina, Directorate-General for Health & Food Safety (DG SANTE)

  • Reject any plan or proposal to allow unlimited or permanent chemical approvals.
  • Protect the requirement that companies must prove their chemicals and pesticides are safe.
  • Defend the precautionary principle and independent scientific assessment.

For a decade, we’ve been fighting to keep glyphosate and pesticides off our plates.

Now the EU could undo it all, letting these toxic chemicals into our food forever. 

Greedy companies like Bayer-Monsanto and others are pushing hard for exactly this outcome. Unless we act fast, they will win.

We learned about this plan before the Commission made it public, and that gives us a rare chance. [1] If we show a massive public backlash before the proposal is even published, they will think twice about putting it forward at all.

2025-11-trial-pensions-petition-EN.description_full:
Fair Pensions Now!

To the European Commission and the European heads of state and governments

Petition

The European Union and national governments must commit to

  • End pension poverty.
  • Protect pension rights from budget cuts.
  • Guarantee a dignified retirement for all Europeans.

We are specifically demanding the European Commission to ensure that

  • “Everyone in old age has the right to resources that ensure living in dignity”, as agreed to in the Pillar of Social Rights.
  • EU budget rules and funding conditions never force governments to cut pension spending or raise retirement ages.

Why is this important?

After a lifetime of work, people deserve rest and security. Not punishment and fear.

But the message from those in power couldn’t be clearer: Work longer. Earn less. Expect nothing. [1]

Across Europe, pensions are under attack. Governments are being pushed to cut benefits and raise the retirement age, to meet demands from Brussels. [2] 

That’s why we’re launching Fair Pensions Now — a new Europe-wide campaign demanding that the EU and national governments:

  • End pension poverty,
  • Protect pensions from budget cuts,
  • Guarantee a dignified retirement for everyone.


Europe has promised us that “everyone in old age has the right to resources that ensure living in dignity.” [3] Now we’re holding them to that promise.

From France to Italy to Spain — millions are taking the streets demanding fair pensions. Whether that’s a stop to raising the retirement age or minimum pensions that prevent poverty. [4]

Now it’s time to unite these voices and make them impossible to ignore. Because the Europe we believe in treats its elders with care. 

Will you join us?

2025-11-trial-silence-on-sudan-petition-.description_full:
Europe must act to stop Sudan’s genocide

To Kaja Kallas, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy

Petition

We call on the European Commission to:

  • Suspend trade discussions with the UAE until it ends support for the Rapid Support Forces.
  • Increase humanitarian aid and access to Sudan and neighboring countries.
  • Propose a strengthened EU sanctions package under the EU Global Human Rights. Sanctions Regime, including financial sanctions, travel bans, and asset freezes.

Why is this important?

In Sudan, a genocidal war has killed more than 150,000 people. And now satellite images show something unimaginable— blood from mass killings visible from space [1]. 

Yet, the EU is pressing ahead with trade talks with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), even as credible evidence shows that the UAE is backing one side of the brutal conflict. [2,3]

You can’t claim to stand for human rights while doing business with governments who bankroll massacres. We’ve seen this before. Gaza has shown us what happens when Europe turns a blind eye. 

A new ceasefire in Sudan has been announced, and this is the moment when strong EU pressure could help push for a lasting peace. But right now, EU leaders ignore Sudan because it isn't making headline news, and that silence protects those in power.  

Together, we can break that silence. By raising our voices now, we drag this crisis onto their desks and force Europe to live up to its own values — not reward regimes that bankroll mass violence.

Add your name to demand that the EU suspends trade talks with the UAE now and take action for peace in Sudan.

2025-12-eu-budget-2028-2034-allocate-ded.title: Explicitly Include Roma in the EU Budget 2028–2034
2025-12-eu-budget-2028-2034-allocate-ded.description_full:
Explicitly Include Roma in the EU Budget 2028–2034

The European Commission – in particular the Commissioner for Budget and Administration and DG Budget (DG BUDG)

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Allocate dedicated and ring-fenced funding within the EU Budget 2028–2034 specifically for Roma communities, with mechanisms that allow direct access for Roma-led civil society organisations.

This should include:
• clear budget lines for inclusive education, desegregation and social inclusion;
• simplified and accessible funding mechanisms for Roma-led and community-based organisations;
• strong anti-discrimination and anti-segregation conditionalities attached to EU funds;
• transparent monitoring and accountability to ensure funds reach Roma communities and deliver real impact.

Why is this important?

The European Union is currently shaping its long-term budget for 2028–2034, a decision that will set funding priorities for the next decade. This is a critical moment to ensure that EU commitments to equality, inclusion and human rights are translated into concrete financial action.

Despite existing EU strategies on Roma inclusion, Roma communities across Europe continue to face persistent school segregation, poverty, discrimination and exclusion. Too often, EU funds do not reach Roma communities directly, and Roma-led organisations are excluded from meaningful access to funding and decision-making.

Without dedicated, ring-fenced funding and direct access mechanisms in the next EU budget, these structural inequalities will continue. This petition calls on the EU to act now and ensure that the 2028–2034 budget delivers real, measurable change for Roma communities through inclusive education, desegregation and social inclusion.

Say No to Mass Deportations in Europe

To the European Council, the Council of the European Union, the European Parliament and the European Commission

Petition

All of us want to live in safety and contribute to the community we are from. 

The European Commission’s new Deportation Regulation would tear families apart, expand detention, and turn migration into a business for private security and surveillance companies.

We call on the EU to choose care, dignity, and humanity - not fear and profit.

We urge you to:

  • Reject the Deportation Regulation in its current form;
  • Stop outsourcing migration control to private corporations and third countries;
  • Invest in protection, inclusion, and safe pathways for people on the move.

Europe must stand for human rights, not human suffering.

Why is this important?

Millions of us are watching the scenes from the United States: agents dragging people out of their homes at dawn, tearing families apart on the street while neighbours freeze in shock. [1]

An entire country waking up to the sound of knocking - the kind that makes your stomach drop.

Now imagine that on your own street. This is the path Europe is preparing to take.

In 5 days, EU leaders will meet to sign off on the next phase of a plan lifted straight from Trump’s hardline agenda. A plan that would make it easier for governments to raid people’s homes, search their belongings and deport them to countries they’ve never set foot in. [2]

Our politicians are pushing this fast. Hoping we stay quiet while they expand their power and blame newcomers for problems they refuse to solve.

But they’ve miscalculated.

Because this is exactly the moment when people like us step in - loudly. And when we do, they have no choice but to listen. 

We can stop this. But only if we act now.

Stop Europe from adopting Trump-style raids and deportations: add your name!

2025-12-protect-digital-creativity-suppo.description_full:
Protect Digital Creativity: Support Safe, Community-Driven Multiplayer Mods in Europe

Tech leaders and descion maker

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We, the undersigned, call on European digital authorities, online rights organizations, and gaming policy advocates to recognize and support the growing community of players who use safe, community-developed game modifications—such as private multiplayer servers and fan-made updates—to enhance creativity, learning, and social connection.

Across Europe, millions of young players rely on community creations like Null’s Brawl, custom maps, private servers, and educational modding tools to learn strategy, teamwork, coding basics, and digital skills. These platforms have become modern creative playgrounds, offering a safe, non-commercial space where players can experiment, test ideas, and grow.

However, community gaming projects are often misunderstood or unfairly restricted, despite being harmless, non-profit, and essential for digital innovation. Instead of punishing or suppressing these spaces, Europe should encourage responsible modding communities that respect user safety, data protection, and creativity.

We urge European regulators and digital rights advocates to:
• Acknowledge community-driven modding as a legitimate form of digital expression.
• Promote guidelines that protect players while supporting creativity.
• Encourage fair and transparent policies for private servers used purely for learning and entertainment.
• Create publicly accessible resources for safe modding to help young creators develop digital literacy.

This petition stands for a future where European youth can learn, create, collaborate, and express themselves without unnecessary barriers. Gaming culture is evolving—our policies should evolve with it.

We ask you to support safe, innovative, community-driven digital spaces that help millions of players unlock their creativity. https://null-brawl.io/

Why is this important?

Europe is entering a new era of digital transformation. Young people are no longer just playing games—they are designing, modifying, and experimenting with them to develop real-world digital skills. Creative modding communities like those around Null’s Brawl inspire imagination, teamwork, and problem-solving, contributing to digital literacy and future tech talent.

Unfortunately, the lack of clear policy tends to push these communities into uncertain territory. Without recognition or support, young creators risk losing accessible digital learning opportunities. At the same time, policymakers risk overlooking a massive opportunity to empower youth creativity.

This petition is important because:

• It protects safe digital learning spaces.
Kids and teens use modding to learn coding, logic, design, and testing—all crucial digital-era skills.

• It supports Europe’s digital future.
Tomorrow’s developers, cybersecurity experts, and creative designers often start by experimenting with game mods.

• It encourages safe, responsible community behavior.
With supportive guidelines instead of bans, policymakers can help shape healthier online spaces.

• It prevents over-regulation that harms creativity.
Not all mods or private servers are harmful. Many are non-profit, educational, and made purely for entertainment.

• It uplifts millions of young European gamers.
Players deserve fair treatment and the right to explore their creativity in safe, supportive environments.

By supporting this petition, you are supporting digital freedom, innovation, and the next generation of European creators.

2025-12-save-the-wilija-neris-river-and-.title: Save the Wilija–Neris River and the Wild Baltic Salmon: Stop Nuclear Risks and Military Ecological Destruction
2025-12-save-the-wilija-neris-river-and-.description_full:
Save the Wilija–Neris River and the Wild Baltic Salmon: Stop Nuclear Risks and Military Ecological Destruction

To the European Commission (Directorates-General for Environment; Energy; European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations) To the European Parliament (Committee on Environment, Public Health and Food Safety – ENVI) To the Espoo Convention Implementation Committee To the Bern Convention Standing Committee To the HELCOM (Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission) To the UNESCO (given potential Outstanding Universal Value of the ecosystem) To the Government of Belarus To the Government of Lithuania

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We call for immediate action to:

• permanently halt all river-engineering, dredging and navigation-related works on the Neris, especially within Natura 2000 sites
• establish full international oversight and transparency at the Astravets nuclear facility, including an Independent International Expert Group to safeguard the Wild Baltic Salmon migration corridor
• permanently prohibit the siting of any radioactive-waste storage or disposal facilities within the Wilija–Neris river basin

Why is this important?

The Wilija–Neris is one of the last largely intact river ecosystems in the Baltic region — a vital migration corridor for Wild Baltic Salmon and a lifeline for protected Natura 2000 habitats. Yet this living river is increasingly exposed to overlapping nuclear, ecological and infrastructural risks.

The Astravets nuclear plant — already associated with repeated safety incidents — uses the river system for cooling and process water. At the same time, the Astravets district is being prioritised as a potential site for deep radioactive-waste disposal within the same catchment. Any contamination would move downstream into Lithuania and the Baltic Sea — one of the most environmentally stressed seas on Earth.

In parallel, publicly discussed plans in Lithuania would convert the Neris into heavy-duty transport infrastructure, including proposals for dredging and river-engineering works — even within Natura 2000 areas. Such interventions would destroy spawning grounds, damage river morphology and sever one of the last functioning salmon migration routes in the Baltic basin.

This is not a domestic matter. It is a transboundary risk affecting ecosystems, biodiversity, communities and the Baltic Sea as a whole. A living river must not be sacrificed to nuclear hazards or military-driven ecological destruction.

2025-12-support-survivors-of-sexual-viol.title: Support Survivors of Sexual Violence During the Kosovo War and Break the Silence
2025-12-support-survivors-of-sexual-viol.description_full:
Support Survivors of Sexual Violence During the Kosovo War and Break the Silence

We call on the Government of Kosovo, local institutions, international partners, universities, and civil society organizations.

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Support survivors of wartime sexual violence in Kosovo by demanding stronger recognition, justice, and long-term psychosocial, legal, and economic support, and by backing universities like AAB College that create safe spaces for truth, research, and advocacy.

https://aab-edu.net/en/aab-college-voices-breaking-the-silence-roundtable/

Why This Petition Matters

Sexual violence during armed conflict is a grave violation of human rights and human dignity. Thousands of women, men, and children were subjected to sexual violence during the Kosovo conflict, yet too many survivors still live with stigma, silence, poverty, and trauma, often without the justice, recognition, and long-term support they deserve.

Today, survivors of conflict-related sexual violence in Kosovo continue to face social exclusion, economic hardship, and barriers in accessing specialized health, psychosocial, and legal services. Many have waited decades for public acknowledgement, reparations, and a system that fully recognizes their rights and protects them from discrimination and secondary victimization.

Survivors of wartime sexual violence are not only victims of the past, they are members of our communities who need ongoing solidarity, protection, and opportunities to rebuild their lives. Breaking the silence around sexual violence in conflict is essential to preventing denial, combating stigma, and ensuring that such crimes are never repeated.

AAB College: A Leader in Survivor Support and Education

AAB College (https://aab-edu.net) is one of the leading higher education institutions in Kosovo and has committed to opening its doors as a space of dialogue, research, and support for survivors. Through initiatives such as the "Voices Breaking the Silence" roundtable
https://aab-edu.net/en/aab-college-voices-breaking-the-silence-roundtable/
organized within the global 16 Days of Activism Against Violence campaign, AAB College brings together survivors, students, experts, and civil society to listen to testimonies, promote dignity, and strengthen institutional responsibility.

By supporting this petition, you amplify the voices of survivors and support the role of universities, human rights organizations, and institutions that work to transform pain into action, policy, and education.

Don’t let Big Tech lobbyists exploit our data!

To the European Commission, the Irish Government, and the Irish Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration

Petition

We call on the European Commission to ensure 

  • The impartiality and independence of all national Data Protection Authorities.
  • Especially the impartiality and independence of the Data Protection Commission in Ireland, responsible to enforce Europe’s GDPR rules on tech companies operating all over Europe from Ireland. 

We also call on Ireland to ensure the independence of their data supervisory body by

  • Re-hiring a new Commissioner to the Irish Data Protection Commission with a track-record of protecting citizen rights and fundamental freedoms, and data protection in particular.
  • Doing an independent review of the hiring process by which the current appointment was made.

Why is this important?

Ireland has appointed an ex-Facebook lobbyist as its new data chief - the person meant to keep Big Tech in check. [1]

Ireland is home to all the Big Tech companies. They chose it because of low taxes. And because regulators there have looked the other way for years.

Now, the government has dropped all pretense, and put a Facebook insider in charge of policing Big Tech. Policing their former bosses.

What happens in Ireland affects us all. If Europe’s privacy laws don’t apply to Big Tech in Ireland, they don’t protect anyone, anywhere in Europe.

Digital rights groups have raised the alarm, but the government hopes it will disappear. [2]

Enough of us need to speak up and make them appoint someone who actually defends our rights, not corporate profits.

They have their backroom deals. We have people power. Every signature adds to the growing outcry. Together we can force the EU to call on Ireland to reverse course.

Add your name now to demand real data protection in Ireland — and all of Europe.
