Keep the Baltic Sea clean and safe!

To the Ministry of Climate and Environment of Poland, the Helsinki Commission (HELCOM), the European Commission, Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (Germany), the Ministry of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern (Germany) and the Secretariat of the Espoo Convention (Convention on Environmental Impact Assessment in a Transboundary Context)

Petition

We call on you to undertake urgent actions to:

  • Stop the plans for oil and gas extraction in the Oder Estuary and the Pomeranian Bay, which would violate climate and environmental regulations and goals;
  • Ban any new oil and gas extraction across the Baltic Sea, preventing deterioration and ensuring protection of the Baltic marine ecosystem;
  • Ensure strong cross-border cooperation and communication among all involved states, including the sharing of environmental impact assessments and timely notifications of planned consultations or other measures.

Why is this important?

Shocking plans just came to light: drilling for oil and gas in the Baltic Sea on the edge of a protected bird sanctuary in Poland. [1] Imagine holiday beaches shadowed by drilling rigs, seas filled with toxic leaks, and porpoises silenced by constant underwater noise. It’s an immediate danger to nature, our climate and the livelihoods of people who depend on tourism and a clean Baltic sea.

Scientists are clear: if we want to slow down global warming, no new oil or gas fields can be developed. [2] Yet the Polish government risks locking us all into decades more of fossil fuel dependence, while breaking EU nature protection rules and climate goals. [3] 

We can force decision-makers in Warsaw and Brussels to stop the drilling plans off the Polish coast and ban all oil and gas extraction in the Baltic Sea. If we flood them with signatures and community voices just before that meeting, they’ll be forced to respond.

Every signature is proof that people across Europe refuse to let short-term profits destroy our seas and our future. Add your voice to a growing European movement calling for a rig-free, safe Baltic!

References:

  1. https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7786/artykul/3554241,central-european-petroleum-confirms-major-oil-discovery-off-baltic-coast  
  2. https://www.iea.org/reports/net-zero-by-2050
  3. Such projects contradict the purpose of EU NATURA 2000 protected areas and would breach several EU and international commitments, including the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, the Birds Directive, the Habitats Directive, the Helsinki Convention and its Baltic Sea Action Plan (BSAP) as well as climate goals. 
  4. https://www.oceanweek.eu/

2025-12-translation-test-plastic-era-pet.description_full:

End the Plastic Era!

To the Commissioner for Environment, Water Resilience, and a Competitive Circular Economy, Jessika Roswall, and the Chair of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) on Plastic Pollution, Ambassador Luis Vayas Valdivieso.

Petition

We demand that the EU and the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC) on Plastic Pollution hold the line and push for a rapid, transparent and strong text for the Global Plastics Treaty — one that includes:

  • Binding caps on virgin plastic production worldwide.
  • Mandatory global targets — not voluntary pledges.
  • Regulation of the full lifecycle of plastics, from design to disposal.
  • A ban on harmful single-use plastics with clear phase-out deadlines.
  • Strict controls and phase-outs for toxic chemical additives in plastics.
  • Fair support for Global South countries through funding and technology transfer.


To achieve this goal, we urge the INC to move beyond unanimity and adopt a two-thirds majority voting system that ensures progress.

Why is this important?

Every year, 21 million tonnes of plastic waste leak into the environment — enough to cover every single beach in the world with a thick layer of trash — poisoning soils, oceans, and every living being. Scientists have found microplastics in our lungs, brains, and even placentas. [1]

In 2022, world leaders proposed a Global Plastics Treaty to stop plastic from further suffocating our planet. It was meant to be one of the most ambitious environmental deals in history, forcing polluters to take responsibility, and finally breaking Big Plastic’s grip on our future. [2]

But just two weeks ago, negotiations in Geneva collapsed. [3] Why? Because it required unanimous approval from more than 180 countries. Even just one plastic-polluting country can block the entire world from acting. 

It doesn’t have to be this way. The EU, backed by more than 100 countries, has voiced its frustration and wants this deal to move forward. [4] The only solution is to ditch the broken unanimity rule and move to majority voting. If two-thirds of countries want to save the planet from plastic, the negotiations can move forward.

Right now, leaders are considering this proposal after the last disappointing summit. Now is our moment to push for change. A powerful wave of public pressure can help world leaders move to majority voting and secure a strong Global Plastics Treaty.

Will you add your name to help seal the deal?

2025-12-trial-deportation-ICE-trial-INT-.description_full:
Say No to Mass Deportations in Europe

The European Council and Council of the European Union

Petition

All of us want to live in safety and contribute to the community we are from. 

The European Commission’s new Deportation Regulation would tear families apart, expand detention, and turn migration into a business for private security and surveillance companies.

We call on the EU to choose care, dignity, and humanity - not fear and profit.

We urge you to:

  • Reject the Deportation Regulation in its current form;
  • Stop outsourcing migration control to private corporations and third countries;
  • Invest in protection, inclusion, and safe pathways for people on the move.

Europe must stand for human rights, not human suffering.

Why is this important?

Millions of us are watching the scenes from the United States: agents dragging people out of their homes at dawn, tearing families apart on the street while neighbours freeze in shock. [1]

An entire country waking up to the sound of knocking - the kind that makes your stomach drop.

Now imagine that on your own street. Because this is the path Europe is preparing to take.

In two weeks, our EU representatives will meet to advance a plan lifted straight from Trump’s hardline agenda. A plan that could let governments deport people to countries they’ve never set foot in, and lock them away in distant detention camps. [2]

Some politicians are pushing this fast, hoping the public stays quiet while they expand their power and blame newcomers for problems they refuse to solve.

But they’ve miscalculated.

Because this is exactly the moment when people like us step in - loudly. And when we do, they have no choice but to listen. 

We can stop this. But only if we act now.

Add your name and help stop Europe from adopting Trump’s anti-immigration agenda!

A Europe where everyone belongs

The European Council and Council of the European Union

Petition

All of us want to live in safety and contribute to the community we are from. 

The European Commission’s new Deportation Regulation would tear families apart, expand detention, and turn migration into a business for private security and surveillance companies.

We call on the EU to choose care, dignity, and humanity - not fear and profit.

We urge you to:

  • Reject the Deportation Regulation in its current form;
  • Stop outsourcing migration control to private corporations and third countries;
  • Invest in protection, inclusion, and safe pathways for people on the move.

Europe must stand for human rights, not human suffering.

Why is this important?

Freddie Mercury is shining again on a giant London billboard with one blazing message: Thank God for immigrants. [1]

It’s a reminder that migration built the Europe we love - our nurses and doctors, our teachers and artists, our neighbours and friends.

And Spain is proving this every single day. 

Right now, Spain is the fastest-growing major economy in the EU. And one of the reasons is because it’s chosen policies that try to make it easier for people moving to Spain to work, study and build a future together. [2]

But instead of learning from this success, the EU is heading in the opposite direction - pushing a new Deportation law inspired by the harsh, raid-driven model we see in Trump’s America. [3]

A model built on sending people to countries they’ve never known, expanding offshore detention camps, and encouraging racial profiling in our streets. [4]

And they’re trying to push it through quietly to avoid public attention - the vote is in just two weeks.

But they’ve miscalculated. When people speak up together, loudly, plans like these crumble. 

Let’s defend the Europe we’re building every day - a Europe where families stay together and communities grow stronger. Sign the petition to stop this law!

Energy drinks: the hidden danger

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call for robust, binding EU-level action built on two main pillars: 

  • Ban the sale of energy drinks to under-18s throughout the EU 
  • Ban advertising and promotion of energy drinks to minors

Why is this important?

Heart failure. Seizures. Sleep disorders. Energy drinks have been linked to all these serious health conditions and, in some cases, death. [1]

So why do millions in Europe, including two thirds of teenagers and one in every five children, consume them? [2]

Because the companies making billions off them use enchanting words like ‘guarana’ to conceal the reality. They commission influencers to attract people to their addictive products. And they fight hard against any regulation. 

Leaders have finally turned their attention to these fatal beverages. [4] The Commission just published a new health plan, and politicians are considering new rules, like ensuring these drinks are out of reach for teenagers. But the companies are preparing to step up their fight.

It took people power to get us to this point - where leaders are taking these fatal drinks seriously. But as companies pour millions to pump their propaganda, we need to rise in the thousands to challenge them. 

Every signature is a voice calling out companies who put profit before people. Take action in just a few seconds!

2025-12-trial-omnibus-PFAs-petition-EN.title: Ban Forever Chemicals Now
2025-12-trial-omnibus-PFAs-petition-EN.description_full:
Ban Forever Chemicals Now

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

To the European Commission:

We call on you to protect people’s health by strengthening, not weakening, Europe’s rules on toxic “forever chemicals.”

Right now, you are considering changes that risk rolling back essential protections against PFAS contamination. We urge you to reject any proposal that delays or dilutes the planned phase-out of PFAS — and instead put forward the strongest possible restrictions, including on industrial uses that account for the majority of PFAS pollution.

Across Europe, governments are already showing that ambitious action is possible. France is phasing PFAS out of cosmetics, textiles and consumer products. Denmark has banned PFAS in food packaging, firefighting foam and pesticides. Sweden recognises high PFAS levels in blood as personal injury. Europe should match — and exceed — this level of protection.

Every delay means more toxic chemicals entering our water, our food, and our bodies — contamination that can last for generations.

We urge you to act now and deliver a PFAS ban that puts people’s health above industry profit.

Why is this important?

Nothing lasts forever, except for toxic man-made PFAS chemicals.

Everyday we’re exposed to these ‘forever chemicals’: in food packaging, frying pans, raincoats, and the list goes on. No wonder 98% of Europeans have toxic chemicals in their blood. [1]

They weaken our immune systems, disrupt hormones, and are linked to cancer. [2] Entire communities across Europe can’t even drink from the tap because contamination is so high. [3]

But here’s the good news: we finally have a real chance to ban them across Europe — pressure from countries like France, Denmark and Sweden has opened the door for a historic ban. [4]

But chemical lobbyists like 3M, DuPont and Bayer-Monsanto are fighting back hard: they’ve spent over €100 million lobbying the EU to gut or weaken any proposal. [5]

Now we need to stand with the countries fighting for this ban, and make sure our voice is louder than the corporations trying to erase it.

Let’s show EU leaders that people across Europe will not tolerate toxic forever chemicals in our bodies, our water, and our future.

2025-12-trial-pensions-eu-budget-petitio.title: Fair Pensions Now!
2025-12-trial-pensions-eu-budget-petitio.description_full:
Fair Pensions Now!

To the European Commission and national governments of Europe

Petition

The European Union and national governments must commit to

  • end pension poverty
  • guarantee a dignified retirement for all Europeans
  • ensure gender equality by maintaining the right to survivors’ pensions at adequate levels

 We are specifically demanding the European Commission to

  • come up with a binding directive setting a framework for minimum income, so that “everyone in old age has the right to resources that ensure living in dignity” as agreed to in the Pillar of Social Rights
  • never force governments to cut pension spending or raise retirement ages via EU budget rules 

Why is this important?

How do you feel about growing older these days? For so many people across Europe it feels less like planning for the future and more like bracing for it. 

Wondering whether our savings will stretch far enough to afford a decent quality of life. 

Thousands just went on strike in Belgium against austerity and rising pension ages. [1] From France to Italy to Spain, millions already took the streets demanding fair pensions. [2]

While people worry about their future, leaders fall back on their favourite line: tighten your belts. [3] 

Now the EU wants to push governments to cut pensions to save money. [4]

And here’s the critical moment: EU officials are finalising these budget rules right now. Public pressure can decide whether pensions are protected – or pushed closer to the chopping block.

Let’s ensure that no generation – young or old – has to cut its pension or delay retirement. 

So, will you add your voice so Europe scraps these plans?

Fair Pensions Now!

To national governments of Europe and the European Commission

Petition

The European Union and national governments must commit to

  • end pension poverty
  • guarantee a dignified retirement for all Europeans
  • ensure gender equality by maintaining the right to survivors’ pensions at adequate levels

We are specifically demanding the European Commission to

  • come up with a binding directive setting a framework for minimum income, so that “everyone in old age has the right to resources that ensure living in dignity” as agreed to in the Pillar of Social Rights
  • never force governments to cut pension spending or raise retirement ages through EU budget rules

Why is this important?

How do you feel about growing older these days? For so many people across Europe it feels less like planning for the future and more like bracing for it. 

Wondering whether our savings will stretch far enough to afford a decent quality of life. 

Just last week, thousands went on strike in Belgium against austerity and pension cuts. [1] From France to Italy to Spain, millions already took the streets demanding fair pensions. [2]

While people worry about their future, leaders fall back on their favourite line: tighten your belts. 

Across the EU, national leaders are taking steps that could leave people working longer for less. [3]

We see that governments back off when the political cost gets too high. [4] A wave of public pressure can close that window fast.

Let’s ensure that no generation – young or old – has to cut its pension or delay retirement. 

So, will you add your voice to protect our pensions?

A multi-millionaire oil-refining company is fighting hard to avoid paying its fair share.

If they paid the tax they owe, that money would go into lowering our households’ energy costs.  How can a company avoid the law? It’s easy: 

There are courts - invisible to most of us - that rule in favour of corporations. The company simply demands they be let off their duties, and a private lawyer grants their wishes. All behind closed doors. 

But across Europe people are waking up to this secret. 

We know that if enough of us learn about this, and take action, we can win. We’ve done it before. Last year, we opposed a treaty that let corporations sue countries for taking climate action. And we won!

But some of the worst companies still exploit this loophole to get what they want. 

Let’s be the roar that brings this scandal to the news. If we expose these secret courts we can get rid of them for good!

Stop destroying our coast!

To Marc García-Durán Huet, project promoter, Rosa Dávila Mamely, president of the Tenerife Island Council, and to European authorities.

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We demand:

• Marc García-Durán Huet’s immediate abandonment of the Underwater Garden project.
• A public commitment from the Cabildo of Tenerife to not support massive tourism infrastructures disguised as sustainability.
• The prioritisation of real marine conservation measures and the expansion of marine reserves instead of tourism megaprojects.

Why is this important?

Presented as a “regenerative” space with underwater gardens and high-end entertainment activities, Underwater Garden is in fact a speculative megaproject in a protected area that will endanger the ecosystem, restrict free access to the sea, and negatively impact the lifestyle of the local community.

Why we say NO:

  • It is not regenerative: it is a luxury theme park that will bring speculation, overcrowding, and destruction.
  • Severe environmental impact: it will alter marine and coastal ecosystems, increase boat traffic, and affect vulnerable species.
  • It excludes the community: it effectively privatizes a space that has always been freely used by locals.
  • A threat to a unique wave: its infrastructure could change currents and ruin an iconic wave for surfers and biodiversity.
  • Gentrification: it will raise housing prices and displace the local population.
  • Lack of transparency: the promoter hides key information and greenwashes the project.
  • Dangerous precedent: it would open the door to more destructive megaprojects we’ve been fighting for years, like the now-forgotten Fonsalía port.

 

Instead of further destroying the coast and local lifestyle, there are sustainable and respectful alternatives for nature and island culture:

  • Protect the coast and seabed: expand reserves like the Special Conservation Zone (ZEC) Teno-Rasca and effectively protect existing ones.
  • Regenerate degraded coastal areas: restore natural spaces and conserve biodiversity without turning nature into a business.
  • Promote dignified local economies: support the primary sector and the blue economy, creating real jobs for the local population.

 

Tenerife doesn’t need more theme parks and greenwashing projects—it needs to protect its natural wealth.

Sign and join us to stop Underwater Garden! The island belongs to its people, not to multinationals.

Demand Immediate Inclusion of Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) in the Public Health Systems of all EU Member States!

To the Public Health - European Commission

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

What we ask

We urge the Public Health - European Commission to take immediate action to integrate Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) into the public healthcare systems of all EU member states. This essential step will ensure that every citizen has access to a comprehensive range of treatment options, promoting health equity and enhancing overall well-being across Europe.

Why is this important?

Integrating Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) with conventional medicine is crucial for several reasons. First and foremost, it addresses the diverse health needs of the European population, as many individuals seek already holistic approaches to their well-being. CAM has been shown to enhance health outcomes, offering additional options for those who may not find relief through conventional treatments alone.

 

Moreover, many individuals find CAM treatments prohibitively expensive, leaving them without the holistic care options they need. This financial barrier restricts access to very important therapies, further widening the gap in health equity across the region. With only Germany and Austria incorporating CAM into their public healthcare systems, citizens in other nations are deprived of essential treatment options. This inequity not only limits individual options but also undermines the fundamental right of all Europeans to receive comprehensive, effective healthcare assistance.

 

Furthermore, expanding CAM access and incorporating it into the Healthcare system can lead to better health outcomes, reduced healthcare costs in the long run, and a more resilient healthcare system. By advocating for CAM inclusion in public healthcare in the EU countries, we empower individuals to take charge of their health, ultimately fostering a healthier society. It is imperative that we rectify this situation to ensure that all EU state citizens have equal access to a full range of therapeutic options, promoting health equity and improving overall community well-being.

To the President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Dear Commission President von der Leyen,


the defense capability and the renovation of ailing infrastructures in Europe must only be moderately financed by debt. Ensure now that tax justice prevails throughout Europe by placing a heavier burden on the wealthy and companies that generate high profits.

Since the 1980s, companies and the wealthy around the world have benefited from the exploitation of infrastructure and the environment to an unprecedented extent. In return, their taxes have been cut and public goods such as healthcare, education, communications and transportation financed by citizens have been sold off for decades.

The enormous damage caused by this overexploitation is now catching up with us. To counteract this, high levels of debt are being planned across Europe. This is intended to finance the state welfare system, which was once taken for granted but is now crumbling, including protection against attacks that violate international law.

However, future generations are already facing the enormous task of combating climate change and must not be burdened any further. The high additional interest rates would severely restrict government budgets in their day-to-day tasks, for example in the social sector. Support for poor countries would also have to be reduced, which would force more people to flee. The necessary funds must therefore be raised through taxes.

The following taxes should be newly levied or adjusted according to income or turnover *), whereby the top tax rates (see below) must increase significantly:

  • Financial transaction tax of at least 1%
  • Stock exchange turnover tax
  • Corporation tax
  • Capital gains tax
  • wealth tax
  • Inheritance tax
  • Kerosene tax for all flights
  • Relocation and disentanglement tax of up to 100% **) depending on turnover/income for people and companies wishing to relocate their primary residence
  • CO2 tax based more on consumption than before
  • Levy corporate taxes in the country of turnover
  • Strict sanctions against tax havens up to Swift exclusion
  • Closing tax loopholes

These measures will generate so much revenue that many consumption taxes can be reduced for the benefit of all.

For orientation: After the Second World War, the top tax rate in the USA and the Federal Republic of Germany was up to 95% in order to finance reconstruction. Today's challenges, such as man-made climate change, are no less.

A top tax rate of 90% would mean that someone with a gross annual income of 6 million euros would have 50,000 euros net per month in future - more than enough for a comfortable life.

*) Income and turnover-oriented means taking into account appropriate allowances, for example for heirs who continue to run businesses, companies that build up reserves for employees or people who live in an inherited house themselves.

**) Expected profits make it possible to levy taxes of up to 100 %. Deferral plans can be drawn up if required.

Why is this important?

At this point in time, it is of course essential to get large financial packages off the ground quickly and to incur debt to do so. But this can only be a temporary solution:

Taking on new debt once again spares those who have profited from the tax and financial policies of recent decades. However, it is high time to call to account those who have amassed immeasurable wealth and to correct at least part of their overexploitation.Future generations will have to bear enormous costs to keep this planet habitable at all. It would be irresponsible to cover up today's failings with debt and pass this burden on to younger generations. At the same time, the further increase in interest payments by governments reduces their room for maneuver - and once again only the companies in the financial industry benefit.

2025-3-for-a-united-and-sovereign-europe.description_full:
For a United and Sovereign European Defense

To the European Commission, the European Parliament, and the Heads of State and Government of the European Union

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Russia's aggression against Ukraine together with questions about US support have shattered the illusion of peace in Europe. We, European citizens, demand that the European Union take decisive and coordinated action to ensure its security, sovereignty, and military independence: ONE army, ONE nuclear deterrence, ONE defense budget, ONE military industry.

We demand urgent action on these 4 priorities:

1️⃣ ONE EU army

Defense must become a EU competence under the European Commission (with decisions by qualified majority).

Develop an action plan for a European peacekeeping force in Ukraine (short term), an EU army based on NATO model able alone to deter Russia (5 years), and a fully integrated and autonomous European defense based on its most experienced army in Ukraine (10 years).

 

2️⃣ ONE EU nuclear deterrence 

Develop a shared European nuclear deterrent (based on the independant French nuclear capabilities) under the responsibility of the président of the commission.

Reform EU institutions so that the European Commission President is directly elected, ensuring democratic legitimacy for nuclear deterrence.

 

3️⃣ ONE EU defense budget 

Introduce an EU defense budget representing 5% of EU GDP within 5 years, consolidating all country defense budgets with the aim to improve efficiency of spending: it is shocking that EU countries spend together massively more than Russia in defense to end up with a weaker setup. Support budget increase with EU bonds available to individual citizens as well as institutions.

 

4️⃣ ONE EU military industry 

Build weapons and munitions factories with the first priority being to supply Ukraine. Invest both in high tech and mass production.

Streamline European military production by limiting key technologies to max two complementary European manufacturers to increase efficiency, covering all defense products and services.

Only provide EU defense aid for the purchase to these selected EU providers (except for urgent aid to Ukraine if required).

 

Why is this important?

Europe must act—NOW.

We call on the European Union and member states to adopt these urgent measures and to establish a clear, binding roadmap for a sovereign and unified European defense. We cannot afford to wait. Sign this petition and help us make Europe safer, together.

2025-3-for-an-independent-and-peaceful-e.description_full:
For an Independent and Peaceful Europe

To the European Commission, to the Presidents of European Nations and European Representatives

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The conflict in Ukraine represents a serious threat to the stability of our continent. 

We are convinced that a lasting solution can only be achieved through dialogue and diplomacy, not through military escalation, which risks having devastating consequences for all the peoples involved.

We call on our representatives and the European institutions to:

  • Ensure Ukraine's sovereignty over its resources: Fully support the Ukrainian people's right to maintain complete sovereignty over their natural and economic resources, protecting them from any form of external appropriation. 
  • Actively promote European mediation: Take a leading role in negotiations between Ukraine and Russia, offering the mediation of the European Union as an impartial third party, with the goal of achieving a lasting ceasefire and a diplomatic solution that respects international law. *
  • Develop constructive relations with Russia: Work towards the gradual normalization of economic and diplomatic relations between the European Union and Russia, in mutual respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all involved states, promoting a shared area of economic cooperation and security from the Atlantic to the Urals. 
  • Strengthen Europe's strategic autonomy: Develop a more independent European foreign and security policy, capable of defending the interests of European citizens without subordinating them to those of other global powers.

Why is this important?

Beyond the rearmament policy, which is an important deterrent considering today's challenges, we believe that war is never an option. Europe does not 'lose face' if it engages in civil dialogue with other parties; on the contrary, it would gain more reputation internally and externally.

We believe that only a more united, more autonomous Europe, actively engaged in peace, can guarantee a future of stability and prosperity for our continent. We are convinced that war is never in the interest of the people and that it is the duty of our representatives to always seek peaceful solutions to conflicts.

By signing this petition, we call on the European institutions to take these requests seriously and to act in the best interest of all European citizens and the fundamental values ​​of the European Union.

2025-3-mehr-steuergerechtigkeit-nicht-nu.description_full:
English

  • Deutsch

More tax justice – not just new debts!

To the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen To the President of the European Council, António Costa To the Members of the European Parliament

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

The defense capability and the renovation of ailing infrastructure in Germany should only be financed modestly through debt. Ensure now that tax justice prevails throughout Europe by placing a greater burden on the wealthy and on companies that make high profits.

Since the 1980s, companies and wealthy individuals worldwide have benefited to an unprecedented extent from the exploitation of infrastructure and the environment. To make this possible, taxes were reduced and, over decades, citizen-financed public goods such as health, education, communication and transportation were sold.

The enormous damage caused by this overexploitation is now catching up with us. To counteract this, high debts are being planned throughout Europe. These are to finance the once taken for granted, now crumbling state welfare, including protection against attacks in violation of international law. At this point in time, it is of course essential to get large financial packages off the ground quickly, and to incur debt to do so. But this can only be a temporary solution:

Future generations are already facing the enormous task of combating climate change and must not be burdened further. The high additional interest rates would severely restrict government budgets in their day-to-day tasks, for example in the social sector. Support for poor countries would also have to be reduced, which would force more people to flee. Therefore, the necessary funds must be refinanced through taxes.

In order to establish fair taxation in the medium term, the following taxes must be levied for the first time or adjusted in line with income or turnover:

  • Financial transaction tax of at least 1%
  • Stock exchange tax
  • Corporation tax
  • Capital gains tax
  • Wealth tax
  • Inheritance tax
  • Kerosene tax for all flights
  • Exodus and de-gambling tax up to 100% **) depending on turnover/income for people and companies that want to relocate their primary residence
  • More than previously consumption-based CO2 tax
  • Levying corporate taxes in the country of turnover
  • Strict sanctions against tax havens, up to and including Swift exclusion
  • Closing tax loopholes

These measures will generate such high revenues that many consumption taxes can be reduced for the benefit of all. Nevertheless, the state will collect significantly more than before.

By way of illustration: 

In Germany alone, a financial transaction tax, which currently does not even exist, would raise several hundred billion euros at a rate of 1%. 

After World War II, the top tax rate in the United States and the Federal Republic of Germany was as high as 95% to finance the reconstruction. Today's challenges, such as man-made climate change, are no less daunting. A top tax rate of 90% would mean that someone with a gross income of €6 million per year would in future receive a net monthly income of €50,000 – more than enough for a comfortable life.
 

*) Income and revenue-based means a proportional increase. The higher the income or revenue, the higher the percentage that has to be paid in tax – as is already the case with income tax today. Appropriate allowances must, of course, ensure that heirs continue to run family businesses, that companies set aside reserves for employees, or that people can live in an inherited house themselves.

**) Expected profits make it possible to levy taxes of up to 100%. If necessary, deferral plans could be drawn up.

Why is this important?

Once again, taking on new debt spares the profiteers of the tax and financial policy of recent decades. But it is high time to hold those who have accumulated immense wealth accountable and to at least partially correct their plundering. Future generations will have to bear enormous costs to keep this planet habitable at all. It would be irresponsible to conceal today's failures by incurring debts and passing this burden on to younger generations. At the same time, the ever-increasing interest payments by governments are reducing their room for maneuver – and once again the only companies to benefit are those in the financial industry.

I call on EU institutions and industry to support the symbolic gesture of chocolate Santas being sold this Christmas with a European blue wrapping with stars to show European unity and compassion.

Why is this important?

Today’s geopolitical situation requires the European Union to step up. Citizens demand it: in the latest Eurobarometer, 89% of respondents asked Europe to be more united [1]. However, “unity” is easy to preach but hard to practice, because:

  • There is no real “European” consciousness
  • The EU is terrible at marketing itself

 

Christmas would offer a great opportunity for showing some paneuropean unity. You don’t need to rewatch, “A Christmas Carol” [2] to know that the idea of Christmas is compassion and caring for your next-of-kin. In other words: to stand together, for one another, to be united.

Santa wearing red has become a global marketing phenomenon since Coca-Cola pushed it from 1931 onwards [3]. But with the US becoming “scrooge” in Charles Dicken’s sense, I believe we can send a strong symbol for the European Union, if chocolate Santas would no longer wear a “maga-red” but have a “European blue and stars” wrapping this Christmas.

France was once scolded with“freedom fries” [4]. On Christmas, the EU can pull even with Santas in European blue that:

  • Help build EU branding
  • Reclaim part of the christmas narrative for Europe
  • Allow you to participate with a sweet sign of protest

 

Help spread the word by signing and sharing the petition. The more, the “merrier” and the more likely we can convince chocolate manufacturers and retailers to support the idea. 

#sweeterTogether #EUSanta 🇪🇺🎅

2025-4-8-mart-dunya-emekci-kadinlar-gunu.title: Let 8 March International Working Women's Day be a day off with pay!
2025-4-8-mart-dunya-emekci-kadinlar-gunu.description_full:
English

  • Türkçe
  • Français
  • Deutsch

Let 8 March International Working Women's Day be a day off with pay!

European Parliament

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

8 March, International Working Women's Day, was won as a result of women's long-term struggles. This important day is an important day when women express their struggles against the male-dominated system, violence, war and all kinds of oppression and exploitation, and their demands for equality and rights.  However, this important day is not recognised as an official holiday in many countries and is not recognised as paid leave. We believe that this situation must change, because:

Recognition of Women's Rights: International Women's Day is a reminder of the struggle for women's rights. Declaring it as a paid holiday emphasises the importance of this struggle and sends a strong message to recognise the contributions of women in the social, economic and political spheres.

Ensuring Gender Equality: A paid holiday on Women's Day sends a strong message about gender equality. This further advances the debate on equality and increases public sensitisation to the inequalities faced by women. It gives voice to the struggle for rights against discrimination in the labour market, education and health.

Setting an example for future generations: A paid 8 March holiday is a powerful example to younger generations that gender equality is important not only in theory but also in practice. Women's rights and equality are recognised as fundamental values of our society and these values are passed on to future generations.

Unequal Wages: Women are still paid less than men for the same job in many European countries. The "Gender Pay Gap" is still a serious problem. Women are more likely to be in sectors that pay lower wages and do not have the same promotion opportunities as their male counterparts.

Gender Stereotypes and Roles: In many European societies there are still entrenched gender roles. These roles often relegate women to lower status jobs. They limit their personal and professional development. These stereotypes can even affect women's educational opportunities.

Violence against women: Violence against women is widespread in Europe. Domestic violence, sexual harassment, economic violence and all forms of violence... Despite legal protection measures and anti-violence initiatives, there are gaps in many countries in protecting women from such attacks. Women do not feel safe and often do not have access to the necessary support.

Women's Representation: Women are less likely than men to hold political, economic and scientific leadership positions. Although women have more university degrees in many countries, they rarely reach senior positions in large companies or political positions.

Access to reproductive health services and freedom of choice regarding pregnancy and family formation vary across Europe. In some countries abortion is still strictly regulated or prohibited. This limits women's freedom of decision-making and jeopardises their health.

Today, women are still forced to work in precarious and flexible jobs.  8 March should be a public holiday to make women's labour visible in the private and public spheres and to give labour its due.

The patriarchal system that condemns women to poverty, governments that ignore and condone domestic labour should declare 8 March a paid holiday to show their support for women's struggle for existence.

All countries that are signatories to the Council of Europe (Istanbul) convention should recognise 8 March as a paid holiday to show their opposition to all forms of violence against women, to eliminate the inequality created by gender roles and to demonstrate the inequality in society.

Making 8 March a paid holiday is not only a symbolic step but also an important step towards a more just and egalitarian society. This step must be taken to recognise the contribution of women in all areas of social life and to show that we value them.

Let 8 March International Working Women's Day be a day off with pay for equality and our acquired rights, for struggle and resistance!

Democratic Women's Movement in Europe(ADKH)

2025-4-do-not-deregulate-new-genomic-tec.title: Do not deregulate New Genomic Techniques (NGT) for wild plants!
2025-4-do-not-deregulate-new-genomic-tec.description_full:
Do not deregulate New Genomic Techniques (NGT) for wild plants!

To the Members of The European Parliament, the EU Commission, and EU Council

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We call on the European Commission, Parliament and Council to not allow the deregulation of New Genomic Techniques for wild plants. The discussion about unregulated use of NGT must be limited to agricultural applications.

A fast, efficient, and safe transition towards sustainable agriculture is needed. It must be based on sound scientific evidence. Therefore, agricultural diversification must be prioritized over NGTs for promoting the EU Green Deal.

Why is this important?

An estimated minimum of 300,000 [2] plant species exist on Earth, and many are endangered. With the new legislation for the deregulation of New Genomic Techniques (proposal by the Commission [1]), so-called NGT1 can be applied to all of them without prior assessment of risks or benefits. Wild NGT1 plants could be manipulated and planted into natural populations without justification, without risk assessment, without liability and possibly without labeling.

Manipulated wild plants set out into the wild compromise the genetic integrity of natural plant populations. Wild NGT plants will inevitably reproduce with their wild relatives with unpredictable and irreversible consequences: they may introduce maladaptations or spread aggressively with potentially detrimental consequences for natural communities.

At the same time, the Parliament proposes that: “(13a) NGT plants with the potential to persist, reproduce or spread in the environment, within or beyond fields, should be evaluated with the highest level of scrutiny in respect of such plants’ impact on nature and the environment.”

Allowing unregulated NGT applications in the wild is in direct contradiction with this goal. 

The most problematic applications with wild plants have been ignored in the current debate.

1) Application in research and DIY: Most plant scientists work with wild plants. Deregulating NGT1 for wild plants, will allow almost unrestricted field research with manipulated plants whose traits are subject to individual preferences and interests of researchers. 

2) Applications in nature conservation: National [e.g., 4] and international laws are in place demanding a sound risk assessment prior to release of novel genotypes into the wild, for example for conservation purposes. The proposed new regulations are at odds with these laws.

3) Many wild plants are used in agriculture. Many of their traits may be detrimental for a life beyond agricultural fields. An example: NGT poplars with reduced lignin content or altered flowering times would greatly reduce fitness of wild poplars – a common wild tree in Europe. 
 

The GFÖ- the largest scientific ecological society in Europe- maintains [4]:
- applications to all plants pose a serious risk for biodiversity protection
- the EU proposals lack ecological expertise
- a fast, efficient and safe path towards sustainable agriculture does not need technological promises such as NGT

Advocates of NGT for the Green Deal rely on many promises without sound scientific evidence, and major solutions for sustainable agriculture have been lost out of sight. Namely, myriads of scientific studies point towards a climate-resistant agriculture with largely reduced need for pesticides, herbicides, and fertilizer via diversification- of varieties within a field, crops among fields, or agricultural practices within and among farms [e.g., 5,6,]. Adopting such science-based solutions would enable the EU to spearhead a true agricultural revolution towards social and environmental sustainability. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

REFERENCES

1  European Commission 2023: 411 final 2023/0226 (COD) Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on plants obtained by certain new genomic techniques and their food and feed, and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/625. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX%3A52023PC0411

2 Mora C, et al. 2011: How many species are there on Earth and in the ocean? PLoS Biology 9: e1001127

3   §40 Abs. 2 Satz 3 BNatSchG (German Federal Law for Nature Conservation)

4  Expert Group “New Genomic Techniques”, Ecological Society of Germany, Austria and Switzerland (GFÖ) 2023: New genomic techniques from an ecological and environmental perspective: science-based contributions to the proposed regulations by the EU Commission. https://gfoe.org/sites/default/files/ngt_gfoe_final.pdf

5 He X et al. 2023 Agricultural diversification promotes sustainable and resilient global rice production. Nature Food 4: 788–796. https://doi.org/10.1038/s43016-023-00836-4

6 Rasmussen VL et al. 2024: Joint environmental and social benefits from diversified agriculture. Science 384: 87-93.  DOI: 10.1126/science.adj1914

English

Tribune - For a strong and united European Union closer to the territories

The European Parliament, the European Commission, the Council of the European Union, the governments of the EU Member States, Members of the European Parliament (MEPs), the Committee of the Regions (CoR), local elected officials, and parliamentarians from the Member States of the European Union, as well as public authorities in general

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We, therefore, put forward this message in several points, for a European Union that must uncompromisingly assert the principles and values that set it apart:

● The European Union is a project strongly supported by its inhabitants, elected representatives, associations and intermediary bodies.

● The European Union is the guardian of solidarity, built on the Charter of Fundamental Rights, which must also be able to protect its values, its democratic space and peace through a strengthened defence policy.

● The European Union is a source of inspiration beyond its borders

● The European Union must confirm its closeness to its Territories and European citizens

● The European Union has the duty to assert its ambition for a peaceful world which is fairer and more sustainable, by supporting territories in their ecological, energy and digital transitions and by supporting the dynamics of territorial development in all its components (social equity, rural development, agriculture and food, crafts and industry, culture, etc.).

Why is this important?

As local players from local authorities, the ecological transition, local democracy, the social economy and popular education, we are calling for firm and committed support for a strong European Union that is closer to the regions.

The unprecedented context in which the European Union finds itself, under attack from all sides (internally and externally), is a consequence of a confused and bellicose international situation, where obscurantism is gaining ground. Unfortunately, this objective observation compels us. It demands that we send a strong message to all European citizens, who are deeply attached to the democratic, social and societal values and principles that underpin the European project, enshrined in 1957 in the Treaty of Rome, and which guarantee our future.

Our Europe, based on social, economic and territorial cohesion, can certainly be improved, although it is also precious, indispensable and protective. The European collective is our energy, cooperation is our strength, pooling asserts our responsible power, and sharing values consolidates this will.

By means of this press release, we are sending a strong, responsible and demanding message to our European authorities and elected representatives: The territories and local players make up the European Union, the territories and local players support the European Union, the territories and local players must be supported by the European Union!

2025-4-the-us-is-not-a-safe-country-anym.title: The US Is Not a Safe Country anymore – End Its Safe Country Status Now!
2025-4-the-us-is-not-a-safe-country-anym.description_full:
The US Is Not a Safe Country anymore – End Its Safe Country Status Now!

EUAA (European Union Agency for Asylum)

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We urge the European Union and its Member States to immediately revoke the designation of the United States as a “safe country of origin.”

Why is this important?

1. Political Persecution and Legal Repression

In the United States, there have been systematic and legal measures taken to suppress political dissent and rights. For example, the reintroduction of the death penalty for certain offenses, particularly those affecting undocumented immigrants, has resulted in the criminalization of this group. These legal changes have severely impacted the lives of migrants, increasing the risk of arrests and harsh sentences. (Prism Reports)

2. Reversal of Marriage Equality

Despite the long-standing legality of same-sex marriage in the USA, recent judicial decisions and legislative actions have threatened the full recognition of these marriages. There have been instances where legally contracted same-sex marriages were not recognized by government institutions. (SF Chronicle)

3. Criminalization of Immigrants

The reintroduction of the death penalty, particularly for cases involving migrants without legal status, has exacerbated the criminalization of these populations. This impacts their living conditions and increases the risk of deportation, arrest, and harsh punishment. (Prism Reports)

4. Systematic Discrimination Against Minorities

Reports indicate systemic discrimination against Black, Latino, and other marginalized groups, which has contributed to increased violence and abuse by law enforcement. Concerns include racial profiling, police brutality, and biased treatment of non-white groups. (CBP.gov)

5. Voter Surveillance and Suppression

There are reports of surveillance and discrimination against voters, especially those of Hispanic origin. Several states have passed laws that disproportionately affect these communities, limiting their access to voting. One such law involves married women who may be disenfranchised due to name changes after marriage, as highlighted in an article by the San Antonio Express-News. (San Antonio Express-News)

6. Shift from Democracy to Autocracy

Recent developments in the United States have raised concerns about a potential shift from democratic governance to autocratic practices. Analysts point to actions such as unprecedented executive orders that alter the balance of power and undermine the separation of powers. For instance, President Donald Trump issued 46 executive orders within the first 30 days of his second term in January 2025, raising alarms about the centralization of power. This trend reflects a move towards authoritarian governance. The Economist Intelligence Unit downgraded the U.S. from a "full democracy" to a "flawed democracy" in its 2024 Democracy Index, citing political polarization, challenges to electoral integrity, and diminished public trust in democratic processes. Furthermore, the CIVICUS Monitor added the U.S. to its Watchlist in March 2025, signaling threats to civic freedoms under the Trump administration. (CIVICUS Monitor; Economist Intelligence Unit)

Moreover, Systemicpeace.org, a prominent research site on global political systems, has officially classified the U.S. as an "anocracy" due to its decreasing levels of political freedom and increasing centralization of power, signaling a clear trend toward autocracy. (Systemic Peace Index)

Conclusion

The issues outlined above demonstrate the complex challenges facing the United States, especially concerning the rights and protection of migrants, minorities, and political dissenters. The intersections between political persecution, legal repression, and discrimination create a dangerously hostile environment for these groups. It is therefore crucial that the European Union carefully reassess its classification of the United States as a safe country of origin. This reassessment should be based on a thorough analysis of the current political, legal, and social conditions in the U.S., particularly regarding how these developments affect vulnerable populations.

Call to Action

In light of the documented decline of democratic norms, the erosion of civil liberties, and the growing repression of marginalized communities in the United States, it is imperative that the European Union urgently re-evaluates the classification of the United States as a "safe country of origin." Continued designation under this status fails to reflect the current political and human rights realities on the ground.

The European Union is called upon to:

Initiate a formal review of the United States' democratic status and human rights record.

Suspend the designation of the U.S. as a safe country of origin until robust democratic safeguards and equal protections are reinstated.

Strengthen protections for asylum seekers, particularly those at risk due to political persecution, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, or immigration status.

Failure to act risks complicity in the denial of fundamental rights and protections to those fleeing repression. The responsibility to uphold international human rights standards demands immediate and decisive action.

2025-5-save-shqipville-cultural-house-EN.title: SAVE SHQIPVILLE CULTURAL HOUSE
2025-5-save-shqipville-cultural-house-EN.description_full:
SAVE SHQIPVILLE CULTURAL HOUSE

To Philippe Close, Mayor of Brussels, Collège des Bourgmestre et Echevins, to Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, to Roberta Metsola, President of the European Parliament, to the European Commission and national EU governments, European Parliament, Brussels Parlement, le Parlement de la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale, Vlaams Parlement, Federaal Parlement, Parlement Francophone Bruxellois, Parlement De la Communaute Française, International Press

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

ShqipVille (Maison Culturelle Belgo-Albanaise ASBL), a unique and beloved cultural centre in the heart of Brussels, is being forced to stop its activities, and we urgently need your support to prevent this from happening. 

• Sign and share the petition

• Speak out about the importance of protecting community spaces and heritage

• Share our story in your networks, organisations, and circles of influence

We need your voice. Your solidarity. Your support.

Let’s keep ShqipVille alive and its soul untouched. Let’s keep this dream beating.

Why is this important?

Currently housed in one of the oldest and most iconic buildings on Brussels’ Grand-Place, ShqipVille is more than a cultural centre: it is a living bridge between Albanian and Belgian identities and heritages, a space where music, literature, language, and shared stories bring people together. Here, diversity is not just a word: it is a way of life and a welcoming attitude celebrated and nurtured on a daily basis.

To all of you who have visited ShqipVille, or taken part in our activities, you already know this: ShqipVille is not just a cultural centre. It is a living, breathing dream led by the Albanian community in Belgium. It is a vibrant place in the heart of Europe, conceived and managed as a safe space, a welcoming harbour, and a symbol of shared belonging for everyone.

Born from the need of integration and inclusion, and built without political or financial backing, ShqipVille has flourished and in less than 3 years, it has quickly become a true home for art, dialogue, learning, and inclusion by welcoming residents, newcomers, the curious, and contributors from diverse backgrounds. Writers, musicians, painters, journalists, actors, civil society organisations, educators, artisans - from across the world – they’ve all found here their voice and their stage.

ShqipVille is a concrete bridge between cultures and a symbol of what Europe can become: a continent of genuine inclusion, diversity, and shared citizenship practices, built from the bottom up instead of the top down. Albania, as a candidate country to join the EU, needs places like this, community hubs where future citizenship is built together, every single day, through inclusive growth and civic participation.

Nowadays, we are the only civil society organisation in Brussels offering professionally structured, free courses specifically designed for adult foreign learners. This is not only education: it is empowerment, integration, and dignity in action.

ShqipVille has been built on two unshakable foundations:

No political affiliations - We welcome diverse views, stand against discrimination, and foster meaningful dialogue.

No shady money – Despite evident financial struggles, we have never accepted support from untrustworthy sources. We remain fully committed to upholding the values and practices of transparency and integrity.

Losing this space would mean losing more than a building. It would mean silencing voices, breaking connections, and stepping back from a genuinely inclusive, intercultural future.

European Commission and the European Parliament

2025-6-mandatory-transparency-for-produc.title: Mandatory Transparency for Products Made with Exploitation
2025-6-mandatory-transparency-for-produc.description_full:
Mandatory Transparency for Products Made with Exploitation

Ursula von der Leyen (President of the European Commission) Didier Reynders (European Commissioner for Justice) Thierry Breton (European Commissioner for Internal Market) We also call on Lara Wolters (Member of the European Parliament & lead rapporteur CSDDD) and all other MEPs involved in supply chain legislation, to champion this proposal in Parliament.

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We call on the European Commission - and especially Commissioners Reynders and Breton - to introduce binding legislation that requires:

1 Visible warning-style labels on consumer products made with:

  • child labour
  • forced labour
  • dangerous, unregulated mining or extraction
  • conflict minerals and ecologically destructive sourcing

2 Transparant digital traceability of all major components (e.g. kobalt, lithium, gold, textiles) showing:

  • origin country
  • working conditions 
  • percentage of profits received by workers

3 Accountability for importers and producers, even if violations occur deep in the supply chain.

The EU must ensure that no product is allowed onto our shelves without exposing the hidden suffering behind it. We're sold a future of clean energy and ethical consumption - but behind every ‘’green'' battery and shiny device lies a trail of child labour, toxic mines, and corporate silence.

It's time to bring the truth to the surface - and force corporations to face it too. Real sustainability begins with honesty.

Why is this important?

We're told that the future is clean, green and ethical - powered by electric cars, smartphones and renewable energy, but the reality behind these technologies is far from clean.

The batteries in our phones and EVs are built with cobalt mined in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where children work in toxic conditions, earning less than €2  a day. These people suffer in silence while corporations profit in the billions. And consumers are never told the truth.

If we truly care about sustainability and justice, we must stop hiding the human cost behind shiny technology. A visible, mandatory label would expose what's behind the product - and force companies to take real responsibility. 

It's not just about transparency, it's about dignity, truth and a future that's fair for everyone - not just those at the top of the supply chain.

Protect the Freedom Flotilla: End the aid blockade on Gaza NOW!

European Commission, Member State governments, the European Parliament, and world leaders

We call on you to immediately: 

  • Guarantee the safe passage of the Freedom Flotilla to Gaza
  • Facilitate the unhindered entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza
  • Guarantee compliance with international law by the State of Israel
  • Impose sanctions on Israel and suspend the EU-Israel Association Agreement
  • Impose an EU-wide arms embargo on Israel
  • Ensure EU compliance with ICC arrest warrants, and an end to Israel's genocide, occupation and colonisation of Palestine.

We urge global leaders to go beyond words - to take concrete, public action in support of this humanitarian mission and the rule of law.

Why is this important?

A humanitarian mission is under threat.

The Madleen, a humanitarian ship from the Freedom Flotilla Coalition, is sailing toward Gaza with food, medicine, and infant supplies. [1] On board are 12 humanitarians, including MEP Rima Hassan and Greta Thunberg, risking their lives to break the blockade and deliver essential aid. [2]

Since 2 March 2025, all aid access to Gaza has been shut down. [3] Dozens of children have died of starvation. Over 90% of Gaza’s population is at risk of famine. [4] 

This is not a crisis—it is a genocide.

The Flotilla has been surveilled by Israeli ‘Heron’ military drones “battle-tested” on Gaza’s civilian population and deployed by EU coast guards [5], raising urgent fears of an imminent attack. A vessel from the same coalition was already targeted and destroyed by a drone on 2nd May near Malta [6]. 

The risk of a deadly attack is real - a naval commando is being prepared to stop the Flotilla from reaching Gaza. [7] The consequences of inaction are deadly for the people of Gaza and the Freedom Flotilla.

This mission is legal. The aid is urgent. The responsibility to act lies with all of us. UN member states have both a legal and moral obligation to end the famine and the crimes being committed in Gaza.

More than 200 entities and NGOs have already signed this demand for immediate action.

Millions of Palestinians face starvation. Aid must reach Gaza. The Freedom Flotilla must be protected.

Sign now to demand action!

2025-6-protegeons-le-gouf-de-capbreton-p.title: Protect the Capbreton Canyon : establish a genuine Marine Protected Area now !
2025-6-protegeons-le-gouf-de-capbreton-p.description_full:
English

  • Français

Protect the Capbreton Canyon : establish a genuine Marine Protected Area now !

President Emmanuel Macron; Ministry for Ecological Transition, Biodiversity, Forests, the Sea and Fisheries; The French Office for Biodiversity; The National Council for Nature Protection (CNPN); The Prefect of the Nouvelle-Aquitaine Region; The European Commission; The European Parliament; The European Environment Agency

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We call for the swift designation of the French side of the Capbreton Canyon, located in the heart of the Bay of Biscay, as a Marine Protected Area (MPA) with strong and binding protections. This measure is essential to safeguard the area’s unique marine biodiversity and geological features, and to ensure that France’s ocean policies align with its international commitments to protect critical marine habitats in metropolitan waters.

Why is this important?

The Capbreton Canyon is one of the deepest and most ecologically rich underwater canyons in Europe. This natural treasure is home to iconic species like orcas, sperm whales, dolphins, sunfish, and the mythical giant squid, along with vital habitats such as deep reefs and submarine caves.
In 2025, the EU protected the Spanish side of this ecosystem via the Natura 2000 network — now the French side urgently needs protection too.

✊ OUR DEMANDS

✅ Protect the Capbreton Canyon as a Marine Protected Area (MPA)
→ Following the recent the Spanish designation (Natura 2000 site Jaizkibel–Capbreton).
→ The National Council for Nature Protection (CNPN), in its March 2025 advisory (self-referral – deliberation no. 2025-11), highlighted the canyon’s exceptional character as “a global rarity” and recommended “identifying the French sector of the Capbreton Canyon as a Strong Protection Zone (ZPF) in the short term, even though it is not currently proposed for designation before 2027.”

✅ Preserve its exceptional biodiversity
→ Orcas, sperm whales, fin whales, minke whales, giant squids, deep-sea habitats, underwater caves, unique marine ecosystems, nurseries and migratory corridors — including in the shallower coastal waters surrounding the canyon.

✅ Protect its unique oceanographic dynamics
→ Which form remarkable waves, supporting surfing, artisanal fishing, and coastal ecosystems.

✅ Strengthen France’s Marine Protected Areas
→ With real enforcement against overfishing, pollution, and industrial activities, especially in deep-sea canyons.

✅ Apply in mainland France the same ambition shown overseas
→ France recently announced the creation of the world’s largest MPA in French Polynesia.
→ Yet only 0.1% of metropolitan waters are under strong protection, with a new target of just 4%.
→ Let’s also protect the Bay of Biscay — starting with the Capbreton Canyon!

We, citizens, associations, and committed stakeholders, urge immediate action to safeguard this exceptional and fragile natural heritage.

Sign this petition to demand the protection of the Capbreton Canyon and the Bay of Biscay — so that France can truly lead on marine conservation.

Together, let’s protect our ocean — our future depends on it.

NO to the Submission Deal with the United States – Defend Europe’s Economy

European Parliament, the Council of the European Union, and all European citizens concerned about our economic sovereignty

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

European Parliament, the Council of the European Union, and all European citizens concerned about our economic sovereignty

 

Why is this important?

We call on the European Parliament and the governments of the EU Member States to reject the EU-US trade agreement signed on 27 July 2025, to demand the immediate resignation of the President of the European Commission, and to launch a comprehensive plan to restore Europe’s economic independence.

Why this petition?

On July 27, 2025, the European Union signed a disastrous trade agreement with the United States that raises tariffs on our exports from 1.5% to 15%.
In return, Europe opens its markets wide to American products, removes its own tariffs, commits to purchasing $750 billion worth of American energy, and pledges $600 billion of European investments into the US economy.

This deal endangers our industry, our jobs, and our economic sovereignty.

Why is this alarming?

European exporters, especially the German automotive sector, will lose billions of euros.

Economists estimate that the EU’s GDP could drop by 0.5% in the medium term.

Europe is becoming increasingly dependent on the United States for energy, pharmaceuticals, technology, and capital.

Many European political leaders have already denounced the deal as unbalanced and unsustainable.

What we demand

The immediate rejection of this agreement by the member states of the European Union.

The resignation of the President of the European Commission, who betrayed her mandate by accepting a text that goes against European interests.

The launch of an economic independence plan aimed at:

repatriating essential services and pharmaceutical production to Europe;

securing our energy resources and investing in nuclear and renewable energy;

developing sovereign IT infrastructures and European artificial intelligence solutions.

Sign to defend Europe

This agreement is a threat to our common future. We refuse to let Europe submit to an external power at the expense of its citizens.

By signing this petition, you demand that our leaders protect our industries, our jobs, and our sovereignty.

Sign and share widely.
Because a Europe that does not defend itself is a Europe that disappears.

To the European Commission, especially to President von der Leyen, Vice-President for a Clean, Just and Competitive Transition, Teresa Ribera, and Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, Henna Virkkunen

Petition

We call on you to:

  • Reject any weakening or deregulation via the proposed Digital Omnibus of:
    • the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR);
    • the Digital Services Act (DSA);
    • the Digital Markets Act (DMA);
    • and the Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act).

Europeans demand strict, enforceable digital rules - not watered-down laws. Protect our rights, safety, and democracy online. Don’t bend to Big Tech!

For the first time ever, Big Tech lost.

EU authorities fined Google and Elon Musk for breaking Europe’s digital rules - rules designed to protect people from scams, abuse, and unchecked corporate power. [1]

Democracy wins. We all live happily ever after. Or at least this is how it should end.

Now, Big Tech is panicking. And fighting back. Trump even publicly attacked the EU fine on Musk’s X, calling it “nasty” and warning Europe to “be very careful”. [2]

Our partners have recently proven that powerful lobbyists are pushing behind closed doors for an “omnibus” law. In reality, it’s a rollback - written to protect billionaires’ profits, not people. [4]

The tantrum Big Tech is throwing shows just how much is at stake. Because these rules are the only thing standing between corporate power and people’s safety.

Together, we’ve already shown that citizens can take on tech giants - and win. [5] Now we must make sure this victory isn’t undone in the shadows.

Tell EU decision-makers: don’t water down Big Tech rules. Protect people, not billionaires!

Boycott Trump's World Cup!

To the football associations of World Cup-qualifying countries in Europe:

  • Deutscher Fußball-Bund (Germany)
  • Federação Portuguesa de Futebol (Portugal)
  • Fédération Française de Football (France)
  • Hrvatski nogometni savez (Croatia)

  • Schweizerischer Fussballverband / Association Suisse de Football (Switzerland)
  • Scottish Football Association (Scotland)
  • The Football Association (England)

Petition

We call on you to:

  • Demand that FIFA moves any World Cup matches due to be played in the USA to alternative host countries.
  • Pledge to boycott any matches not moved out of the USA, in order to ensure the safety and security of all players and fans, regardless of their ethnicity or country of origin.

Why is this important?

There seems to be no red line Trump won’t cross. 

One day he’s threatening to invade Greenland. Next, he’s defending the murder of protesters by ICE agents. [1]

This summer the football World Cup will be co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico. 

But a country that attacks protesters and snatches innocent people off the streets cannot ensure the safety of players and fans. And supporters from countries on Trump’s travel ban list - like Iran and Haiti - won’t even be allowed to come and support their teams. [2]

There’s a relatively easy solution. Canada and Mexico are co-hosts. The matches planned for the US - including the big final - could and should be played there instead. 

Trump has shown time and again that he cares above all about image. And even if only a few countries join the boycott, it will be a huge embarrassment for him and a powerful, global rejection of his actions. 

The global football governing body, FIFA has the final say. But national football associations and the regional blocs that make up FIFA have huge power. [3] 

Together we can turn up the pressure on them to take a stand: boycott any matches played in the USA, unless they get moved. And ensure the World Cup is a place that welcomes all fans and players. 

Sign the petition to demand a boycott of Trump’s World Cup!

2026-01-trial-digital-euro-petition-EN.title: Save the digital euro
2026-01-trial-digital-euro-petition-EN.description_full:
Save the digital euro

To the European Parliament, the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs (ECON), the Council of the European Union and the European Commission

Petition

We call on you to create a digital euro that:

  1. Enables Europe’s independence from foreign payment providers.
  2. Acts as a foundation of a sovereign and resilient European payment infrastructure that follows the highest privacy standards.
  3. Gives all Europeans access to public money with a generous holding limit, so it can become a credible alternative to private money of commercial banks.
  4. Simplifies transactions between people within Europe.

Do not lower the ambitions of the digital euro project under pressure from banks and Big Tech. Ensure it serves people above profits.

Why is this important?

Imagine this: groceries in hand, you tap your card to pay. Denied. No access to your money. 

Europe almost entirely relies on US companies to handle digital payments. If political pressure rises in the US, they could be forced to restrict access to our money. [1]

There is a way out: Europe’s own digital money.

A digital euro: backed by our central bank, accessible to everyone. Even without a private bank account. Free from foreign interference. After years of preparation, a strong proposal is now on the table. 

And that’s exactly why banks and Big Tech are panicking. They’re pushing hard to weaken the digital euro to protect their profits and US companies like MasterCard and PayPal. 

Now, Members of the European Parliament have two weeks to decide. They are elected to represent us and track messages from voters. And when thousands of people speak up at once, they feel the pressure. 

If we stay silent, the banks and Big Tech win. So let’s send a message to our MEPs they can’t ignore: Europeans must control their own money.

Tell your MEP today: Save the digital euro. Don’t give in to banks and Big Tech.

References:

  1. https://www.dw.com/en/can-europe-wean-itself-off-us-credit-card-firms/a-72403227

2026-01-trial-landfills-petition-EN.title: End the toxic landfill crisis in Europe
2026-01-trial-landfills-petition-EN.description_full:
End the toxic landfill crisis in Europe

To the European Commission, European Parliament, European Environment Agency

Petition

We call on you to:

  1. Establish an EU-wide, publicly accessible database of all the landfill sites, with risk assessments
  2. Require systematic testing at all identified landfills and enforce actions to prevent contamination of groundwater and surface water
  3. Amend the Landfill Directive and Drinking Water Directive to close regulatory gaps
  4. Establish dedicated EU funding to support member states and local authorities in safely remediating high-risk landfills

Why is this important?

Thousands of forgotten landfill sites lie beneath our fields, forests and playgrounds across Europe. Now, many of them are leaking toxic waste into our rivers and the water we drink.

A shocking new investigation revealed the location of 60,000 old landfills in the UK, France, Italy, Spain and other countries in Europe. [1] Some of them are already releasing heavy metals, arsenic and “forever chemicals”. 

These landfills poison us. Communities unknowingly drink contaminated water. Farmers grow food on polluted land. Wildlife is exposed to chemicals that never break down.

There is no complete EU map of where these sites are and no systematic monitoring. Worst of all - there's no coordinated plan to clean them up.

We have an opportunity right now to change this. The EU’s Landfill Directive is scheduled for review this year - a rare moment when rules can be strengthened. 

Together we can tell EU leaders we know the damage these landfills are doing. We can force them to ensure toxic landfills are finally monitored, and prevent decades-old waste from poisoning our communities.

References:

  1. https://www.investigate-europe.eu/posts/europes-toxic-landfill-crisis-exposed-in-groundbreaking-mapping-project

2026-01-trial-noise-pollution-petition-E.title: Cure the noise pandemic
2026-01-trial-noise-pollution-petition-E.description_full:
Cure the noise pandemic

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

To address the noise pandemic we call for:

  • Legally binding noise reduction targets at the Member State level, in line with the EU’s Zero Pollution Action Plan, which aims to reduce the number of people chronically disturbed by transport noise by 30% by 2030.
  • Urgently provide cities with updated guidance on interpreting noise data, following the new EU noise calculation methodology. 
  • Increased funding to support noise reduction initiatives.

Why is this important?

Traffic. Drilling. Sirens. Your body can’t cope with today’s noise levels. 

Experts say noise is like a chemical inside your body eroding your heart and brain functions - shortening your life. Even if you don’t notice it, you’re equally affected because you never get to switch off.

66,000 people die prematurely every year from traffic noise in Europe. It causes diabetes, obesity, hypertension, hyperactivity and attention deficit - to name a few.

But there is good news. The World Health Organisation has finally recognised that noise pollution is the second leading health hazard for people living in cities. 

Our health urgently needs more than recognition. We need better, binding targets - not just weak recommendations - from our governments. Then, city mayors need funding to implement the changes needed. 

That’s where we matter: A massive wave of citizens’ action could force European authorities to fund cities to give us better, longer lives. The longer we wait to act, the more of us will become victims of the noise pandemic.

A multi-millionaire oil-refining company is fighting hard to avoid paying its fair share.
