2026-06-08-trial-Stop-ReArm-Europe-verA-.title: Stop European rearmament!
2026-06-08-trial-Stop-ReArm-Europe-verA-.description_full:
Stop European rearmament!

To the Members of national parliaments, European heads of state and government, Members of European parliament, President and vice-presidents of the European Commission

Petition

We oppose the European Union's plans to spend an extra €800 billion on arms. 

Likewise, we oppose increased military spending in non-EU states.
These hundreds of billions will be stolen from social services, health, education, labour, peace building, international cooperation, from a just transition and climate justice. These billions will only benefit arms manufacturers in Europe, in the USA and elsewhere.
We believe that such spending will make war more likely, and the future less safe for everyone. At a time of acute nuclear tension, this is unforgivable. It will generate more debt, more austerity, more borders. It will deepen racism. It will fuel climate change. We do not need more weapons; we do not need to prepare for more wars. What we need is a totally different plan: real, social, ecological and common security for Europe and for the world.

We are taking a stand against war. We want European decision-makers to stop European rearmament and take a serious commitment to global disarmament.

Why is this important?

When I think about war, I think about my grandfather. He was sent to Indochina with the French army. And like many of his generation, he experienced war first-hand.

I grew up hearing stories about young men who never made it home.

That's why I find it unsettling to hear politicians tell us that Europe must spend an extra €800 billion on weapons to keep us safe. [1]

History offers a warning. Again and again, arms races have created a dangerous cycle: one side rearms, the other feels threatened and rearms too, tensions rise, and eventually the very conflict everyone feared becomes reality. [2]

European countries already spend several times more on their militaries than Russia. [3]The problem is not that Europe lacks weapons, but that another arms race risks making war more likely, not less. 

That's why dozens of organisations from across Europe will take to the streets of Brussels next week to show that another path is possible. [4]

To be heard, they need to show that thousands of Europeans stand behind them. And this is where you come in. 

If enough people speak out now, leaders will know that Europeans want to imagine a different future - one built on diplomacy, peacebuilding and common security. Will you sign the petition?

References:

  1. https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_25_793 ; https://commission.europa.eu/topics/defence/future-european-defence_en

  2. This concept is known as the “security dilemma”: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_dilemma  ; https://freshwriting.nd.edu/essays/the-security-dilemma-and-the-causes-of-world-war-i/

  3. https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2025/unprecedented-rise-global-military-expenditure-european-and-middle-east-spending-surges ; https://peace.fes.de/projects/visualising-military-capabilities.html

  4. https://stoprearm.org/invitation-rally-in-brussels-on-14-june-month-of-decentralized-action-across-europe/

2026-06-ban-coral-killing-sunscreen-tria.title: Ban coral-killing sunscreen!
2026-06-ban-coral-killing-sunscreen-tria.description_full:
Ban coral-killing sunscreen!

To Jessika Roswall, European Commissioner for Environment, Water Resilience and a Competitive Circular Economy, Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy, and Costas Kadis, European Commissioner for Fisheries and Oceans. 

Petition

We call on you to:

  • Phase out and ban these dangerous substances from sunscreen products sold in the European Union: oxybenzone, octinoxate, octocrylene, benzophenone-1, benzophenone-8, nano titanium dioxide and 4-Methylbenzylidene Camphor (4-MBC) from sunscreen products sold in the European Union, and restrict harmful UV filters in Marine Protected Areas and other ecologically sensitive coastal zones.
  • Introduce mandatory marine ecotoxicity assessments for all UV filters authorised under EU cosmetic legislation, and ensure environmental claims such as “marine-safe” or “reef-safe” are scientifically verified and legally regulated.
  • Promote safer alternatives, including mineral-based UV filters with demonstrated lower environmental impacts.
  • Create a dedicated EU funding programme for the conservation, restoration and recovery of Mediterranean coral ecosystems, including coralligenous reefs, red coral habitats and gorgonian forests.

Why is this important?

This summer, millions of people are reaching for sunscreen - slathering it on before going for a swim or enjoying the beach. Many of us choose bottles labelled "reef safe" or "reef friendly", thinking we're helping to protect the sea. 

But here’s the problem: in Europe, these labels can mean almost anything - and, most of the time, they mean nothing at all.

Companies don't have to prove their products are safe for marine life before selling them to us. [1]

Several commonly used UV filters accumulate in marine environments and contribute to coral stress, bleaching and wider coastal damage. [2] Some of these same ingredients could also cause lower fertility and hormonal disruption in humans. [3]

Our oceans are under threat. Every summer season that passes without proper regulation is causing damage that we can't undo. [4] Hawaii and Palau have already acted to restrict sunscreen ingredients that threaten marine wildlife. [5] The EU hasn’t.

We should be able to protect our skin and protect the sea with confidence. But that will only happen if enough of us demand change.

Sign the petition calling on the EU to regulate harmful sunscreen ingredients and put an end to misleading "reef safe" claims!

References:

  1. https://savethereef.org/about-reef-save-sunscreen.html 
  2. https://www.reefsafety.com.au/ ; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/news/sunscreen-corals.html
  3. https://suntribesunscreen.com/en-es/pages/toxic-sunscreen-ingredients-to-avoid
  4. https://www.icm.csic.es/en/news/climate-crisis-drives-mediterranean-coral-populations-collapse
  5. Hawaii Senate Bill 2571 (effective 2021), prohibits the sale of sunscreens containing oxybenzone and octinoxate. Palau Responsible Tourism Education Act (2020), bans several reef-toxic sunscreen ingredients. https://www.reefsafety.com.au/blog/what-hawaii-palau-teach-australia

2026-06-lyle-letter-translation-petition.title: Make Homes for People, Not for Profit
2026-06-lyle-letter-translation-petition.description_full:
Make Homes for People, Not for Profit

To: Dan Jørgensen, European Commissioner for Climate Action and Housing/Urban Policy; the European Commission’s Housing Task Force (DG ENER); and Members of the European Parliament’s Committee on Housing (HOUS)

Petition

Homes are disappearing for ordinary Europeans. Families freeze, students struggle, locals are pushed out.

Housing is a human right - not a profit opportunity.

We call on those in power to act now:

  • Guarantee decent, affordable housing for all.
  • Hold developers and investors accountable for speculation and empty homes.
  • Invest in social and public housing that keeps people in their communities.
  • Renovate homes for people and planet — with fair rules that keep bills low and residents in place.
  • Keep rents fair and limit tourist rentals so cities stay homes for people.


Homes are the foundation of our lives and our future.

It’s time to put people before profit and make housing a right for all.

Why is this important?

Everyone deserves a safe, affordable place to call home.

But across Europe, people are being priced out of their cities. [1] Forced to move farther and farther away from their jobs, their friends, their roots.

It doesn’t have to be this way. And European lawmakers know it.

EU leaders discussed housing for the first time in history. [2] They are now looking at solutions to the housing crisis. [3]

We are a part of a movement putting affordable housing at the top of the EU agenda. Together, we refuse to accept a system that puts profit before people. [4]  

As our leaders look at solutions, now is the time to speak up. We can still change the course, if we act now. Let’s make it impossible for leaders to ignore us: our right to housing is not for sale.

2026-06-lyle-opus-petition-EN.title: Run EU data centres on 100% renewables!
2026-06-lyle-opus-petition-EN.description_full:
English

  • Français
  • Deutsch
  • Italiano
  • Nederlands
  • Nederlands

Run EU data centres on 100% renewables!

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We demand that: 

  • All new data centres in Europe must meet their energy demand with 100% new, local and additional renewable energy 
  • Companies must be made to be transparent on energy demand projections, real energy use and emissions per site for planned and existing data centres
  • No new data centres in Europe until they are made compatible with Europe’s energy transition and climate goals

Why is this important?

Thousands of enormous, energy-hungry data centres, forcing up electricity prices for all of us. That’s what risks happening unless we demand an alternative.

Data centres use huge amounts of energy. In Ireland alone, they already consume 20% of the country’s electricity. [1] Now, driven by skyrocketing AI use, Big Tech wants to build thousands more in Europe. [2]

New data centres in Europe should only be built if they can be powered by renewable energy. We could fight climate change and bring down bills for everyone by making Big Tech invest in wind and solar. 

Decisions are being made in Brussels right now on how to make sure data centres are energy efficient. These decisions will have real impacts on our bills, our lives, and our local communities. 

Our planet should be the priority, not AI company profits. We need decisionmakers to be bolder and require all data centres to run on 100% new, renewable energy.  

They need to know that people across Europe are behind them. Sign the petition now to tell the EU: Data centres must be powered by 100% new renewable energy.

  2. https://reference.eu
  3. https://reference.eu

2026-06-trial-maximum-working-temperatur.title: Keep workers safe in the heat
2026-06-trial-maximum-working-temperatur.description_full:
Keep workers safe in the heat

To the European Commission and the governments of the member states of the EU and the UK 

Petition

As climate change worsens, heat waves will become more frequent and more severe. We call on you to ensure there is sufficient legislation in place to protect workers from excessive heat. This includes setting maximum working temperatures - with different levels taking into account the type of work (e.g. sedentary or physical labour) and whether it is carried out indoors or outside. 

Why is this important?

Too hot to think. Too hot to sleep. Too hot to work. 

That’s what it’s like for many of us right now, as temperatures climb past 40 degrees in parts of Europe. [1]

Working in extreme heat can be deadly. [2] And as our bodies struggle to function in the heat, accidents on the job become more common. When temperatures rise over 30C, workplace accidents rise sharply. [3]

Some countries, like Belgium and Hungary, have introduced maximum working temperatures. But with no EU-wide law, millions of us risk injury or even death when a heatwave hits.

And every year it gets hotter. France just recorded its hottest day ever. [4] This won’t be the last record set. 

If we don’t force our leaders to act now, there will be more deaths, more illness and more injuries at work. But nothing is final yet. If enough of us speak up, we can push them to guarantee that workers are protected from extreme heat. 

Sign the petition now to call on the EU, its member states and the UK to ensure workers are safe from extreme heat.

2026-06-trial-stop-smart-glasses-petitio.title: Stop smart glasses filming us without our consent
2026-06-trial-stop-smart-glasses-petitio.description_full:
Stop smart glasses filming us without our consent

To the European Commission, European Parliament, and EU governments

Petition

Smart glasses, like Meta RayBans, and their ability to secretly record people without their consent are a dangerous invasion of our privacy. 

We call on you to:

  • Amend or create new regulation to stop smart glasses being able to record people without their consent.
  • Ban the sale of smart glasses unless they comply with data protection and privacy regulation.

Why is this important?

Imagine someone coming up to talk to you in the street. Without your knowledge, the whole interaction is filmed and put on YouTube, strangers mocking you in the comments. 

It happened to Oonagh. She was chatted up by a man on the beach who secretly recorded her. Online, the video was viewed over a million times and received sexual and abusive comments.[1]

This is possible because of smart glasses, like Meta RayBans. They look like ordinary glasses, but have a small camera embedded in the frames - recording everything the viewer sees. 

Europe has strong laws on privacy, but right now they’re powerless to stop this new and dangerous invasion of it.

But politicians are speaking up. [2] National data protection agencies are raising the alarm and lawsuits are being brought against Meta. [3]

We know pressure can work. Because when the Irish privacy regulator called them out, Meta announced they would make the recording light on the glasses bigger for transparency.[4] But this is not enough. Work-arounds are already being shared online on how to cover it up. 

Our leaders need to know they have people like you and me backing them. Together, we can force them to take action to address the dangers that smart glasses pose to us and to our privacy. 

Sign the petition to call for the EU to stop smart glasses invading our privacy.

2026-06-trial-verB-Stop-ReArm-Europe-pet.title: Stop European rearmament!
2026-06-trial-verB-Stop-ReArm-Europe-pet.description_full:
Stop European rearmament!

To the Members of national parliaments, European heads of state and government, Members of European parliament, President and vice-presidents of the European Commission

Petition

We oppose the European Union's plans to spend an extra €800 billion on arms. 

Likewise, we oppose increased military spending in non-EU states.
These hundreds of billions will be stolen from social services, health, education, labour, peace building, international cooperation, from a just transition and climate justice. These billions will only benefit arms manufacturers in Europe, in the USA and elsewhere.
We believe that such spending will make war more likely, and the future less safe for everyone. At a time of acute nuclear tension, this is unforgivable. It will generate more debt, more austerity, more borders. It will deepen racism. It will fuel climate change. We do not need more weapons; we do not need to prepare for more wars. What we need is a totally different plan: real, social, ecological and common security for Europe and for the world.

We are taking a stand against war. We want European decision-makers to stop European rearmament and take a serious commitment to global disarmament.

Why is this important?

I'm writing this while hail lashes against my window in Brussels. Just a few days ago, the city was sweltering in 35°C heat.

Climate disasters are becoming more frequent. Families are struggling with rising energy costs. Wars dominate the headlines. [1]

And in this uncertainty, European leaders are preparing to spend another €800 billion on weapons. [2]

When did security become something measured by missiles and military budgets rather than by lives protected? 

Because when floods destroy homes, weapons don't stop the water. When families struggle to pay their bills, weapons don't lower prices. And when wars devastate entire communities, weapons are part of the cycle - not the solution. 

Europe does not lack weapons. What it lacks is a conversation about what actually keeps people safe. [3]

And that conversation cannot wait.

Next week, dozens of organisations from across Europe will gather in Brussels to challenge the idea that more weapons are the only answer to insecurity. [4]

If enough people sign this petition before then, we can show that they are speaking for thousands of Europeans - not just the ones gathered in Brussels. Will you sign the petition?

Stop Volkswagen’s dangerous new deal

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

Volkswagen wants to move from building cars to supplying systems used in warfare - and make billions from it.

The German corporation is exploring a deal linked to Israeli military technology at its Osnabrück factory.

The deal is not done yet. That means we can still stop it. But we don’t have long. We call on Volkswagen to:

  • Rule out producing parts linked to Israeli military technology;
  • Keep the Osnabrück site focused on civilian manufacturing;
  • Publish full transparency on any talks with military contractors.

Pressure is growing over Germany’s military support to Israel. 

Europe should not become a hub for expanding military production tied to war and genocide.

Volkswagen still has a choice. We’re calling on it to stop this dirty deal now.

Why is this important?

Volkswagen built its reputation making cars. Now they want to build war machines. [1] 

Eight billion euros in profits isn’t enough, so they’re considering manufacturing parts for Israeli military technology. A new deal means they would make parts for the Iron Dome - a critical tool for Netanyahu’s war chest. [2]

Deadly air strikes. Unlawful use of white phosphorus in Lebanon. Children killed in Gaza. If Volkswagen agrees to this deal, they are complicit. [3] We need them to hear from us - Europe should not become a hub fuelling illegal wars.

Volkswagen is still recovering from the Dieselgate scandal. They’re under fire for plans to cut over 10,000 factory jobs. [4] Now, they want to sweep their plans to profit from war under the rug. 

We don’t have long to force Volkswagen to stop this deadly deal. And the fastest way to make them listen is by damaging what they depend on most: their brand.

If people start speaking out against VW, bosses start to panic. If trust in the brand falls, people will stop buying its cars - and they will lose a lot of money. 

Volkswagen still has a choice. We won’t let them build war machines.

Investigate FIFA’s leader Gianni Infantino

To the FIFA (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) Ethics Committee

Petition

The recent removal of a player’s red card after pressure from US President Donald Trump is unacceptable. This is just one of many instances of the head of FIFA - Gianni Infantino - breaking the association’s own rules around political impartiality. Football must remain fair and equal for all teams.

A US player receives a red card in the World Cup. Donald Trump makes a phone call. The red card disappears. [1]

But as the World Cup is taking place, its leader, Gianni Infantino, is openly and shamelessly cosying up to Trump. 

He removes inconvenient red cards against the US. He praises Trump to the media. He even created a made-up FIFA peace prize just to feed his ego. [3]

But after the red card incident, FIFA and its leader are under enormous pressure. [4]

2026-07-protect-europe-from-burning-tria.title: Protect Europe from burning!
2026-07-protect-europe-from-burning-tria.description_full:
Protect Europe from burning!

The European Commission, especially the Commissioner for Preparedness, Crisis Management and Equality, Hadja Lahbib and the Commissioner for Climate, Net Zero and Clean Growth, Wopke Hoekstra.

Petition

Every summer, millions of Europeans face devastating wildfires, floods and extreme heat. Climate disasters are no longer exceptional events: they are a permanent threat to our safety.

If Europe can invest billions to prepare for military threats, it must also invest in protecting people from the climate emergency.

We call on the European Union to:

  • Allocate at least €12 billion to the Union Civil Protection Mechanism in the next EU budget, giving Europe the firefighting aircraft, equipment, emergency teams and trained personnel it needs to protect people from climate disasters. 
  • Adopt binding EU legislation requiring every Member State to meet minimum standards for wildfire prevention and emergency preparedness, including prevention work throughout the year, sufficient trained firefighters, early warning systems and coordinated emergency planning.
  • Hold governments accountable when they fail to protect people, by enforcing these standards through EU law and linking compliance to access to relevant EU funding.

Europe must stop treating climate disasters as national emergencies. They are a shared European responsibility.

Why is this important?

“It looked like the apocalypse”. [1] This is how firefighters describe this summer’s wildfires.

From Spain to France, Greece to Portugal, more than 300,000 people have been evacuated as forests, homes and lives disappear in smoke. [2] Entire families forced to say goodbye to a lifetime of memories, of savings, of the places they grew up. This can’t go on.

Europe cannot afford to treat every summer as another emergency. [3] Without far greater investment in prevention and firefighting, more people will be forced to flee, more lives will be put at risk, and entire landscapes will burn for months.

The European Parliament is already calling to put  €12 billion into fighting wildfires and preventing them. The money isn’t final yet. It’s part of the EU budget being decided now, for the next 5 years. [4] If enough of us speak up before that budget is closed, we can make sure it stays in. Together, we can demand the protection every European deserves. 

Sign to protect the EU from burning!

2026-07-toxic-coffee-trial-petition-EN.title: No more poison in our coffee!
2026-07-toxic-coffee-trial-petition-EN.description_full:
No more poison in our coffee!

To Oligvér Várhelyi, European Commissioner for Health and Animal Welfare, and Maroš Šefčovič, European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security.

Petition

Coffee is one of the least‑tested imported commodities despite proven high pesticide contamination rates. Consumers have a right to know what is in their cup, and we won’t accept residues of toxic poison in our coffee. That’s why we ask you to:

  • Require routine testing of all imported coffee, green and roasted.
  • Require disclosure of all detected residues, including multi‑residue “cocktail effects.”
  • Align import rules with export rules: if a pesticide is banned for use, it should not be tolerated as a residue

Why is this important?

For millions across Europe, coffee is a daily ritual. A moment to wake up, take a break, or catch up with friends. That’s why this caught me off guard: Our coffee is being poisoned.

One in every five cups of coffee sold in Europe contains toxic pesticides. Often, it's not just one pesticide, but a cocktail of chemicals - including some that Europe has already banned because they're linked to cancer, birth defects, neurological damage, and the destruction of nature. [1]

How is that possible?

There is a loophole: European companies can still manufacture these same poisons and export them to countries where our coffee is grown. [2]

These farmers, farm workers, and nearby communities are exposed to chemicals Europe decided are too dangerous for us. Water sources are polluted. Wildlife suffers. Entire ecosystems are put at risk.

And the poison doesn't stay there. It comes back to Europe in the coffee we drink every day.

No one should sacrifice their health, their environment, or their future so chemical companies can keep selling products Europe has already declared too dangerous.

It's time. Sign and share today to keep our coffee safe!

References:

  1. https://coffeewatch.org/poison-in-your-coffee/
  2. https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/10/10/the-eus-double-standard-on-toxic-pesticides

2026-07-trial-big-food-trial-EN.title: Big Food is making us sick - We need an EU sugar tax!
2026-07-trial-big-food-trial-EN.description_full:
Big Food is making us sick - We need an EU sugar tax!

To the European Commission, the European Parliament, and the governments of EU Member States 

Petition

Investigative journalists have revealed the dirty tactics giants like Coca-Cola, Kellogg's, and Ferrero use to keep sugary products widely available, even though they harm our health. They deploy legal threats and intense lobbying to pressure you, our elected officials, into blocking or delaying measures that could reduce sugar consumption, like sugar taxes.

This is unacceptable. As our representatives, your duty is to the health and well-being of European citizens, not to the profits of Big Food.

We call on you to stand firm against this corporate bullying and take bold, coordinated action at the EU level:

  • Introduce an EU-wide sugar tax on sugary drinks and ultra-processed foods. 
  • Resist industry pressure and implement sugar taxes at the national level. 
  • Combine sugar taxes with other measures like junk food marketing restrictions and mandatory front-of-pack nutrition labeling to maximize the public health impact.
  • Invest the revenues from sugar taxes in health promotion campaigns and programs to make healthy diets more affordable and accessible for all.

Obesity, diabetes, and heart disease are placing an ever-growing burden on our health systems and our society. We cannot allow the narrow interests of a few multinationals to override the health of millions of Europeans.

Why is this important?

Junk food giants like Coca-Cola, Kellogg's and Ferrero are fighting to keep our kids hooked on sugar. And blocking every rule that would stop them. [1]

An investigative report has exposed their dirty tactics: legal threats and intense lobbying to pressure governments into stopping or delaying the very policies that could cut sugar consumption. That means trying to block taxes on sugar, limits on junk food ads, and clearer labeling. [2]

Too much sugar is linked to obesity, diabetes, heart disease, and tooth decay. But these corporations are putting profits ahead of our children's health. [3]

Where sugar taxes have been introduced, they work. In Portugal, a sugar tax cut calories from sugary drinks by around 11%, the equivalent of 30 fewer sugar cubes per person each month. [4]

Now, imagine that across Europe. An EU-wide sugar tax would push companies toward healthier, nutritious alternatives. But Big Food will do everything it can to stop this. 

We can't let them win. With the truth now out in the open, we have a narrow window to act before Big Food's lobbyists bury these findings. 

Sign the petition for an EU-wide sugar tax that makes food and drinks healthier. Your voice will give our politicians the backbone they need to stand up to corporate bullying and put our children's health first!

EU: Protect us from another financial crisis, don’t deregulate banks!

To the EU Commission, the EU Parliament and the member states of the EU

Petition

We call on you to protect people over profits, and ensure EU banking regulation is strong enough to withstand another financial crisis like the one in 2008. Avoid following the US’ lead in cutting crucial rules that protect our financial system and keep banks in check - including easing capital requirements and removing caps on bankers’ bonuses.  

Why is this important?

The Trump administration is making a “bonfire” of banking rules in the US, and there are signs the EU wants to follow suit. [1]

The EU is about to carry out a major review of banking rules and many fear it will give banks too much freedom. It could reduce the funds banks need to keep to cover unexpected losses, and remove caps on bankers’ bonuses. [2]

If it’s allowed to go ahead, it could lead to another 2008-style crisis. Where profit-hungry banks need to be bailed out by the state and people like you and me have to bear the brunt of the cost. 

Right now, the new rules are a draft. This means there’s still time for us to push back, and make sure we are kept safe from another financial crisis. [3]

Sign the petition to tell the EU: Don’t push us into another financial crisis, don’t deregulate banks!

To the EU Commission, the EU Parliament and the member states of the EU

Petition

We call on you to protect people over profits, and ensure EU banking regulation is strong enough to withstand another financial crisis like the one in 2008. Avoid following the US’ lead in cutting crucial rules that protect our financial system and don’t remove caps on bankers’ bonuses.

Why is this important?

Food prices are going up. Bills are going up. Our wages stay the same. All while billionaires and multi-millionaires get wealthier.

And what is the EU doing? Making it easier for bankers to get bigger bonuses. 

The Trump administration is making a “bonfire” of banking rules in the US, and now there are signs Europe wants to copy them. [1] In a major review of banking rules, the EU is considering removing a bonus limit for bankers. 

The limit is there to stop dangerous risk-taking in the financial sector. [2] To stop bankers profiting recklessly, then letting us pick up the pieces when it all goes wrong.

It was put in place after the 2008 financial crisis, when profit-hungry banks had to be bailed out by the state - with people like you and me paying the price. 

For now, the new rules are a threat, but just a draft. This means there’s still time for us to push back, and force the EU to prioritise people over helping the rich get even richer. [3]

Sign the petition to tell the EU: Don’t push us into another financial crisis, don’t remove caps on bankers’ bonuses!

2026-07-trial-investigate-FIFA-petition-.title: Investigate FIFA and its leader Gianni Infantino
2026-07-trial-investigate-FIFA-petition-.description_full:
Investigate FIFA and its leader Gianni Infantino

To FIFA

Petition

The recent removal of a player’s red card after pressure from US President Donald Trump is unacceptable. Football must remain fair and equal for all teams. 

We call on you to urgently investigate Gianni Infantino’s multiple breaches of article 15 of the FIFA Code of Ethics, which says FIFA must remain “neutral in matters of politics and religion”.

Why is this important?

A US player receives a red card in the World Cup. Donald Trump makes a phone call. The red card disappears. [1]

Football - the sport millions of us love - is under threat. FIFA is the global organisation that is supposed to make sure football is fair. It should not favour any country or politician -  it’s written in its own rules. [2]

But its leader, Gianni Infantino, is openly and shamelessly cosying up to Trump. 

He removes inconvenient red cards against the US. He praises him to the media. He even created a made-up FIFA peace prize just to feed Trump’s ego. [3]

But after the red card incident, FIFA and its leader are under enormous pressure. [4] 

Now there are calls for an investigation into Infantino, backed by 50 EU lawmakers. [5] Mass public pressure right now - as the World Cup is in the news - could help tip the scale. 

In order to keep football fair we need to force FIFA to follow its own rules - instead of giving in to Trump. Sign the petition to call for an urgent investigation into Gianni Infantino.

2026-07-trial-menstrual-products-trial-p.title: Demand safe, transparent period products
2026-07-trial-menstrual-products-trial-p.description_full:
Demand safe, transparent period products

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Member States

Petition

We call on the EU to:

  • Require full ingredient transparency on all menstrual products.
  • Introduce independent safety testing before period products reach consumers.
  • Set stronger EU-wide safety standards that put people's health first.

Why is this important?

Would you buy food with no ingredient list?

That’s what I thought.

Yet millions of women and girls use period products every month without knowing exactly what's in them. Companies are not required to fully disclose the ingredients, or to have them independently tested.

And period products aren't something people use once or twice, many rely on them every month, for decades.

When scientists had a look they found traces of heavy metals, including lead and arsenic, in the tampons they tested. [1] 

This affects almost every family in Europe. Your partner. Your daughter. Your granddaughter. 

The good news is that this is fixable. We're calling on European decision-makers to require full ingredient transparency, independent safety testing and stronger standards for menstrual products.

It’s a simple, common-sense demand and if enough of us raise our voices, it becomes impossible to ignore. If a product goes inside our bodies, we deserve to know what's in it.

[1] https://edition.cnn.com/2024/07/11/health/tampons-lead-arsenic-plastics-wellness https://www.chemistryworld.com/features/how-safe-and-sustainable-are-period-products/4021461.article https://www.wen.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Blood-Sweat-and-Pesticides-1-May-2025.pdf

2026-07-trial-police-racism-trial-EN.title: End racist police brutality in Europe: Justice for Abderrahim Fakir
2026-07-trial-police-racism-trial-EN.description_full:
End racist police brutality in Europe: Justice for Abderrahim Fakir

To the European Parliament, the European Commission, and the Italian Government 

Petition

On July 19th, 2026 in Bologna, Italy, Abderrahim Fakir, a 42-year-old Moroccan man who had lived in Italy since he was a child, was brutally killed by police while in distress and in need of help. His death is a tragic reminder of the systemic racism and police brutality that people of colour face in Europe every day.

The police officers involved in Abderrahim's death are not even being investigated. This lack of accountability is unacceptable and only perpetuates a culture of impunity within police forces.

We demand justice for Abderrahim and all victims of police violence. We call on the Italian authorities to:

  • Launch an immediate and thorough investigation into Abderrahim's death, and hold those responsible accountable;
  • End the culture of impunity within police forces by ensuring that all incidents of police violence and misconduct are promptly and thoroughly investigated by an independent body;
  • Address the systemic racism within police forces and implement mandatory anti-racism and de-escalation training for all officers;
  • Invest in community-based mental health and social services to provide care and support for people in distress, instead of relying on police intervention.

We call on the European Parliament and the European Commission to:

  • Condemn the killing of Abderrahim Fakir and call for a thorough investigation;
  • Develop EU-wide guidelines and best practices for addressing racism and discrimination within law enforcement;
  • Support initiatives that promote racial equality, inclusion, and anti-discrimination across Europe.

Why is this important?

Last Sunday in Bologna, the police killed Abderrahim Fakir, a 42-year-old Moroccan man who had lived in Italy since he was a child. His crime? Being in distress and needing help. [1] 

When his friends called for assistance, the police arrived only to pin him to the ground, handcuff him, and press their knee into his neck until he couldn't breathe. Abderrahim died there on the street, his last moments filled with fear and pain. [2] 

Not one of the police officers who held Abderrahim down has been treated as a suspect. [3] If we don't act now, the police will sweep his death under the rug and continue to act with impunity. 

People all over Italy are mobilizing to demand justice. Now it's on all of us to build a movement too big to ignore. Every name we add builds pressure, and ensures those responsible are held to account. 

The murder of George Floyd in America sparked a global movement against police brutality and racism. We need to do the same for Abderrahim in Europe. [4]

Sign the petition to demand justice for Abderrahim Fakir!

2026-07-trial-protect-europe-from-burnin.title: Make Polluters Pay for Climate Disasters
2026-07-trial-protect-europe-from-burnin.description_full:
Make Polluters Pay for Climate Disasters

The European Commission, especially the Commissioner for Climate, Net Zero and Clean Growth, Wopke Hoekstra, Commissioner for Preparedness, Crisis Management and Equality, Hadja Lahbib and the Executive Vice-President for a Clean, Just and Competitive Transition Teresa Ribera, the European Parliament and EU Heads of State.

Petition

We call on the European Union to:

  • Make fossil fuel companies contribute financially to the damage caused by the climate crisis.
  • Use those revenues to better protect people from climate disasters, including wildfire prevention, firefighting, emergency preparedness and climate resilience.
  • Accelerate Europe's transition away from fossil fuels so future climate disasters become less severe.

Why is this important?

"It looked like the apocalypse." [1] That's how firefighters described this summer's wildfires.

From Spain to France, Greece to Portugal, more than 300,000 people have been evacuated as forests, homes and lives disappear in smoke. [2] Entire families forced to say goodbye to a lifetime of memories, their savings, and the places they grew up. 

These disasters are no longer rare. Every summer, Europe burns a little more.

Experts say Europe needs €12 billion to protect people from future wildfires. Last year alone, the biggest oil and gas companies made around €40 billion in profits. Shell alone made almost €18 billion. [3]

While homes burn, the big polluters driving the climate crisis continue to profit. 

Right now, the EU is deciding its next long-term budget. [4] 

One solution is obvious: make oil and gas giants pay for the protection Europe urgently needs. That money could help protect us from climate disasters now and for years to come. But it's still missing from the EU's budget plans.

The money exists. It's just in the wrong hands.

If enough of us speak up now, we still have a chance to make polluters pay instead of leaving ordinary people to foot the bill. Those billions could help protect people from future wildfires, floods and heatwaves - while helping Europe break free from the fossil fuels driving the climate crisis.

Will you sign the petition and tell the EU to make polluters pay?

2026-07-trial-return-regulation-petition.title: Spain, stop Europe's deportation law!
2026-07-trial-return-regulation-petition.description_full:
Spain, stop Europe's deportation law!

To the Prime Minister of Spain Pedro Sánchez

Petition

We’re calling on the Spanish government to use their power to ask the Court of Justice of the European Union to stop the EU's new deportation law from putting fundamental rights at risk. Don't let Europe create a future of immigration raids, family separation and deportations to countries people have never even set foot in.

Why is this important?

After voting for the EU's new deportation law, some politicians celebrated by chanting "Send them back." [1]

They thought the fight was over. But they celebrated too soon.

National governments still have a chance to stop the most dangerous parts of this law before they become Europe's new normal. Over the next few weeks, they can ask Europe's highest court to step in and decide whether the law violates people's fundamental rights. After that, the door closes.

This law could push Europe towards its own ICE-style deportation system: raids on people's homes, families torn apart, people being deported to countries they have never even set foot in. [2]

If any government is likely to act, it's Spain. It has repeatedly raised concerns about the direction Europe is taking on migration and argued for a different approach.

But Spain won't take this step without public backing.

If thousands of us speak up together now, we can show the Spanish government that people across Europe expect it to defend human rights before the deadline runs out.

2026-07-trial-stolen-wildlife-petition-E.title: Stop traffickers. Protect wildlife
2026-07-trial-stolen-wildlife-petition-E.description_full:
Stop traffickers. Protect wildlife

To the Commissioner for Environment, Water Resilience and a Competitive Circular Economy Jessika Roswall, and the entire European Commission

Petition

Europe should never be a safe marketplace for stolen wildlife. Today, criminals can exploit legal loopholes to sell wild-caught animals as captive-bred, allowing endangered animals taken from nature to enter the legal market.

We urge the European Commission to strengthen EU rules so that stolen wildlife can no longer be laundered through legal trade. Close the loopholes, improve traceability, strengthen verification of captive breeding claims, and make it much harder for traffickers to profit from wildlife crime.

Why is this important?

This summer, maybe you'll spot turtles on a beach. Hear birds at sunrise. Or even see monkeys swinging through the trees. 

But while we admire wildlife, traffickers steal thousands of wild animals from their natural homes. Once they reach Europe, they can sell them.

Weak rules and legal loopholes have made  the EU a main destination for wildlife stolen from Africa, Asia, the Americas and other parts of the world. [1]

A baby parrot stolen from the rainforest. A rare reptile taken from the wild. Once they enter the legal market, almost nobody knows where they really came from. Buyers often have no idea they're helping fuel wildlife crime. [2]

Every sale pushes more species towards extinction. Every loophole makes more money for criminal networks.

The good news is that this can change.

The European Commission is reviewing the rules right now. If enough of us speak up, we can help make sure Europe closes these loopholes and make it much harder for traffickers to profit. 

Wild animals belong in nature - not locked in cages and sold for profit. Will you add your name today and call for stronger EU rules to stop wildlife smuggling?

2026-08-29-trial-food-prices-rising-tria.title: Make food affordable for all
2026-08-29-trial-food-prices-rising-tria.description_full:
Make food affordable for all

To the European Commission, the European Parliament, national governments and competition and consumer protection authorities across Europe:

Petition

Food should be affordable for everyone. But prices keep rising and the biggest supermarket chains have enormous power over what we pay at the checkout.

We need governments to make sure everyone can afford to put food on the table:

  • Stop greedy price rises. Give consumer and competition authorities the power to investigate and act when companies push up prices unfairly.
  • Show us where our money goes. Make food prices and profits more transparent
  • Stop supermarket giants from calling the shots. Make sure a handful of giant chains can't decide what farmers earn and what families pay.

Why is this important?

The coffee. The bread. The eggs. Every time another item is scanned, you hear that beep and wonder: how much will my weekly shop cost this time? And it’s not just you.

Food prices have surged for millions of other Europeans. In Italy alone, they've risen by almost 25% since 2021. And experts expect grocery prices to keep climbing this year. [1]

But what your coffee, bread and eggs cost, is not a reflection of what it cost to put them on your plate. It’s the price supermarkets set, often overcharging you, so they can make an extra profit. [2] And governments are letting them get away with it.

Giant corporations like Carrefour, Lidl, and Tesco have enormous power over what we pay. [3] They can choose to feed their customers, or feed their bulging profits.

Our governments have a choice too. They can protect people, or leave supermarket giants to call the shots.

And we know it's possible to make them play fair. In Greece, companies have been fined for breaking rules designed to stop excessive profits from rising prices. Austria and Sweden are also taking action to protect people from soaring food prices. [4]

Supermarkets aren't above the law. And right now, Europe is writing rules that could shrink or inflate our weekly shopping budgets.

Will you sign the petition to demand EU action on food prices?

2026-08-smart-glasses-trial-petition-EN.title: Don’t let smart glasses secretly record us
2026-08-smart-glasses-trial-petition-EN.description_full:
Don’t let smart glasses secretly record us

To the European Commission, European Parliament, and EU governments

Petition

Smart glasses, like Meta’s, can secretly record people without their consent, posing a serious threat to our privacy.  

We call on you to:

  • Strengthen EU rules to ensure smart glasses cannot record people without their knowledge and consent.
  • Require all smart glasses sold in the EU to meet strong privacy and data protection standards, with effective safeguards against covert recording.
  • Act now to protect people’s privacy before camera-equipped smart glasses become commonplace.

Why is this important?

Toluwa thought she was having an ordinary conversation with a stranger.

She had no idea he was wearing Meta smart glasses - or that the glasses were recording her.

She only found out when friends started sending her the video. It had been posted online and viewed more than 200,000 times. [1]

Toluwa had never agreed to be filmed. She had no chance to say no.

It could happen to any of us - on the street, in a café, at work or on our daily commute. 

Just this week, Norway announced plans to tighten the rules around smart glasses. And Poland’s data protection authority has warned that smart glasses pose serious risks to our privacy. [2]

European countries are starting to act. Now the EU needs to step up.

We can push for rules that make sure smart glasses cannot secretly record us without our consent - and cannot be sold in Europe unless they protect our privacy.

Will you join us in calling on the EU to protect our privacy before secret recording becomes our everyday reality?

2026-08-toxic-coffee-trial-2-petition-EN.title: No more poison in our coffee!
2026-08-toxic-coffee-trial-2-petition-EN.description_full:
No more poison in our coffee!

 To Oligvér Várhelyi, European Commissioner for Health and Animal Welfare, and Maroš Šefčovič, European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security, the European Coffee Federation and Coffee Traders Associations.

Petition

Coffee is one of the least‑tested imported commodities despite proven high pesticide contamination rates. Consumers have a right to know what is in their cup, and we won’t accept residues of toxic poisons in our coffee. That’s why we ask you to:

  • Require routine testing of all imported coffee, green and roasted.
  • Require disclosure of all detected residues, including multi‑residue “cocktail effects.”
  • Align import rules with export rules: if a pesticide is banned for use, it should not be tolerated as a residue.
  • For the European Coffee Federation and Coffee Traders Associations to stop supporting or defending the use of pesticides that are prohibited in the EU, and to require that their members and suppliers stop using them.

Why is this important?

For millions across Europe, coffee is a daily ritual. A moment to wake up, take a break, or catch up with friends. That’s why this caught me off guard: Our coffee is being poisoned.

One in every five cups of coffee sold in Europe contains toxic pesticides. Often, it's not just one pesticide, but a cocktail of chemicals - including some that Europe has already banned because they're linked to cancer, birth defects, neurological damage, and the destruction of nature. [1]

How is that possible?

There is a loophole: European companies can still manufacture these same poisons and export them to countries where our coffee is grown. [2]

These farmers, farm workers, and nearby communities are exposed to chemicals Europe decided are too dangerous for us. Water sources are polluted. Wildlife suffers. Entire ecosystems are put at risk.

And the poison doesn't stay there. It comes back to Europe in the coffee we drink every day.

We don’t have to accept this. The European Coffee Federation, which decides what goes in our cups, meets in Brussels on the 16th and 17th of September - just as the EU revisits its pesticide laws. [3] [4] Let's flood them with one message from thousands across Europe: keep poison out of our coffee.

No one should sacrifice their health, their environment, or their future so chemical companies can keep selling products Europe has already declared too dangerous.

It's time. Sign and share today to keep our coffee safe!

References:

  2. https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/10/10/the-eus-double-standard-on-toxic-pesticides

2026-08-trial-2-AI-agents-petition-EN.title: Stop rogue AI tech
2026-08-trial-2-AI-agents-petition-EN.description_full:
Stop rogue AI tech

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on you to strengthen safeguards in AI to protect our data and to legislate a pause in the development of the most dangerous AI systems until their builders can prove, to independent evaluators, that they are safe. AI systems should not threaten our jobs, livelihoods and safety.

Why is this important?

A company got hacked. The really shocking part? It was hacked by an AI system with “little or no human guidance”. [1] 

It sounds like the plot of a sci-fi film. But this is real, and it’s just the tip of the iceberg. 

Technology experts have warned about the dangers of rapid AI progress. [2] It has already impacted real jobs and lives across Europe. [3] This hacking case shows that AI agents can behave in ways we cannot control or predict.

Right now, technology is advancing way faster than the rules are being written. Without safety measures and restrictions in place - anything could happen, fast.

2026-08-trial-insurance-natural-disaster.title: People shouldn’t pay for climate disasters
2026-08-trial-insurance-natural-disaster.description_full:
People shouldn’t pay for climate disasters

To the European Commission, European Parliament and Council of the European Union

Petition

We call on the EU to:

  1. Introduce a public-private EU reinsurance scheme to ensure wide insurance coverage before natural disasters hit
  2. Create an EU disaster fund that functions as a public safety net, to reduce the burden on national budgets after climate catastrophes
  3. Require governments and insurers to have credible climate transition and adaptation plans if they want to access EU-level support

Why is this important?

Your home could burn down, and your insurance company might refuse to pay for it. 

As wildfires and other disasters become more common and more devastating, insurance companies are making insurance more expensive – or removing it altogether. [1]

But people who lose their homes shouldn't also lose their savings.

The good news is that later this year, the EU will present proposals to tackle this problem. But right now, they’re hearing a lot from insurance companies, who want to dodge responsibility. They haven’t heard from the public. 

When disasters become too big for insurance companies to handle, a public system should step in, so the cost is shared and people in Europe aren’t left to scrape money together. [2] 

If the proposal writers feel the pressure from people, we can convince them to make sure no-one pays the price of disasters alone. Insurers pockets’ shouldn’t benefit from catastrophes.

Sign now to tell the EU: Create a disaster fund that doesn’t leave anyone behind!

References:

  1. https://www.politico.eu/article/climate-change-europe-insurance/
  2. https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/eiopa-and-esm-staff-propose-mechanism-better-manage-fallout-outsized-natural-catastrophes-2026-04-09_en

2026-09-trial-cheaper-electricity-petiti.title: Make Clean Energy Cheaper
2026-09-trial-cheaper-electricity-petiti.description_full:
Make Clean Energy Cheaper

To finance ministers across Europe

Petition

Across the EU, electricity is taxed more heavily than dirty gas. That makes heat pumps, electric cars and hot water from clean power the expensive choice, while the fuel that's heating the planet stays cheap and our climate emergency gets worse.

We call on you to lower taxes on clean electricity, so burning carbon is no longer the cheaper option.

Why is this important?

It’s been a summer of record heat. Wildfires across Spain and France. Rivers like the Danube and the Rhine dropping to record lows. [1] 

Our governments need to act fast. And there's one thing they could do right now: make electricity cheaper than gas. Electricity is the clean option: it can come from wind and sun. 

When the clean option is the cheap option, we can all switch.

The heat pump instead of the gas boiler. The electric car instead of the petrol one. Dinner cooked on an induction hob instead of a flame. Across Europe, that's how we bring emissions down quickly.

But most governments have it backwards. [2] 

They tax the clean option more heavily than gas. They could choose differently for next year's budget. They're writing it right now and it has to be published by October 15. [3] Once the draft is finished, it's too late.

Denmark and Austria have already cut their electricity tax to the lowest level allowed. [4] If these countries can move, your government can too. But they won't move on their own, they need thousands of people asking for it. 

Will you tell your government to make clean energy cheaper, before they finish writing next year’s budget plans?

References:

[1] https://joint-research-centre.ec.europa.eu/jrc-news-and-updates/worsening-drought-and-record-heat-grip-europe-fuelling-extraordinary-wildfires-and-extremely-low-2026-08-12_en

[2] In the first half of 2025, taxes on electricity were 2.2 times higher than the tax component on fossil gas, with particularly significant differences in Spain (4.2 times) and Germany (3.2 times). https://caneurope.org/publications/factsheet-how-can-europe-bring-electricity-prices-down 

[3]
For euro-area countries, the budget has to be published by October 15, according to EU regulation. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2013/473/oj/eng

[4] https://caneurope.org/publications/factsheet-how-can-europe-bring-electricity-prices-down/

2026-09-trial-social-media-design-petiti.title: Protect our kids, not social media giants’ profits
2026-09-trial-social-media-design-petiti.description_full:
Protect our kids, not social media giants’ profits

To the President of the European Commission

Petition

Digital products from social media to games and AI chatbots are deliberately designed to keep children and young people hooked, influence their thinking and manipulate their behaviour. This is damaging their health, development and relationships.

Politicians are finally discussing solutions, and some could take effect by the end of the year. But social media companies are profit-hungry and practiced at piling on pressure. They want to protect their profits - even if it costs kids’ lives.

Von der Leyen could buckle under pressure from social media companies, and put all the responsibility on parents and children, instead of the designers of the addictive apps. 

Our children, families and communities deserve better. We are calling on President von der Leyen to:

  • Put safety at the heart of design. Make child safety certification a pre-requisite for all tech used by kids.
  • Protect under 13s from manipulation. Enforce a legal ban on personalised services for under 13s.
  • Mandate age-tiered access and support guardrails for all under 18s that evolve as they grow.
  • Ban services that do not comply. Use EU market access powers to restrict services that expose children to risk and harm.

Don’t bow down to Big Tech - our children’s health is worth more than their profits. 

Why is this important?

For social media bosses it’s simple. The longer our children stare at their phone screens, the more money they rake in. Even when it harms children. 

Infinite scroll. Autoplay. Algorithms that learn what a young person’s insecurities are, then push dangerous content to keep them hooked. [1] Their billions in profits depend on keeping our children addicted.

Governments are finally listening to the warnings from parents, teachers and those who built the apps. Courts are ruling against platforms like Meta and YouTube. Countries are proposing bans and age limits. [2]

We need strong rules that force social media companies to protect children, not exploit them. Von der Leyen is expected to propose the first European law on children and social media before the end of the year. [3] But tech giants know this will shrink their profits, and they’re piling on the pressure. 

If she backs down, social media companies will get a free pass to keep using addictive traps that hook our kids and threaten their mental health. If a massive wave of us raises an outcry, we can make her stand firm and put our children’s health and safety first. 

Tell President von der Leyen: don’t bow down to Big Tech. Our children’s health is worth more than their profits.

References:

[1] https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2025/10/tiktok-steering-children-towards-depressive-and-suicidal-content ; https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/POL40/0360/2025/en/

[2] https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c747x7gz249o ; https://www.euronews.com/next/2025/12/23/which-european-countries-are-considering-banning-social-media-for-children

[3] https://www.politico.eu/article/inside-ursula-von-der-leyens-push-for-eu-social-media-ban/

2026-1-let-the-digital-euro-become-the-w.description_full:
Let the digital euro become the standard for digital money

To the members of the European Parliament, the Council, and the European Commission

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Ensure that the digital euro becomes: 

  • The backbone of a sovereign, resilient European payment infrastructure based on domestic providers adopting the highest privacy standards.
     
  • A public digital money accessible to all Europeans, supporting financial inclusion and reducing cross-border frictions. 
     
  • A credible store of value through a generous and gradually rising holding limit.
     

Why is this important?

Today, Europe’s payment system is dominated by a handful of non-European corporations e.g. Mastercard, Visa and PayPal. And you have the so called stable coins.  
This dependence on foreign (US) payment providers makes us as European citizens, but also our business and governments, vulnerable for geopolitical influences and (bank) systemic risks without the possibility Europe can take control. [1]

How can we as Europe take control back. By implementing a digital euro by the European Central Bank (ECB). This will provide the safety and opportunities of ‘public’ (cash) money for all citizens alongside the private money of commercial banks.

The EU countries agreed to implement the digital euro. The European Parliament has to commit this. Now is the moment you can influence the content of the law concerning the digital euro.

The private banks lobbied in such a way that the digital euro is doomed to fail. 
The amount of digital euro you can possess is limited. The amount being circulated is €3,000. This means that someone who wants to buy a used car or a new kitchen and pays for it with digital euros will immediately encounter limitations.  [2]
And also a large part of European companies is excluded or allowed to refuse the digital euro.

If this will remain in the current proposition of the law, then the digital euro will fail to realise its potential.

Stop the influence of the financial lobby and realise a digital euro that can become the standard: add your name!

My health is not for sale. Stop EU - Mercosur

All european health ministers

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Look at this video before to sign, she explain why your health at stake: https://youtu.be/2E-3NPn2Poc

Why is this important?

Because the food security and health of Europeans are being sacrificed to international trade.

+ Our health before trade: The European Union is preparing to ratify a free trade agreement with the Mercosur countries. This agreement directly affects what millions of European citizens eat every day. Yet, for decades, Europe has banned the use of numerous pesticides, medicines, chemicals, and livestock farming standards to protect human health and the environment. These bans are based on scientific advice and the precautionary principle. However, these same substances can now return to our plates through imports, with limited controls and raised residue limits to allow these products to enter the European market.

+ “Mirror standards” that don't protect: So-called mirror standards are illusory, and the resources put in place to monitor them are and will remain weak in both quantity and quality.

+ European agriculture is currently the most regulated, controlled, and safest in the world. And yet, in the past, Europe has already experienced serious industrial health scandals: mad cow disease, dioxin-contaminated oils, horsemeat fraud, fipronil-contaminated eggs, PFAS pollution… Each time, public trust was shattered, and some even paid with their health and their lives. How can Europe guarantee the same level of standards for animal husbandry or crop cultivation thousands of kilometers away?

+ A question of responsibility towards our children: Tomorrow, what will we tell parents if serious illnesses appear as a result of avoidable food exposure? Can we accept importing products that we refuse to produce ourselves, in the name of commercial advantages? Public health cannot be a bargaining chip for economic gain.

What we want: We call on the European institutions and member states to: suspend the ratification of the EU-Mercosur trade agreement in its current form; exclude European food and health from all free trade agreements; guarantee an effective ban on imports that do not strictly comply with European health standards; reject any increase in residue limits; and place the health of European citizens above commercial interests.

Sign and share this petition to defend: your health, the health of your children, and a Europe that adheres to its own rules. My health is not for sale.

NO TO WEAPONS YES TO PEACE

To the European Commission, to the European Council, to the European Parliament, to the Governments of the Member States of the European Union

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We call for the creation of a European defense system based on pacifism and nonviolence.

We also call for:

  1. the renewal and revitalization of the UN to enable the pursuit of its goals;
  2. he development of diplomacy and dialogue with all stakeholders, especially those involved in conflict or tension;
  3. the disarmament of words to disarm minds and disarm the Earth.

Why is this important?

We live in an era of global rearmament. To oppose this trend and not participate in it, it's not enough to oppose it; we must propose a real alternative.

The only real alternative I see—beyond the renewal and revitalization of the UN, diplomacy, dialogue, the disarmament of words, and improved relations between nations—is to replace or at least implement our defense systems with one based on pacifism and nonviolence. To do this, I propose the creation, rather than a European army, of a European defense system for nonviolent opposition to potential attacks and their deterrence, based not on force, but on peace, love, and brotherhood among peoples.
Obviously, this is a difficult and ambitious undertaking, one that could take generations to achieve. It requires the involvement and consensus of the entire population, or at least a clear majority, both to implement it and make it effective and simply to prepare it and make it a concrete and acceptable alternative. However, if we want to invest resources in what is truly important and indispensable—to reject war, the arms race, the logic of the strongest and opposing blocs, and to avoid further conflicts that could potentially annihilate the entire human species—it is necessary and our duty to propose a concrete alternative to these logics. This alternative cannot be merely ideological, but must be effective and consistent with the history of humanity, current geopolitics, and the presence of leaders, governments, and ideologies which force us to have defensive alternatives other than armed and force-based ones.

I am convinced that such a defense system could be a decisive step in promoting world peace and fundamental in directing economic resources to the well-being of the community.

2026-2-proper-um-and-date-format-EN.title: Proper UM and date format
2026-2-proper-um-and-date-format-EN.description_full:
Proper UM and date format

European Parliament

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

We petition the European Union to require that any website made accessible to users within the EU must:

Use an unambiguous date format by default, such as ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), or a date format commonly used in the user’s EU locale.

Provide users with a clear option to select their preferred date format, with the chosen setting being respected across the website.

Display measurements in metric (SI) units by default for EU users.

Provide an option to switch measurement units, allowing users to choose alternative units if they wish, without removing metric units.

Why is this important?

A large number of websites accessible within the EU display dates in ambiguous or non-European formats (such as MM/DD/YYYY), and present measurements exclusively in non-metric units (such as inches, feet, miles, pounds, or gallons). This creates frequent confusion, misinterpretation, and in some cases real-world errors, especially in areas such as commerce, travel, health, education, and technical information.

The European Union already operates on well-defined standards:

ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) and common European date formats

The International System of Units (SI), i.e. the metric system

Despite this, many digital services ignore these standards when presenting information to European users.

Rationale

Ambiguous date formats cause unnecessary confusion and errors.

Metric units are the legal and educational standard across the EU.

User-selectable formats improve accessibility, usability, and inclusivity.

These requirements align with existing EU principles of consumer protection, digital clarity, and cross-border interoperability.

Scope

These requirements should apply to:

Commercial websites

Public information websites

Online services and platforms

Any digital service intentionally accessible to EU users, regardless of the provider’s country of origin

Conclusion

The internet is a critical part of daily life, commerce, and public communication. Ensuring that information is presented in clear, standardised, and user-respectful formats is a reasonable and necessary step toward a more accessible and user-friendly digital environment for European citizens.

We therefore ask the European Union to consider and act upon this petition.

2026-2-urgent-petition-greenland-is-not-.title: URGENT PETITION: GREENLAND IS NOT FOR SALE. TRUMP DOES NOT OWN THE ARCTIC.
2026-2-urgent-petition-greenland-is-not-.description_full:
URGENT PETITION: GREENLAND IS NOT FOR SALE. TRUMP DOES NOT OWN THE ARCTIC.

To presidente of Greenland, Denmark and Eurpean Parliament

This petition is run by [% inititator_name %]

Petition

Greenland is not empty land waiting to be stripped. It is not a bargaining chip for billionaire egos or a resource warehouse for political ambition.

 

Donald Trump’s attempt to push for mineral exploitation in Greenland is a direct assault on one of the most fragile ecosystems on Earth and a blatant act of climate denial dressed up as “economic opportunity.” This is not development. It is extraction at any cost.

 

Mining in Greenland would accelerate Arctic melting, destroy irreplaceable habitats, and impose foreign interests on Indigenous and local communities who have the absolute right to decide their own future. Turning the Arctic into a sacrifice zone for profit is reckless, unethical, and dangerous.

 

Allowing Trump or interests linked to his influence to exploit Greenland’s minerals would send a devastating message: that money and power matter more than science, sovereignty, and the survival of our planet.

 

We say NO.

 

  • No to Arctic mining driven by political and corporate greed.
  • No to Trump’s interference and economic interests.
  • No to treating Greenland as a resource colony.


 

We demand an immediate block on any authorization that would allow mineral extraction in Greenland connected to Donald Trump or his allies, and we call for Greenland’s protection to be treated as a global responsibility.

 

The planet cannot survive leaders who confuse power with ownership.

Greenland is not for sale

Why is this important?

This matters because it goes far beyond Greenland, but it begins with Greenland.

Any concession by Denmark under political pressure would signal that European sovereignty is negotiable when confronted with U.S. power. It would weaken Europe’s strategic position in the Arctic and expose its climate and territorial commitments as fragile when tested.

For Greenland, the stakes are existential. Mineral exploitation threatens fragile ecosystems, accelerates climate damage, and risks overriding the will and rights of Greenlandic communities to decide their own future. Treating Greenland as a strategic asset rather than a living homeland reduces its people to spectators in decisions that will shape their land for generations.

 

For Donald Trump, this would be a political victory. A demonstration that pressure works, that environmental limits can be bent, and that international resistance can be worn down. Such victories do not stay isolated. They set precedents, spill into other regions, and embolden further demands elsewhere.
 

Stopping this is not only about minerals or diplomacy.

It is about protecting Greenland’s right to self-determination, defending Europe’s credibility, and drawing a line against extractive power politics before they spread.


Signing this petition is choosing life over profit, responsibility over greed, and the future over short-term gain. 🌍🔥🧊

aarongiuliotest-petition-EN.title: Protect Our Food From Toxic Pesticides
aarongiuliotest-petition-EN.description_full:
Protect Our Food From Toxic Pesticides

To the European Commission, the Council and the European Parliament

Petition

Our European food safety is at risk. The new Omnibus regulation on Food and Feed would allow toxic pesticides to be approved 

without ever having to prove they are safe.

 

We call on you to:

  • Reject any plan or proposal that would allow unlimited, permanent, or untested approvals of chemical pesticides.

  • Strengthen - and not weaken - the requirement that companies must prove their chemicals and pesticides are safe, based on independent scientific assessment.

  • Defend the precautionary principle as a cornerstone of EU health and environmental protection.

  • Close existing regulatory loopholes and set Europe on a clear path toward reducing and ultimately phasing out the use of toxic pesticides, as millions of Europeans have already demanded through the Save Bees and Farmers ECI and repeated EU-wide opinion polls.

The EU must put the health of people, pollinators, and the environment above the interests of Bayer-Monsanto and other pesticide giants.

Why is this important?

Bayer-Monsanto and pesticide giants are closer than ever to getting what they’ve always dreamed of: toxic pesticides approved forever, without ever having to prove they are safe.

Right now, Europe has the safest rules in the world to protect us from pesticides. If a company wants to sell a pesticide, they have to prove it’s safe. And they must re-prove it every few years to keep it on the market.

But before the end of the year, the EU plans to push through new rules that would remove our food safety system.

For a decade, we’ve been fighting to keep glyphosate and pesticides off our plates.

Now the EU could undo it all, letting these toxic chemicals into our food forever.

Greedy companies like Bayer-Monsanto and others are pushing hard for exactly this outcome. Unless we act fast, they will win.

We learned about this plan before the Commission made it public, and that gives us a rare chance. [1] If we show a massive public backlash before the proposal is even published, they will think twice about putting it forward at all.

Together, we can stop this disaster before it poisons our future, and our children’s future, forever.
